Preparing for responsive management versus renal dialysis in older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity in the UK (Prepare for Kidney Care): a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The comparative effectiveness of conservative kidney management and dialysis in older people (aged ≥80 years regardless of frailty and comorbidity or aged 65-79 years if frailty or multimorbidity are present) living with kidney failure is unknown. We aimed to assess the relative effectiveness of preparing for responsive management-a protocolised version of conservative kidney management-and preparing for renal dialysis. METHODS: Prepare for Kidney Care was a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial conducted in 31 kidney centres in England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. Eligible patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 15 mL/min per 1·73 m2, confirmed by at least one additional reading in the 12 months preceding consent that was not due to acute kidney injury, and were either aged 80 years or older, or aged 65-79 years with a WHO performance status of at least 3 or a Davies comorbidity score of at least 2. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to prepare for responsive management-a patient-centred approach focused on slowing disease progression, active symptom management, and preserving quality of life without the use of dialysis or kidney transplantation-or to prepare for renal dialysis. Randomisation was stratified by centre and minimised by age; a centralised system ensured allocation concealment until randomisation had taken place. The primary outcome was the mean difference in quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), combining length and health-related quality of life from the patient-reported EQ-5D-5L scale, including all follow-up from randomisation to Aug 31, 2025. The primary outcome was analysed by intention to treat in the full analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants, with missing EQ-5D-5L values for living participants imputed. Harms (hospital admissions and dialysis access complications) and adverse events (deaths and hospital admissions, by cause) were assessed in the full analysis set. The trial was registered with ISRCTN, 17133653 (completed). FINDINGS: From July 1, 2017, to Aug 31, 2024, 6120 patients were screened across 31 kidney centres in the UK, 445 (7%) of whom were eligible and agreed to be randomly assigned. 228 (51%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for responsive management and 217 (49%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for renal dialysis. Median age was 82 years (IQR 80 to 86) and 137 (31%) of 445 participants were female. After a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years (SD 2·1), mean QALYs were 1·354 (95% CI 1·201 to 1·508) in the prepare for responsive management group and 1·472 (1·288 to 1·655) in the prepare for renal dialysis group (adjusted mean difference -0·147 [95% CI -0·350 to 0·056] p=0·16). Specific harms outcomes were not prespecified, but hospital admission rates were similar in the two groups and dialysis access complications were significantly lower in the prepare for responsive management group (adjusted incident rate ratio 0·41 [95% CI 0·19 to 0·88]), based on 74 events in 36 participants across both groups. There were 667 serious adverse events in the prepare for responsive management group (157 [69%] of 228 participants died, with 510 hospital admissions) and 578 in the prepare for renal dialysis group (136 [63%] of 217 participants died, with 442 hospital admissions). None of these serious adverse events met the criteria for expedited reporting. INTERPRETATION: Among older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity, we found no evidence that either preparing for responsive management or preparing for renal dialysis was superior in terms of QALYs over a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years. This trial provides novel comparative information for clinical decision making. FUNDING: National Institute for Health Research Health Technology Assessment programme.

Endothelin 2-Mediated Neuroinflammation Drives Hypertensive Retinal Dysfunction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Systemic hypertension is a risk factor for glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, yet the mechanistic basis connecting the 2 conditions remains elusive. METHODS: A longitudinal assessment of blood pressure, intraocular pressure, retinal function, structure, and perfusion was conducted in spontaneously hypertensive rats and Wistar-Kyoto rats. Transcriptomic analyses and immunofluorescence staining were performed to investigate hypertension-associated retinal biochemical changes. AAV-mediated knockdown of endothelin 2 was used to investigate its mechanistic role. RESULTS: Hypertensive rats develop accelerated retinal degeneration marked by retinal thinning, functional impairment, reduced perfusion, and progressive neuroinflammation. Critically, these changes occur despite persistently low intraocular pressure, indicating an intraocular pressure-independent mechanism underlying the pathology. Biochemical analyses identified robust activation of the retinal endothelin system, with endothelin 2 the most significantly upregulated component. AAV-mediated retinal endothelin 2 knockdown substantially restored retinal function, ameliorated neuroinflammation, and enhanced retinal blood flow in hypertensive rats. Pharmacological blockade of endothelin receptor type A, but not type B, replicated these protective effects without altering intraocular pressure. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings establish endothelin 2 as an important, intraocular pressure-independent contributing factor to hypertension-associated retinal neurodegeneration and identify the endothelin-endothelin receptor type A axis as a potential therapeutic target to prevent vision loss in patients with hypertension.

recs.title: Sex-based differences in the atrial fibrillation care pathway and outcomes: an ITHACA-database analysis.
recs.abstract: AIMS: To characterize sex-specific differences in clinical presentation, evaluate progression through the atrial fibrillation (AF) care pathway from diagnosis to catheter ablation (CA) and assess long-term outcomes. METHODS AND RESULTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients with incident AF at Northwell Health between 2015 and 2024 from the ITHACA-database. Sex-specific differences in clinical presentation were examined. The AF care pathway was operationalized as a stepwise cascade, modelling conditional drop-off to identify care gaps. Sex-specific CA risk ratios were assessed via Poisson regression. Incident AF was identified among 165 563/655 459 patients (71.4 ± 11.6 years, 32% non-white, 45% female) with a recorded diagnosis of AF. Women were older (73.3 ± 10.6 vs. 69.8 ± 12.1 years, P < 0.001), had higher rates of dementia (9.1% vs. 5.2%), stroke (8.6% vs. 7.4%) and congestive heart failure (21.5% vs. 20.8%) at diagnosis. Transfer-of-care gaps [median 3.6 years follow-up, 96% retention] were identified at every level: 31.5% of women vs. 35.3% of men were evaluated by cardiology, 16.2% vs. 21.6% by electrophysiology, and 3.5% vs. 5.7% underwent CA (all P < 0.001). Women were 16% less likely to receive CA (RR 0.84 95% CI 0.77-0.91). In cause-specific Cox models, female sex was associated with incident stroke (aHR 1.24, 95% CI 1.18-1.30) and dementia (aHR 1.30, 95% CI 1.24-1.35), but modestly lower mortality after adjustment (aHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.99). CONCLUSION: In this real-world analysis, significant sex-specific differences in clinical phenotype at presentation, progression through the AF care pathway and clinical outcomes were observed.

recs.title: Digital readiness for cardiovascular care in high-burden US communities with cardiology workforce constraints.
recs.abstract: Digital health may extend cardiovascular care in communities with limited specialist access, but its effectiveness depends on whether communities have the infrastructure, devices, affordability, and capacity needed to use digital services. We linked national data on cardiometabolic disease burden, cardiology workforce, and digital readiness across 82,999 US census tracts. Among high-burden tracts in counties with no cardiologist or declining per-capita cardiologist supply, 4,765 (18.0%) tracts representing 19.9 million residents had higher digital readiness and were thus classified as deployment-priority tracts, whereas 21,752 (82.0%) tracts representing 74.1 million residents had lower readiness and were investment-priority tracts. Investment-priority tracts were spread across the urban-rural continuum and faced different barriers (adoption versus infrastructure). Contrasting classifications frequently occurred among neighboring census tracts within the same metropolitan area, highlighting geographic variation not captured by county-level targeting. Findings were broadly consistent across nine additional analyses with varying measures of readiness, workforce access, and classification thresholds. These findings provide a national framework for distinguishing communities where digital cardiovascular care may be deployed from those where infrastructure and adoption support may first be needed to enable equitable implementation.

Heterogeneity of Treatment Effect of ABC Pathway-Based Care in Older Atrial Fibrillation: Insights from the mAFA-II and MIRACLE-AF Trials Using a Causal Machine Learning Approach.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Integrated care based on the Atrial fibrillation Better Care (ABC) pathway improves outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), but whether treatment effects differ across older patients remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate heterogeneity of treatment effect (HTE) of ABC pathway-based care and assess its transportability across healthcare settings using causal machine learning (ML). METHODS: Individual participant data from the cluster-randomised mAFA-II and MIRACLE-AF trials were analysed, including 3,209 patients aged ≥65 years. Three causal ML models were developed in mAFA-II and externally validated in MIRACLE-AF. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, ischaemic stroke, intracranial haemorrhage, heart failure, acute coronary syndrome, or major bleeding. RESULTS: The uplift random forest demonstrated the best performance and identified meaningful HTE. In the mAFA-II testing cohort, ABC pathway-based care was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome in patients predicted to benefit, whereas no benefit and possible harm were observed in those predicted to derive harm (P-interaction=0.002). In external validation, benefit was preserved in the predicted benefit group but not in the predicted harm group, although treatment discrimination was attenuated. Patients predicted to derive limited benefit had greater clinical complexity, including higher comorbidity burden and CHA2DS2-VASc scores. Sex, heart failure, and hypertension were the strongest predictors of treatment effect. CONCLUSIONS: ABC pathway-based integrated care demonstrates clinically meaningful treatment heterogeneity among older patients with AF. These findings support more personalised implementation of integrated care and highlight the potential of causal ML to guide precision management in AF. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: MAFA-II trial (ChiCTR-OOC-17014138 || http://www.chictr.org.cn/, registered on 26 December 2017), MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514 || https://clinicaltrials.gov/, registered on 10 November 2020).

Long-term Prognostic Value of Sequential Coronary CT Angiography and Quantitative PET in Suspected Chronic Coronary Syndromes: A Multicentre study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The long-term prognostic value of a guideline-recommended selective sequential anatomical-functional imaging strategy using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) followed by quantitative [15O]H2O positron emission tomography (PET) remains uncertain. We evaluated its long-term prognostic value in patients with first symptoms suggestive of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). METHODS: In this multicentre European cohort, symptomatic patients first underwent CCTA and were selectively referred to quantitative [15O]H2O PET in case of suspected obstructive stenosis (≥50%). Patients were stratified according to CCTA findings and PET-derived ischaemia (normal CCTA; non-obstructive CAD on CCTA; obstructive CAD on CCTA without ischaemia; obstructive CAD on CCTA with ischaemia). The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and hospitalization for unstable angina (UA). Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were calculated. RESULTS: Among 3,918 patients (61.0±9.8 years; 54.3% female) with a median follow-up of 5.1 [3.8-8.0] years, 278 (7.1%) experienced the primary endpoint. aHRs increased stepwise across CCTA-PET categories. Compared to normal CCTA, non-obstructive CAD and obstructive CAD without ischaemia were associated with a higher risk of the combined primary endpoint (aHR 1.89, [95%CI: 1.23-2.91], p=0.004; aHR 3.20, [95%CI: 1.95-5.25], p<0.001). Among patients with obstructive CAD on CCTA, PET-derived ischaemia further increased the risk of the primary endpoint (aHR 1.55, [95%CI: 1.05-2.30]; p=0.029), but not when excluding UA from the composite endpoint (aHR 1.37, [95%CI 0.90-2.07]; p=0.141). PET-derived ischaemia primarily predicted events within the first year, while obstructive CCTA findings remained associated with long-term hard outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: A sequential strategy combining CCTA and quantitative [15O]H2O PET provides robust and incremental long-term risk stratification. While PET-derived ischaemia refines prediction of short-term and symptom-driven events, CCTA-derived CAD remains the principal determinant of long-term hard outcomes.

recs.title: Isoform-resolved sequencing uncovers a hidden code inside RNA methylation changes in heart failure.
Conduction System Pacing in Pediatric Patients: Outcomes From a Multicenter International Cohort.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) may be advantageous in children requiring lifelong ventricular pacing, but long-term durability data are limited. OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate the long-term preservation, durability, and safety of CSP in pediatric patients. METHODS: This international, multicenter, retrospective study included consecutive patients aged ≤18 years undergoing His bundle pacing or left bundle branch area pacing at 9 experienced centers. The primary endpoint was long-term preservation of CSP. RESULTS: Among 120 patients (mean age 12.6 ± 3.7 years), 68 (56.7%) had congenital atrioventricular block, 41 (34.2%) had congenital heart disease, and 12 (10.0%) underwent CSP for heart failure/cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Acute CSP implantation, defined as achievement of His bundle pacing, left bundle branch pacing, or left ventricular septal pacing, was successful in 116 patients (96.7%). After a median follow-up of 24 months (Q1-Q3: 10-54 months), electrical lead performance remained stable. Among 101 patients with CSP at implantation and follow-up capture assessment, CSP was preserved in 95 (94.1%). Kaplan-Meier-estimated freedom from loss of CSP was 100.0% at 1 year and 98.2% (95% CI: 94.7%-100.0%) at 2 and 3 years. CSP lead-related complications occurred in 10 patients (8.3%), and reintervention was required in 9 (7.5%). In the CRT subgroup, left ventricular ejection fraction improved from 28.8% ± 9.4% to 46.8% ± 12.0% (P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: CSP is a feasible, safe, and durable physiological pacing strategy in children, with excellent long-term CSP preservation and stable electrical performance despite ongoing somatic growth. CSP may also provide effective physiological resynchronization in pediatric patients requiring CRT.

recs.title: Beyond anticoagulation: defining the role of left atrial appendage closure in stroke prevention for atrial fibrillation.
recs.abstract: Oral anticoagulation has a very strong evidence base for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) at elevated thromboembolic risk. Direct oral anticoagulants have improved the safety and convenience of treatment, yet important limitations remain, including residual ischaemic stroke, major bleeding, treatment discontinuation, and patient refusal. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) offers an alternative strategy for selected patients by excluding the principal anatomical source of AF-related cardiac thrombi. However, the appropriate role of LAAC remains controversial, particularly in patients who can and do tolerate anticoagulation. This viewpoint argues for a more individualized approach that distinguishes absolute contraindications from modifiable bleeding risks, treatment refusal or non-persistence, and stroke occurring despite adequate anticoagulation.

recs.title: AI-ECG: Gatekeeper-in-Training for Population-level Atrial Fibrillation Screening.
High Bleeding Risk and Aspirin Omission at the Time of Primary PCI in STEMI: A Post Hoc Analysis of the PREMIUM Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) at high bleeding risk (HBR) are also at increased risk of ischemic events, making the optimal antiplatelet therapy challenging. Whether HBR identifies patients who may benefit from upfront aspirin omission at the time of primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: In this study, we sought to evaluate whether HBR modifies the effect of aspirin omission in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. METHODS: The PREMIUM trial randomized patients with STEMI before primary PCI to low-dose prasugrel monotherapy or dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin plus prasugrel. In the DAPT group, patients meeting Academic Research Consortium (ARC) for HBR criteria were permitted to discontinue aspirin at 3 months, whereas non-HBR patients were intended to continue DAPT for 12 months. This post hoc analysis assessed the primary outcome of a 12-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, or myocardial infarction and the major secondary outcome of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3 or 5 bleeding according to HBR status. RESULTS: Among 2,189 patients, 786 (35.9%) met ARC-HBR criteria. HBR patients had higher rates of the primary outcome (16.2% vs 6.2%; HR: 2.68; 95% CI: 2.05-3.52) and the major secondary outcome (10.9% vs 4.9%; HR: 2.28; 95% CI: 1.65-3.14). The primary outcome occurred with monotherapy vs DAPT in 18.0% vs 14.5% of HBR patients (HR: 1.29; 95% CI: 0.91-1.82) and 7.4% vs 5.0% of non-HBR patients (HR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.01-2.37; P for interaction = 0.51). The major secondary outcome occurred in 9.2% vs 12.5% of HBR patients (HR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.46-1.11) and 3.8% vs 6.1% of non-HBR patients (HR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.38-1.00; P for interaction = 0.67). CONCLUSIONS: ARC-HBR identified patients with a substantially higher overall risk after primary PCI for STEMI, but did not identify a subgroup with a more favorable treatment effect of upfront aspirin omission. Clinically meaningful treatment-effect modification cannot be excluded, owing to limited precision. These findings do not support using HBR status alone to guide upfront aspirin omission and should be interpreted in the context of the low-dose prasugrel regimen used in Japan. (Prasugrel Monotherapy Following Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction [PREMIUM; NCT05709626]).

recs.title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: Research Summary.
Tackling Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Pacing Performance of a Modular Communicative Leadless Pacing-Defibrillator System.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: MODULAR ATP is an ongoing trial assessing the efficacy of a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter defibrillator (S-ICD) in communication with a leadless pacemaker (LP) that can deliver bradycardia pacing and antitachycardia pacing. The objective of this study was to assess safety and pacing performance of the investigational LP. METHODS: The study enrolled patients with an ICD indication and at high risk for monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. Pacemaker dependent patients were excluded. Primary safety endpoint 2 was the percentage of patients free from major LP-related complications at 12 months. The secondary effectiveness endpoint assessed the rate response performance of the LP under workload. Parameters related to the pacing performance were also measured. RESULTS: In 297 patients, the mean age was 59±12 years, the mean left ventricular ejection fraction was 35.3±13.1%, and 17.5% were female. LP implant was attempted in 286 patients and was successful in 100%. The major LP-related complication free rate at 12 months was 97.2% (one-sided 97.5% LCL 94.5%), surpassing the performance goal of 81%. There were no LP-related complications following Implant. For the secondary effectiveness endpoint, the slope of the normalized sensor rate versus the normalized workload was 0.96 (95% LCL 0.91, 95% UCL 1.02), within the performance goal range of 0.65-1.35. At 12 months, 96.8% of patients had a pacing capture threshold ≤ 2V @ 0.4ms pulse width. CONCLUSIONS: The performance of the modular pacing-defibrillator system at one year demonstrated a low complication rate and reliable pacing functionality.

recs.title: The Cardiovascular Origins of the Aging Brain.
Effects of Walnut Consumption on Anti-MDA-LDL Antibodies and Immunoglobulins in the WAHA Randomized Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Higher total serum IgG levels have been associated with protection from cardiovascular events in ASCOT (Anglo-Scandinavian Cardiac Outcomes Trial). Antibodies against oxidized low-density lipoprotein (LDL) have also been linked to favorable clinical and vascular imaging outcomes. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to determine whether regular walnut consumption influences circulating immunoglobulins, malondialdehyde-modified LDL (MDA-LDL), a highly immunogenic form of oxidized LDL, and antibodies against MDA-LDL. METHODS: The Walnuts and Healthy Aging study was a two-center, randomized controlled trial conducted in Spain and the United States. Adults aged 63 to 79 years were assigned to a walnut-enriched diet or a control diet excluding walnuts for 2 years. Serum total immunoglobulin G (IgG), total immunoglobulin M (IgM), MDA-LDL, and IgG and IgM anti MDA-LDL antibodies were measured by enzyme-linked immunoassays in 474 participants. RESULTS: Baseline immunoglobulin concentrations differed substantially by study center. Participants from the United States had 25% lower total IgM and IgG concentrations than participants from Spain. Walnut consumption increased total serum IgG by 11% in the U.S. cohort (95% CI: 0%-24%; P = 0.040), whereas pooled analysis showed a 6% increase across both cohorts (95% CI: 0%-12%; P = 0.041). Over the 2-year study period, total IgM and both IgG and IgM anti-MDA-LDL concentrations declined significantly in both the control and intervention groups. CONCLUSIONS: Long-term walnut consumption was associated with a modest increase in total serum IgG but had no significant effect on total IgM, MDA-LDL, or antibodies against MDA-LDL. Baseline IgG and IgM concentrations were substantially lower among U.S. participants, suggesting that geographic, environmental, social, or genetic factors may modulate immune biomarkers independently of dietary intervention.

recs.title: One Lesion, Two Perspectives: Next-Generation Hybrid IVUS-OFDI Guidance for Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
BPR-30901649, An Angiotensinogen-Targeting Small Interfering RNA, Achieves Ultra-Durable Target Silencing and Sustained Blood Pressure Reduction Through 20 Weeks in Hypertensive Non-Human Primates.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension affects over 1.3 billion adults worldwide, and poor adherence to daily oral therapy contributes to inadequate blood pressure (BP) control. We characterized BPR-30901649, a liver-targeted small interfering RNA (siRNA) against angiotensinogen (AGT), hypothesizing that its optimized design would confer greater potency and durability than an advanced clinical-stage AGT siRNA benchmark. METHODS: BPR-30901649 was selected through in vitro and in vivo screening in HepG2 cells and human AGT (hAGT) transgenic mice. Off-target risk was assessed by RNA sequencing in primary human hepatocytes. Pharmacodynamics were evaluated in hAGT mice after single and repeat subcutaneous (SC) dosing, and in hypertensive cynomolgus monkeys given a single SC dose of 1.5 or 3.0 mg/kg, with serum AGT and systolic BP (SBP) monitored for 20 weeks. Investigational New Drug (IND)-enabling toxicology was conducted in rats and nonhuman primates (NHPs). RESULTS: RNA sequencing indicated low off-target risk. In hAGT mice, BPR-30901649 produced significantly deeper serum AGT knockdown than the benchmark. In hypertensive NHPs, a single SC injection produced rapid, dose-dependent, and sustained AGT suppression; at week 20, SBP remained reduced by 14.2% (20.3 mm Hg) and 17.3% (25.3 mm Hg) in the low- and high-dose groups, respectively. In repeat-dose toxicology, the no-observed-adverse-effect level was 100 mg/kg in NHPs. CONCLUSIONS: BPR-30901649 surpassed an advanced clinical-stage AGT siRNA benchmark in vivo and showed a wide preclinical safety margin, supporting its clinical development as a potential twice-yearly therapy for hypertension.

recs.title: Iron Repletion in HFpEF: An Endpoint Is Not Yet an Indication.
Vascular Brain Injury in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) are at higher risk of vascular brain lesions. Whether AF and HF synergistically amplify this risk is unclear. In this study, we explored the association of HF and AF and their interaction with the prevalence of MRI-detected vascular brain lesions. METHODS: We analysed 2,712 participants from the Swiss-AF study who underwent standardized brain-MRI and categorised them based on their AF diagnosis and history of HF. In the brain-MRI, we assessed large non-cortical and cortical infarcts (LNCCI), small non-cortical infarcts (SNCI) and white matter hyperintensities (WMH). Logistic regression models were used to analyse associations between AF, HF and their interaction with vascular brain lesions, adjusting for pre-selected covariates. RESULTS: Mean age was 73 years and 30.8% were female. The prevalence of ischemic brain infarcts and WMH increased across groups defined by AF and HF status (brain infarcts: AF-/HF- 22.8%, AF-/HF+ 30.2%, AF+/HF- 34.6%, AF+/HF+ 44.6%; WMH: AF-/HF- 43.2% AF-/HF+ 49.7%, AF+/HF- 50.4%, AF+/HF+ 65.6%). No significant interaction between AF and HF was observed for any brain lesion subtype. Both AF and HF (OR, 95% CI, p-value) were independently associated with brain infarcts (AF: 1.78, 1.48-2.16, p<0.001; HF: 1.32, 1.06-1.64, p<0.001) and WMH (AF: 1.71, 1.44-2.03, p<0.001; HF: 1.45, 1.17-1.80, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: AF and HF are independently associated with a higher prevalence of ischemic brain lesions, with the greatest burden observed in patients with both conditions. No interaction was found between AF and HF with regards to vascular brain lesions.

recs.title: AI-Identified Reasons for Nonescalation of Lipid-Lowering Therapy for Secondary Prevention.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Despite guideline recommendations for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) goals in secondary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) remains underused. Identifying treat-to-target strategy adoption and reasons for LLT nonescalation are critical to close guideline-discordant care gaps. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether large language models (LLMs) can identify a treat-to-target strategy use and extract reasons for LLT nonescalation from clinical notes when LDL-C concentration is above goal. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients from January 1, 2019, through May 15, 2025. Notes from most recent clinical encounters were retrieved and split into development, test, and inference sets. The setting was a large, integrated health system in Northern California. Adults aged 18 to 90 years with 2 or more clinician-billed encounters for ASCVD and with LDL-C level greater than or equal to 70 mg/dL at the most recent encounter were included in note-based analyses. EXPOSURES: Documented LDL-C targets and LLT management decisions. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Model performance was evaluated on LDL-C target documentation, LDL-C target value, LLT adjustment, and reasons for nonescalation against clinical annotations. Outcome prevalence was assessed on the inference set. RESULTS: A total of 28 113 unique patients with ASCVD-related encounters were identified, of whom 13 810 (49.1%; mean [SD] age, 70.9 [11.4] years; 7904 male [57.2%]) had above-goal LDL-C level. Model-annotator and interannotator reliability were not statistically different across outcomes, and micro-weighted F1 scores ranged from 0.80 to 0.98. Of the 13 394 patients with above-goal LDL-C level and 13 354 relevant notes in the inference set, a treat-to-target strategy was identified in 3756 (28.1%) of all relevant notes, most commonly targeting an LDL-C level less than 70 mg/dL (2280 [17.1%]). LLT was not escalated in 11 842 of all relevant notes (88.7%), with 4788 (40.4%) containing at least 1 LLT nonescalation reason, most often due to patient-reported adverse effects (1683 [12.6%]), LDL-C level close to goal (922 [6.9%]), patient preference to avoid LLT (914 [6.8%]), preference for lifestyle changes (811 [6.1%]), and deferral to repeat laboratory tests (617 [4.6%]). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this study show that after using a state-of-the art LLM, nearly 9 in 10 ASCVD encounters with above-goal LDL-C level did not have patient LLT escalated, most often because of adverse effects, patient preference, preference for lifestyle changes, therapeutic inertia (eg, repeat laboratory tests), and near-goal LDL-C level. These findings highlight an avenue for personalizing system-level digital health interventions to help discover and minimize guideline-discordant care gaps in secondary prevention of ASCVD.

recs.title: Reply: From Calcium Volume Correlations to Whole-Plaque Phenotyping: A Road Still to Be Traveled.
Epicardial Fat Thickness and Clinical Outcomes in Heart Failure With Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction.
The weight of evidence: does obesity really not matter for atrial fibrillation ablation? Lessons from CABANA.
Mapping and Outcome Implications of Left Atrial Low Voltage Regions as Determined by a Novel 122-electrode Spherical Mapping and Ablation Catheter.
recs.abstract: AIMS: A novel 122-electrode spherical mapping/pulsed field ablation (PFA) device is known to effectively ablate atrial fibrillation (AF). The aim of this study is threshold optimization of LVA for the unique geometry of the Globe electrodes and the prognostic association, to evaluate if the extent of low voltage areas could predict recurrence. METHODS AND RESULTS: The PULSAR study was an IDE trial of 183 patients undergoing first-time paroxysmal AF ablation with one-year outcomes of any atrial arrhythmia. During this study, a subset of patients (n=82) had detailed pre-ablation voltage maps performed with the catheter. Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) was then performed with PFA. Patients were followed with weekly transtelephonic monitoring, ECG, and Holters at 3, 6, and 12 months. Recurrence was defined as any atrial arrhythmia (AA) > 30 seconds.Receiver operator curve (ROC) analysis revealed that a low voltage threshold of 1.0 mV had the highest value (0.735). The percentage LVA surface area resulting from a threshold of 1.0 mV that predicted AA recurrence was 11.6%. Univariate and multivariate analysis revealed the percentage LVA was the strongest predictor of AA recurrence. The 12-month freedom from AA was 84.6% and 52.9% for subjects under and over the low voltage area threshold respectively. CONCLUSIONS: A voltage threshold of 1.0 mV is proposed as a threshold for defining LVA using the spherical catheter, but a range of approximately 0.5-1.5 mV yielded similar performance. Increased low voltage area in the pre-ablation atrial map was associated with a higher risk of AA recurrence.

recs.title: Multivessel Assessment by Angiography-Derived Index of Microcirculatory Resistance in Patients With Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend testing for coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) in the left anterior descending coronary artery, and it is unclear whether multivessel assessment can improve the diagnostic yield and prognostic value of CMD. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic implications of multivessel CMD assessment using angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (angio-IMR) in patients with nonobstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD). METHODS: Angio-IMR was measured in all 3 major coronary arteries in 439 patients with NOCAD. Single-vessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in the left anterior descending coronary artery only. Multivessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in all 3 major coronary arteries. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events, comprising a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and hospitalization for heart failure. RESULTS: Multivessel assessment identified more patients with CMD than single-vessel assessment (46.7% vs 24.1%; P < 0.001). During a median follow-up period of 4.3 years, an increased number of vessels with CMD was associated with a higher risk for major adverse cardiovascular events after adjustment for diabetes mellitus, smoking, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and history of myocardial infarction (adjusted HR: 1.963 per vessel; 95% CI: 1.513-2.548; P < 0.001). Multivessel assessment showed superior prognostic performance compared with single-vessel assessment when added to a clinical risk factor model (area under the curve: 0.751 vs 0.707; P = 0.034). CONCLUSIONS: Multivessel assessment by angio-IMR improved the diagnostic yield of CMD and added incremental prognostic information compared with single-vessel assessment in patients with NOCAD.

recs.title: Ketone bodies: a double-edged sword for HFpEF.
HFpEF Is Defined by Left Atrial Hypertension and Not by Echocardiography.
Ebstein Anomaly With Pre-excited Atrial Fibrillation.
Reply: Machine Learning Model Using Pre-Cancer Therapy Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Images to Predict Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiac Dysfunction.
From Discrimination to Decision Support in CMR-Based Prediction of Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiac Dysfunction.
1-Year Safety and Effectiveness of a Next-Generation Dual-Seal Left Atrial Appendage Occluder.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is a stroke prevention alternative for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) intolerant to long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC). The next-generation dual-seal device was designed to improve operator ease of use while maintaining effective LAAO of the predicate device. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this analysis was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a next-generation device through 1 year. METHODS: VERITAS is a single-arm, prospective, global, multicenter study. Patients with nonvalvular AF with an increased thromboembolism risk seeking a nonpharmacologic alternative to OAC were enrolled. One-year descriptive endpoints are provided, including mortality, neurological events, major bleeding, and device-related complications. One-year cardiac imaging was assessed for peridevice leak and device-related thrombus (DRT). RESULTS: Complete left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (0 mm leak) was observed in 91.1% (95% CI: 87.9%-93.7%) of patients by either transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or cardiac computed tomography and 96.3% (95% CI: 93.2%-98.2%) by TEE alone. The cumulative DRT rate was 3.3% (95% CI: 2.0%-5.3%) with only 0.4% (95% CI: 0.1%-1.5%) deemed clinically relevant. One-year key clinical outcome rates are as follows: all-cause mortality: 3.9% (95% CI: 2.4%-6.3%); cardiovascular mortality: 1.9% (95% CI: 0.9%-3.8%); major bleeding: 6.6% (95% CI: 4.5%-9.2%); ischemic stroke or systemic embolism: 1.8% (95% CI: 0.8%-3.3%); pericardial effusion requiring intervention: 0.9% (95% CI: 0.3%-2.1%). No (0%) device embolization occurred. Median follow-up was 365 days (IQR: 349-380 days). CONCLUSIONS: The VERITAS study results support the 1-year safety and effectiveness of the next-generation device. (Abbott Medical-VERITAS Study; NCT06707688).

recs.title: Oral Potassium Supplementation Lowers Clinic Blood Pressure in Untreated Primary Hypertension-Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Potassium may lower blood pressure (BP), but its effect in untreated primary hypertension remains uncertain. METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized parallel or crossover trials in adults with untreated primary hypertension comparing oral potassium supplementation with placebo, sodium chloride, or no treatment. The review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews; CRD42024621287). PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, and trial registries were searched through January 31, 2025 and updated October 1, 2025. End-of-treatment between-group mean differences were pooled using inverse-variance common-effect models; random-effects models were sensitivity analyses. Risk of bias, missing-evidence bias, and certainty were assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, Risk of Bias Due to Missing Evidence, and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. RESULTS: Nineteen trials (803 participants; 14 crossover, 5 parallel; median duration, 4 weeks) were included. Potassium reduced clinic systolic BP by 5.3 mm Hg (95% CI, 4.4-6.3) and diastolic BP by 4.5 mm Hg (95% CI, 3.9-5.1). Reductions in 24-hour ambulatory BP were smaller: 2.8 mm Hg (95% CI, 1.3-4.3) systolic and 3.2 mm Hg (95% CI, 2.2-4.2) diastolic. Adverse events were more frequent with potassium (12.8% versus 3.2%), whereas withdrawals and adverse-event withdrawals were uncommon. Heterogeneity was substantial, and ambulatory BP evidence was limited. CONCLUSIONS: In untreated primary hypertension, oral potassium supplementation modestly reduces clinic BP and may produce smaller reductions in 24-hour ambulatory BP. Heterogeneity, short follow-up, and limited ambulatory and safety data warrant cautious interpretation. REGISTRATION: URL: PROSPERO; Unique Identifier: CRD42024621287.

recs.title: Analysis Asks: Are GLP-1 Drugs Safe in People With Frailty?
Timing of Long COVID Improvement in Prospectively Followed RECOVER-Adult Participants.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long COVID (LC) is widespread; however, limited information has been reported on the likelihood that symptoms remit over time. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the likelihood of improvement among persons with likely LC. DESIGN: Prospective, multisite cohort study (RECOVER-Adult [Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery]). SETTING: 83 U.S.-based sites across 33 states; Washington, DC; and Puerto Rico. PARTICIPANTS: 1019 persons in RECOVER-Adult with likely LC (LC Research Index [LCRI] ≥11) 12 months after first SARS-CoV-2 infection. MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was time until 2 consecutive study visits with LCRI less than 11. Secondary outcomes were time until LCRI measure reduced 50% or more and quality of life was good or better, and LCRI decreased to 0. Unadjusted estimates of cumulative incidence and adjusted marginal cumulative incidence by age, sex, SARS-CoV-2 wave, and LC subtype were reported across all follow-up time points. RESULTS: An estimated 36.2% (95% CI, 33.0% to 39.5%) met the primary outcome by 24 months after infection, and 50.1% (CI, 46.1% to 54.0%) met the primary outcome by 36 months. An estimated 56.4% (CI, 52.2% to 60.4%) and 26.9% (CI, 23.3% to 30.5%), respectively, met the 2 secondary outcomes by 36 months. Among persons who still reported likely LC at 18 months and 24 months after first infection, relative timing of subsequent symptom improvement was similar. LIMITATION: Findings in this observational cohort are interpretable in a population with prevalent likely LC and do not address causal relationships between individual characteristics and symptom improvement. CONCLUSION: Among persons with likely LC 12 months after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, one half experience meaningful reductions in symptoms by 36 months, whereas a quarter experience complete remission of symptoms. These findings underscore both the potential for natural recovery and the urgent need for placebo-controlled therapeutic intervention trials. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: National Institutes of Health.

recs.title: Training Our Next Generation of Subspeciality Cardiologists.
Does Different Coronary Blood Flow and Endothelial Shear Stress Explain Sex Differences in CAD?: It Took More Than a CENTURY (Trial) To Get Here.
Reply: Crossover Handling and Atrial Fibrillation Burden in PRAGUE-25.
National Use Patterns and Comparative Effectiveness of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) provides bi-ventricular support for patients with myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (MI-CS); comparative effectiveness data relative to other mechanical circulatory support remain limited. We characterize contemporary ECMO utilization for MI-CS and compare short-term mortality across ECMO and non-ECMO treatment strategies. METHODS: We compared baseline characteristics and temporal trends in mechanical circulatory support utilization among Medicare beneficiaries hospitalized with MI-CS from 2016 to 2023 and treated with ECMO, Impella, intra-aortic balloon pump, or medical management alone. Patient outcomes for each group were evaluated using inverse probability of treatment weighting, G-formula approach, and grace period analysis. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality. RESULTS: The cohort included 102 718 patients: 1165 (1.1%) treated with ECMO, 10 064 (9.8%) Impella, 24 631 (24.0%) intra-aortic balloon pump, and 66 858 (65.1%) medical management alone. From 2016 to 2023, ECMO use for MI-CS increased from 0.8% to 1.8%. The percentage of hospitals using ECMO increased from 9.2% to 17.1%. Unadjusted 30-day mortality was higher for ECMO (69%) compared with Impella (60%), intra-aortic balloon pump (39%), and medical management (46%) (all P<0.0001). Adjusted inverse probability of treatment weighting and G-formula analyses revealed a 30-day mortality rate of 68%-70% for ECMO, which was higher than that for other therapies. The grace period analysis revealed similar mortality between patients treated with ECMO (54%) and Impella (54%). CONCLUSIONS: ECMO use in a contemporary Medicare cohort of patients with MI-CS was infrequent (1.1%) and associated with high 30-day mortality. Despite use of complementary causal inference methods, we were unable to establish valid causal inferences on ECMO use and patient survival.

recs.title: Association Between Cardiologist Ambulatory Workload and Evidence-Based Therapy for Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Most eligible patients are not prescribed guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF). Increased time pressures for providers in the ambulatory setting may contribute to these shortfalls. We assessed the association between cardiologist ambulatory workload and guideline-directed medical therapy prescription for patients with heart failure with reduced EF. METHODS: This was a cross-sectional study of patients with heart failure with reduced EF (EF ≤40%) seen by a cardiologist from October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, using deidentified administrative and electronic health record data from Optum Labs Data Warehouse, which includes data from multiple health systems across the United States. The primary exposure was ambulatory workload, measured as the average number of visits per day, categorized into quartiles. The primary outcome was "comprehensive quadruple therapy," defined as prescription for all 4 guideline-directed medical therapies: β-blocker; angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor; mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor. Analyses were conducted using generalized estimating equations, adjusted for demographic and clinical variables. RESULTS: Overall, 40 173 patients were seen by 881 cardiologists (median ambulatory workload, 9.1 patients per day; interquartile range=5.1-13.0). The percentage of patients prescribed comprehensive quadruple therapy was higher among patients in lower quartiles (quartile 1: 14%; quartile 2: 9.7%; quartile 3: 8.9%; quartile 4: 7.4%; P<0.001). In adjusted analysis, there was a graded association between lower workload quartile and higher odds of comprehensive quadruple therapy, compared with the highest quartile (odds ratio [95% CI], P value=quartile 1: 1.35 [1.09-1.66], 0.008; quartile 2: 1.20 [1.00-1.43], 0.050; quartile 3: 1.11 [0.93-1.32], 0.28; quartile 4 [reference]). CONCLUSIONS: Seeing a cardiologist with lower ambulatory workload was associated with increased prescribing of guideline-recommended, life-saving therapy in patients with heart failure with reduced EF. Current models that incentivize more visits per day may negatively impact care in the ambulatory setting.

recs.title: Coronary CT Angiography versus Intravascular Ultrasound Guidance for PCI.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical and physiological information before cardiac catheterization that may enable PCI planning. Data regarding the use of CCTA-guided PCI as compared with IVUS-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes are lacking. METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, noninferiority trial with blinded end-point adjudication, we randomly assigned patients with a clinical indication for revascularization, at least one epicardial lesion with a diameter stenosis of more than 70%, and a fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA of 0.80 or less in a 1:1 ratio to a CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI strategy. The primary end point was target-vessel failure, defined as a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, at 12 months. The noninferiority margin for the absolute risk difference was 4.5 percentage points, with a prespecified hierarchical testing strategy for superiority. RESULTS: A total of 1105 patients underwent randomization: 556 to the CCTA-guided PCI group and 549 to the IVUS-guided PCI group. The median age of the patients was 65 years, and 21.7% were women. At 12 months, target-vessel failure had occurred in 23 patients (4.1%) in the CCTA-guided PCI group and in 25 patients (4.6%) in the IVUS-guided PCI group (risk difference, -0.42 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.82 to 1.99; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.73 for superiority). A total of 6 patients in the CCTA-guided PCI group and 9 patients in the IVUS-guided PCI group had clinical procedural complications. CONCLUSIONS: A CCTA-guided PCI strategy was noninferior to IVUS-guided PCI with respect to target-vessel failure at 12 months. (Funded by GE HealthCare and Heartflow; P4 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05253677.).

recs.title: A New Frontier in Heart Failure: Promise and Pitfalls of Primary Prevention.
Role of neutrophil extracellular traps in atherosclerosis.
recs.abstract: Neutrophils perform an important antimicrobial function through processes such as neutrophil extracellular trap formation (NETosis). In addition to infections, NETosis has also been observed in sterile inflammatory processes such as atherosclerosis, in which factors within the plaque such as oxidized lipids, complement, inflammatory cytokines, and immune complexes can induce NETosis. NETosis contributes importantly to atherosclerotic plaque formation through multiple mechanisms. These include endothelial cell activation leading to increased leukocyte transmigration into the subintimal space. NETs also promote activation of immune cells such as monocytes, macrophages, and T cells within the developing plaque, and contribute to the developing necrotic core through inducing apoptosis of monocytes/macrophages. Within advanced atherosclerotic plaques, evidence suggests that NETosis promotes thinning and rupture of the protective fibrous cap through induction of smooth muscle cell apoptosis and degradation of the extracellular matrix. Atherosclerotic plaque rupture leads to clot formation and clinical sequelae of atherosclerosis, with extracellular histones and myeloperoxidase released in NETosis contributing to this pro-thrombotic milieu. Taken together, NETosis appears to play an important role in multiple key aspects of atherogenesis and advanced plaque instability, thus representing a viable therapeutic target for ongoing clinical trials.

recs.title: Decompression With or Without Fusion Across Subgroups With Degenerative Lumbar Spondylolisthesis : A Target Trial Emulation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Randomized trials have shown limited benefits and increased risks of adding spinal fusion surgery to decompression for degenerative spondylolisthesis. Decompression with fusion has increasingly been used in the United States. OBJECTIVE: To examine the comparative effectiveness of decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for patient subgroups. DESIGN: Cohort study using the target trial framework. SETTING: Norwegian Registry for Spine Surgery and nested NORDSTEN-DS (Norwegian degenerative spondylolisthesis and spinal stenosis) randomized trial. PATIENTS: Adults aged 18 to 80 years with lumbar degenerative spondylolisthesis and symptomatic back or leg pain lasting at least 3 months. INTERVENTION: Lumbar spinal decompression surgery with fusion versus lumbar spinal decompression surgery alone. MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcomes were Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score and reoperation at 12 months. Linear regression models with inverse probability weighting to control for baseline confounding were used to obtain effect estimates with 95% CIs for decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for prespecified subgroups, including sex, age, smoking, body mass index (BMI), back pain intensity, and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade. RESULTS: Of 2252 patients, 236 were in the NORDSTEN-DS randomized trial. The mean age was 66 years, and 1576 (70%) women were included. A total of 1446 patients had decompression alone, and 806 had decompression with fusion; respective unadjusted baseline ODI scores were 38.9 (SD, 14.9) and 41.4 (SD, 14.7). At 12 months, the ODI score was 22.3 (95% CI, 15.5 to 29.1) for decompression alone and 20.0 (CI, 13.9 to 26.2) for decompression with fusion; the mean difference was 2.2 (CI, -1.6 to 6.1). In exploratory analyses, the ODI score was worse for decompression with fusion for men with BMI of 30 kg/m2 or higher. Reoperation risk at 12 months did not differ. LIMITATION: Possible residual confounding. CONCLUSION: Patient subgroups did not have differential effects from the addition of fusion to decompression at 12 months. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: Research Council of Norway.

recs.title: Posterior Leaflet Restoration for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: EXPLORE MR Results.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) contributes to morbidity and mortality in patients with symptomatic valve disease. Although transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is beneficial, many patients remain suboptimal candidates. Posterior leaflet restoration (PLR) provides a prosthetic coaptation surface via an adaptive coaptation element that inflates during systole and deflates during diastole to facilitate leaflet coaptation. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the safety and feasibility of PLR using the MRace implant (Polares Medical, Inc). METHODS: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant in Georgia and Brazil (EXPLORE MR) enrolled 78 symptomatic patients with severe secondary MR (≥3+), stratified post hoc by left ventricular end-diastolic volume: nonseverely enlarged left ventricle (NSELV) (N = 46) and severely enlarged left ventricle (SELV) (N = 32). The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; secondary endpoints were MR reduction and functional outcomes. RESULTS: The implant was successfully deployed in 96.2% of patients. All-cause mortality at 30 days was 6.4%. MR ≤2+ was achieved in 93.8% of patients at 30 days and was sustained in 90.6% at 1 year. Patients with NSELV showed better results in MR ≤1+ at every time point (94.4% at 30 days, 89.5% at 1 year) compared with the SELV group (79.3% and 69.2%, respectively). The NSELV subgroup demonstrated better functional recovery, with NYHA functional class I or II rising from 8.7% to 84.2%, vs a more attenuated response in the SELV group (15.6%-76.9%). The 6-minute walk test improved in the paired NSELV cohort (Δ +93.9 m), but not in paired patients with SELV (Δ -7.8 m). Kaplan-Meier 1-year all-cause mortality was 29.5% overall and was better in patients with NSELV (19.4%) than in SELV (41.7%). CONCLUSIONS: PLR with the MRace implant achieves substantial MR reduction and meaningful functional improvement, most pronounced in patients without severely enlarged left ventricles. (XPLORE MRace [BR]: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant [EXPLORE MRace]; NCT06113354).

recs.title: A multi-view video-text foundation model for invasive coronary angiography interpretation and risk prediction.
Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Recurrent Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The definition of very high risk from the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology 2018 and 2026 cholesterol guidelines may oversimplify heterogeneity in recurrent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk. OBJECTIVES: We developed a prediction model for recurrent ASCVD and compared its performance with the 2018 cholesterol guideline. METHODS: We used electronic health records from Kaiser Permanente Southern California (KPSC) for model development and the REGARDS (Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke) cohort for external validation. We included adults with a prior ASCVD and followed them for recurrent ASCVD or up to 10 years. We used elastic net regularization for predictor selection and a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards model for model development. Model performance was evaluated using time-dependent area under the curve, sensitivity, and specificity compared with the 2018 guideline. RESULTS: Among 70,310 and 5,239 adults from KPSC and REGARDS, 17,344 and 1,185 experienced recurrent ASCVD during the median (Q1, Q3) follow-up of 6.1 (2.5, 10) and 8.3 (4.0, 10) years, respectively. Time-dependent area under the curves were 0.68 (95% CI: 0.66-0.69) in KPSC and 0.67 (95% CI: 0.65-0.69) in REGARDS. Compared with the 2018 guideline, using a 5-year 15% risk threshold, the model classified a similar proportion of patients as high risk and improved sensitivity from 64% (95% CI: 62%-66%) to 73% (95% CI: 71%-75%) in KPSC and from 69% (95% CI: 65%-72%) to 73% (95% CI: 69%-76%) in REGARDS; specificity remained similar in KPSC (51% and 52%) and improved in REGARDS (from 45% to 50%). CONCLUSIONS: Compared with the 2018 cholesterol guideline, the new model improves identification of individuals at very high risk of recurrent ASCVD, supporting more personalized treatment decisions.

recs.title: A Mobile Application for STEMI Care Optimization in a Multicenter Health System.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Interhospital transfer logistics and fragmented coordination among care team members may cause delays in treating ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients. We developed a secure mobile application, STEMIcathAID (App), to streamline STEMI activation, transfer coordination, and allow time-stamp data capture. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to assess the effect of App implementation on time measures in a multicenter health care system. METHODS: We conducted an observational comparison of STEMI activations managed through the App vs the traditional workflow across 2 interfacility transfer routes (pathways 1 and 2), and 1 percutaneous coronary intervention-capable local pathway. The primary analyses were the composite door-to-device (D2D) and combined transfer pathway door-in-door-out (DIDO) comparisons, reported as median (IQR). RESULTS: Composite D2D time decreased from 92 min (IQR: 63-110) to 71 min (IQR: 60-85; Hodges-Lehmann reduction: 16 min; 95% CI: 8-24; P < 0.001). Combined transfer pathway DIDO decreased from 57.5 min (IQR: 48.3-70.8) to 46.0 min (IQR: 39.5-57.5; Hodges-Lehmann reduction: 12 min; 95% CI: 6-19; P < 0.001). D2D and DIDO improved in both interhospital transfer pathways, whereas the local pathway showed no significant improvement. D2D target attainment according to pathway-specific registry benchmarks improved from 84.9% (79/93) to 100% (123/123; P < 0.001). The proportion of transfer cases achieving DIDO ≤45 min increased from 20.4% (11/54) to 46.0% (29/63; P = 0.006). CONCLUSIONS: In this observational multicenter implementation study, App-managed STEMI activations were associated with shorter transfer-related time metrics and higher attainment of guideline-relevant time thresholds across 2 interfacility pathways.

recs.title: Authors' reply to: 'Interpreting early-life BMI burden in the pathway to atrial remodelling'.
Prevalence of Angiographic Coronary Artery Disease in Systolic Heart Failure Without Infarct-Pattern Late Gadolinium Enhancement: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Rest late gadolinium enhancement cardiovascular magnetic resonance (LGE-CMR) identifies infarct-pattern scar but does not assess coronary anatomy. We estimated the prevalence of angiographic coronary artery disease (CAD) among adults with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) or otherwise unexplained left ventricular systolic dysfunction without infarct-pattern LGE. METHODS AND RESULTS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched to 27 July 2026. Eligible studies provided separable scar-negative denominators and corresponding angiographic CAD counts from invasive coronary angiography (ICA). Scar-negative was defined as the absence of subendocardial or transmural LGE in a coronary distribution. Random-effects logit meta-analysis used restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Twenty-two reports representing 20 studies included 2,236 paired LGE-CMR and ICA. 818 patients had infarct-pattern scar, and 1,418 were scar-negative. Eight studies contributed 44 CAD cases among 468 scar-negative patients for ≥50% stenosis, giving a pooled prevalence of 10.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 7.4-15.4). Five studies contributed 19 CAD cases among 271 scar-negative patients for ≥70% stenosis, giving a pooled prevalence of 7.6% (95% CI 4.4-12.6). Seven studies contributed 33 CAD cases among 679 scar-negative patients for high-risk-pattern CAD, giving a pooled prevalence of 4.9% (95% CI 2.2-10.6) and a 95% prediction interval of 0.8-24.8%. These strata represented different study subsets and were not nested. CONCLUSION: Among selected adults with HFrEF or otherwise unexplained LVSD who underwent paired LGE-CMR and ICA, absence of infarct-pattern LGE did not exclude angiographic CAD. Further coronary assessment should be considered when resolving that uncertainty would alter diagnosis or management.

recs.title: Cerebral Blood Flow-Derived Myogenic Dynamics Reveal Impaired Postischemic Cerebrovascular Recovery in Experimental Stroke.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Restoration of cerebral blood flow (CBF) after ischemic stroke does not necessarily indicate recovery of cerebrovascular regulation. We tested whether myogenic-band dynamics derived directly from CBF signals provide information beyond mean perfusion during cerebral ischemia and after acute stroke. METHODS: Transient focal cerebral ischemia was induced in 29 Sprague-Dawley rats using middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion. Bilateral laser-Doppler flowmetry (LDF)-derived CBF signals were decomposed using empirical mode decomposition and Hilbert transform, and myogenic-band activity (0.15-0.4 Hz) was quantified by absolute and relative power. Cross-validated logistic regression models were used to evaluate whether myogenic-band power provided discriminative information beyond mean CBF alone. RESULTS: Ipsilateral mean CBF fell from 73.5±51.8 p.u. at baseline to 52.2±38.0 p.u. during late ischemia (P=0.0088), then increased to 126.6±91.5 p.u. after 3 hours of reperfusion (P=0.0050 versus baseline). Relative myogenic-band power decreased from 37.43±14.65% to 13.35±7.51% during ischemia (P<0.0001) and remained below baseline after reperfusion (20.74±12.02%, P=0.00033 versus baseline); contralateral relative power was comparatively preserved. Combining mean CBF and myogenic-band power improved discrimination of baseline from late ischemia (AUC, 0.99 versus 0.70 for mean CBF alone) and late reperfusion (AUC, 0.88 versus 0.70). CONCLUSIONS: Frequency-specific analysis of LDF-derived CBF reveals persistent, lateralized abnormalities in myogenic-band dynamics that are not captured by mean perfusion alone. The persistence of depressed myogenic activity despite restored or elevated mean CBF demonstrates incomplete recovery of frequency-specific oscillatory dynamics after reperfusion. These findings support myogenic-band power as a potential functional measure of persistent postischemic cerebrovascular dysfunction.

recs.title: Clopidogrel Versus Aspirin Monotherapy According to Atherothrombotic Risk Profile.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clopidogrel monotherapy has shown superior efficacy compared with aspirin after completion of dual antiplatelet therapy following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, whether treatment effects differ according to overall atherothrombotic risk integrating clinical and angiographic factors remains unclear. METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SMART-CHOICE 3 (Smart Angioplasty Research Team: Choice of Optimal Anti-Thrombotic Strategy in Patients Undergoing Implantation of Coronary Drug-Eluting Stents 3) randomized trial included patients who completed guideline-directed dual antiplatelet therapy after PCI. Atherothrombotic risk was defined using the a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention and complex PCI. Patients with Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention ≥3 or complex PCI were classified as higher risk, and those with a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention <3 without complex PCI were classified as lower risk. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (death, myocardial infarction, or stroke). Bleeding was defined as Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 2, 3, or 5. RESULTS: Among 5506 patients, 4486 (81.5%) were at higher risk and 1020 (18.5%) were at lower risk. Over a median 2.3 years, the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events was higher in the higher-risk group (6.1% versus 3.1%; hazard ratio, 1.83 [95% CI, 1.17-2.78]; P=0.007). In higher-risk patients, clopidogrel reduced major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events compared with aspirin (4.6% versus 7.4%; hazard ratio, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.50-0.89]; P=0.006), with no difference in lower-risk patients (3.0% versus 3.2%; hazard ratio, 1.03; P=0.945; interaction P=0.242). Bleeding was similar between groups. CONCLUSIONS: After completion of dual antiplatelet therapy following PCI, clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with lower ischemic risk than aspirin in patients with higher atherothrombotic risk, without increased bleeding. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04418479.

recs.title: Prime time for gene editing in GATA2 deficiency.
Procedural Volume and Outcomes After Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty for Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) is an established treatment for inoperable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension; however, volume-outcome relationships remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study examined the relationship between hospital and operator volume and BPA-related complications using a nationwide registry. METHODS: The authors analyzed 5,403 BPA sessions for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension in the Japanese Structural Heart Diseases registry between 2021 and 2024. Procedural volume was defined as BPA sessions performed during the preceding 3 years. The primary outcome was a composite of BPA-related complications. Mixed-effects logistic regression models accounted for hospital and operator clustering. RESULTS: BPA-related complications occurred in 751 sessions (13.9%). Severe complications were uncommon, with 3 periprocedural deaths, 6 requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, and 7 requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. The main categorical analysis revealed that hospital BPA volume ≥150 sessions/3 years was associated with higher odds of BPA-related complications (adjusted OR: 1.60; 95% CI: 1.08-2.36; P = 0.019), whereas operator volume was not independently associated. When hospital and operator volumes were modeled separately as continuous variables, each was associated with complications. However, neither remained independently associated after mutual adjustment. In an analysis restricted to 135 complications considered less susceptible to differences in ascertainment, no statistically significant association was detected for either volume measure, although the smaller number of events limited statistical precision. CONCLUSIONS: BPA-related complications demonstrated a complex relationship with procedural volume, while severe complications remained uncommon. The attenuation of hospital- and operator-level associations after mutual adjustment suggests that procedural volume alone may not adequately characterize BPA safety. Further studies incorporating lesion- and procedural-level characteristics and standardized complication ascertainment are warranted.

recs.title: Increased Myocardial Tissue Heterogeneity on T1 Mapping in Preclinical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
It Takes a Cell Village to Map Individual Cardiotoxicity Risk.
Non-invasive tests in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: the LITMUS prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The advent of regulatory-approved pharmacological treatments for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) calls for precise, non-invasive biomarkers that facilitate early diagnosis, support therapy selection, and aid clinical trial enrolment. The European multicentre LITMUS study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a broad range of non-invasive biomarkers for identifying patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), at-risk MASH, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis. METHODS: In this prospective, multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study, adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD were prospectively recruited across 13 countries in Europe and the USA. We assessed 12 single markers and 18 multimarker panels. The reference standard was centrally scored liver histology according to the non-alcoholic steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network Scoring System. Target conditions included MASH (Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Activity Score ≥4 with ≥1 point per component), at-risk MASH (MASH plus significant fibrosis [fibrosis stage F≥2]), advanced fibrosis (F≥3), and cirrhosis (F4). Performance was evaluated by area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with the minimum acceptable criterion (MAC) of AUC higher than 0·80 to indicate potential biopsy replacement. FINDINGS: Between Jan 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023, we analysed data from 1590 participants with centrally scored liver biopsies and at least one biomarker measurement; 609 (38%) had biopsy-confirmed at-risk MASH, 678 (43%) had MASH, 585 (37%) had advanced fibrosis, and 164 (10%) had cirrhosis. For detecting at-risk MASH, SomaSignal showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·83 [95% CI 0·80-0·85]), significantly exceeding MAC, whereas no other test reached the MAC for MASH only. For advanced fibrosis, SomaSignal showed the highest performance (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by FibroMeter-VCTE (AUC 0·87 [0·83-0·92]), Agile 3+ and TSP2 (both AUC 0·84 [0·82-0·86]), and NIS4 (0·82 [0·80-0·85]). For cirrhosis, FibroMeter-VCTE showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·94 [0·90-0·97]) followed by SomaSignal (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by Agile 3+ (0·88 [0·85-0·91]), Agile 4 (0·87 [0·84-0·90]), ADAPT (0·85 [0·81-0·88]), and ELF, LSM-VCTE, and TSP2 (all 0·84 [0·81-0·87]). Sequential two-step approaches using gamma-glutamyl transferase as a first-line test met the MAC for both advanced fibrosis and at-risk MASH. INTERPRETATION: Although single markers resulted in variable and limited performance when compared to histology for detecting at-risk MASH, multimarker panels showed great potential, with a proteomic panel showing strong diagnostic performance. These findings could support the selection and implementation of non-invasive testing strategies in MASLD and inform future clinical guidelines, regulatory evaluation, and clinical trial design. FUNDING: Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking.

recs.title: Impact of obesity on procedural safety and 1-year outcomes after pulsed-field ablation for atrial fibrillation.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Obesity is associated with atrial fibrillation (AF), atrial remodelling, and cardiometabolic comorbidities. Whether baseline body mass index (BMI) influences procedural safety and effectiveness of pulsed-field ablation (PFA) remains uncertain. We evaluated the association of baseline BMI with procedural characteristics, periprocedural safety, and 1-year arrhythmia recurrence after first-time PFA for AF. METHODS AND RESULTS: FRANCE-PFA is a nationwide registry including consecutive patients undergoing first-time AF ablation with a pentaspline PFA catheter. Patients with available BMI were categorized as <25, 25 to <30, 30 to <35, or ≥35 kg/m2. Periprocedural complications and 1-year atrial arrhythmia recurrence were assessed across BMI categories. Among 5223 patients, BMI was available in 4573 (87.6%). Higher BMI was associated with greater cardiometabolic burden, more persistent AF, larger atria, and more extensive ablation strategies, including fewer pulmonary vein isolation-only procedures and more additional lesion sets (all P < 0.001). Periprocedural complications remained infrequent (1.0%), with no significant difference across BMI categories. At 1 year, recurrence was driven mainly by AF type rather than obesity. Within paroxysmal and non-paroxysmal AF, recurrence rates were comparable between patients with BMI < 35 and ≥35 kg/m2 (13.8% vs. 9.1% and 22.9% vs. 23.3%, respectively; log-rank P = 0.925). Severe obesity was not associated with recurrence after multivariable adjustment (HR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.65-1.14; P = 0.299), with similar findings when BMI was analysed continuously. CONCLUSION: In this nationwide PFA cohort, higher BMI identified a more advanced AF phenotype and more extensive ablation strategies but was not independently associated with periprocedural complications or 1-year arrhythmia recurrence.

recs.title: Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Outcomes Risk Reduction Associated With Semaglutide vs Tirzepatide: Methodological Concerns.
Implementation of Single-Pill Combination Therapy Through Team-Based Care for Hypertension Control in Resource-Constrained Settings: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Single-pill combination therapy improves medication adherence and hypertension control. However, limited evidence is available on its implementation in routine clinical practice. OBJECTIVE: To assess the long-term effectiveness, implementation, and sustainability of single-pill combination therapy through team-based care for blood pressure reduction among patients with uncontrolled hypertension in primary care settings in Colombia and Jamaica. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Multicountry, unblinded, pragmatic, cluster randomized clinical trial. Twenty primary care clinics in Jamaica and 20 in Colombia were randomly assigned to either the single-pill combination therapy group or the standard care group. A total of 1706 adults with uncontrolled hypertension were enrolled between February 23, 2023, and September 12, 2024. The final follow-up visit occurred on September 9, 2026. INTERVENTIONS: In the intervention group (n = 869), a team-based care approach that included physician and nurse training, health coaching, home blood pressure monitoring, and blood pressure audit and feedback was used to implement single-pill combination therapy. Single-pill combinations were purchased locally and provided to patients. In the standard care group (n = 837), patients received monotherapy or polytherapy with guideline-recommended medications covered by health insurance or government programs. The intervention lasted 18 months, with additional follow-up at 24 months. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in systolic blood pressure from baseline to 18 months. Three blood pressure measurements were obtained at each of 2 visits at each time point using a standard protocol. RESULTS: Among the 1706 enrolled participants, at baseline, the mean age was 61.4 years, 69.9% of participants were female, and 98.2% were taking antihypertensive medications. Among the 1574 participants included in the primary analysis, systolic blood pressure decreased by 19.1 mm Hg, from 145.9 mm Hg at baseline to 126.8 mm Hg at 18 months, in the intervention group and by 9.0 mm Hg, from 145.0 mm Hg to 136.1 mm Hg, in the standard care group, with a between-group difference of -10.1 mm Hg (95% CI, -13.3 to -6.9 mm Hg; P < .001). At 18 months, 69.5% of patients in the intervention group and 29.2% in the standard care group achieved systolic blood pressure less than 130 and diastolic blood pressure less than 80 mm Hg. Serious adverse events (death and hospitalization) occurred at similar frequencies in the intervention (7.9%) and standard care (9.9%) groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Implementing single-pill combination therapy through team-based care significantly reduced blood pressure over 18 months among adults with uncontrolled hypertension in Colombia and Jamaica. This comprehensive strategy integrating single-pill combination therapy with team-based care could be widely adopted and scaled up for hypertension control, particularly in resource-constrained settings. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05405920.

recs.title: Prospective in silico prediction of the Lp(a)HORIZON trial outcome prior to topline result announcement.
Beyond the Coronary Artery Calcium Score: CTA-Defined Plaque Analysis and Calcium Density in Primary Prevention.
Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development (LATENT): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Electrocardiographic analysis aided by artificial intelligence (AI) may identify atrial electrical vulnerability during sinus rhythm. The objective of this study was to determine whether AI-enabled ECG (AI-ECG) is effective for detecting atrial fibrillation (AF), atrial flutter (AFl), or prespecified pre-AF atrial findings in a randomized trial. METHODS: In this single-center, open-label trial, 14 665 adults 40 to 85 years of age without previous AF/AFl were randomized to an AI-ECG-guided strategy or usual care. Participants randomized to AI-ECG who were then identified by AI as having a high-risk sinus-rhythm ECG in the preceding year were offered Holter monitoring for ≤7 days. Each monitored high-risk intervention participant was paired with an age- and sex-matched control selected before control ECGs underwent AI analysis. Matched controls received identical monitoring to reduce ascertainment bias. Reporting cardiologists were blinded to AI results and randomized assignment. The primary outcome was a composite of newly detected AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings within 90 days. Pre-AF atrial findings comprised frequent premature atrial complexes, short runs of premature atrial complexes, or nonsustained AF/AFl. RESULTS: Among 7337 intervention and 7328 control participants, 84 (1.1%) and 78 (1.1%), respectively, were classified as high risk. Of the 84 high-risk intervention participants, 48 (57.1%) underwent monitoring, as did 48 matched controls. The primary outcome occurred in 54 intervention participants (0.74%) versus 35 control participants (0.48%; odds ratio, 1.54 [95% CI, 1.01-2.37]; P=0.046). Hypothetical reclassification of 1 intervention event to a nonevent changed the primary analysis P value to 0.057. The intervention effect on detection of the primary composite outcome differed by baseline AI-ECG risk (Pinteraction<0.001): 32.1% versus 2.6% among high-risk participants and 0.4% versus 0.5% among low-risk participants. AF/AFl detection (0.3% versus 0.2%) and antiarrhythmic therapy initiation at 180 days (2.3% versus 2.4%) did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups. Participant-reported monitoring-related adverse events, including skin reactions and discomfort, occurred in 22.9% of monitored intervention participants versus 18.8% of matched controls. CONCLUSIONS: AI-ECG-guided monitoring resulted in a modest increase in the detection of new AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings. However, these findings were fragile statistically and sensitive to reclassification of 1 event. LATENT (Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development) demonstrates the clinical application of AI-ECG risk stratification to guide targeted rhythm surveillance, providing a foundation for larger trials evaluating its impact on patient outcomes. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06847932.

recs.title: Myeloid deficiency of the PRC2 complex protein JARID2 promotes foam cell formation through elevated plasma lipids without altering atherosclerosis progression.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease in which macrophages drive plaque development, progression, and eventual destabilization.
