Epigenetic modulation of macrophages may offer a promising approach to reduce disease progression and residual inflammatory risk that persists despite lipid-lowering therapy. EZH2, the catalytic subunit of PRC2 responsible for depositing H3K27me3, a histone modification associated with gene silencing, is pro-atherogenic in macrophages, while the contribution of PRC2 co-factors remains unexplored. We found the co-factor Jumonji AT-Rich Interactive Domain 2 (JARID2) to be upregulated in unstable human atherosclerotic plaques, prompting us to investigate its role in atherosclerosis. METHODS: To investigate the role of macrophage Jarid2 in atherosclerosis, we generated myeloid-specific Jarid2-deficient mice (Jarid2del; LysMCreJarid2fl/fl). Bone marrow from Jarid2del or control (Jarid2wt) mice was transplanted to Ldlr-/- recipients, followed by a high cholesterol diet for 9 weeks to induce atherosclerosis. RESULTS: Myeloid Jarid2 deficiency modestly increased plasma cholesterol and triglyceride levels and enhanced foam cell formation. Despite increased plasma lipid levels, atherosclerotic lesion size and composition remained unchanged. Single-cell RNA sequencing of aortic arch plaques revealed that Jarid2 deficiency has both pro- and anti-inflammatory effects in multiple myeloid subsets. Together, the elevated plasma lipid levels and mixed context-dependent inflammatory phenotype suggest that opposing, potentially compensatory mechanisms counterbalance each other, resulting in no net change in overall plaque size. CONCLUSIONS: JARID2 is upregulated in unstable human atherosclerotic plaques, whereas myeloid Jarid2 deficiency in mice modestly elevates plasma lipid levels and promotes foam cell formation without affecting atherosclerosis progression.

recs.title: Liver Mapping in Tricuspid Regurgitation Informs Adverse Cardiovascular Outcomes.
Age Is More Than Just a Number.
BAHCC1 Drives Smooth Muscle Plasticity and Neointima via Epigenetic Repression.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vascular smooth muscle cell (SMC) phenotypic plasticity drives neointimal hyperplasia (IH) and contributes to atherosclerosis. Epigenetic mechanisms have been implicated in SMC plasticity, but the roles of epigenetic reader proteins are poorly understood. BAHCC1 (bromo adjacent homology domain coiled-coil 1) is a newly identified reader of the gene-repression histone mark histone-3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3). Its role in vascular remodeling is unknown. METHODS: We investigated BAHCC1 in human restenotic and atherosclerotic arteries and in rat and mouse arterial injury models using BAHCC1 silencing, SMC-specific deletion, and an H3K27me3-binding-deficient knock-in mutation. Mechanistic studies in human aortic SMCs integrated transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling, protein-interaction assays, and single-guide RNA-dCas9-based epigenetic editing. RESULTS: BAHCC1 was upregulated in human restenotic and atherosclerotic arteries and rat arteries with IH. While BAHCC1 silenc ing reduced IH in balloon-injured rat arteries, SMC-specific BAHCC1 deletion and the H3K27me3-binding-deficient mutation (BAHCC1Y2537A) attenuated IH in wire-injured mouse arteries. In human SMCs, mitogen induced BAHCC1 expression through nuclear factor Y subunit-α, promoting BAHCC1-dependent dedifferentiation. Integrated transcriptomics and epigenomics identified LMO7 (LIM domain only 7), an IH suppressor, as a key BAHCC1-repressed target. BAHCC1 occupancy at LMO7 required BAHCC1-H3K27me3 interaction, and LMO7-targeted H3K27me3 enrichment through epigenetic editing repressed its expression in a BAHCC1-dependent manner. Furthermore, BAHCC1 associated with SAP30 and RBBP4/7 to form a corepressor complex. Functionally, LMO7 silencing reversed the effects of BAHCC1 knockdown on human SMC phenotype and exacerbated IH in BAHCC1Y2537A mice. Human genetic analyses further identified BAHCC1 variants associated with cardiovascular phenotypes and BAHCC1 expression. CONCLUSIONS: BAHCC1 is a previously unrecognized epigenetic driver of vascular remodeling. By reading H3K27me3 and recruiting corepressors to repress gene expression, BAHCC1 promotes pathological SMC phenotypic transition and IH, highlighting the BAHCC1 pathway as a potential therapeutic target for IH-associated vascular disease.

recs.title: Microgravity and Cardiac Electrophysiology: Autonomic Remodeling, Arrhythmogenesis, and Implications for Long-Duration Spaceflight.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In microgravity, the human heart undergoes significant geometric and functional remodeling due to the removal of gravity-dependent hydrostatic gradients. These adaptations include a transition from an elliptical to a more spherical shape configuration. Furthermore, cephalad fluid shifts trigger an early spaceflight diuresis, inducing a stable reduction in circulating plasma volume. OBJECTIVE: To describe resulting electrophysiologic alterations and arrhythmia promotion. METHOD: While most spaceflight arrhythmias are transient and non-lethal, they remain a concern for long-duration missions. Frequently reported irregularities include isolated premature atrial and ventricular complexes. Other events, including non-sustained ventricular tachycardia during spaceflight, the possibility of early-onset atrial fibrillation, and atherosclerosis in former astronauts following exposure to high-energy ionizing radiation have been documented, though the association is still being evaluated. The underlying arrhythmogenic substrate is driven by autonomic resetting, spatiotemporal heterogeneity, and QTc interval prolongation. RESULTS: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration utilizes a multi-faceted approach to maintain electrical stability, incorporating high-intensity interval training and electrolyte monitoring and supplementation. Real-time monitoring of wearable technology enables continuous telemetry of the heart. Recently, automated chest compression devices have been shown to significantly outperform manual cardiopulmonary resuscitation in microgravity environments. CONCLUSION: Although structural changes typically revert to baseline upon return to Earth gravity, deep-space missions present some risks. Astronauts exposed to ionizing radiation beyond Earth's magnetic field may face risk of long-term cardiovascular disease. Design of personalized nutrition to mitigate electrolyte loss and development of advanced screening tools for cardiac risk assessment are essential to improve the safety of future planetary missions.

recs.title: Worsening renal function during diuretic therapy: success or failure? A matter of context.
A Natural Occluder? Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation With Congenital Absence of the Left Atrial Appendage.
Depressive Symptoms and 6-Year KCCQ Health Status in Chronic Heart Failure: Findings From the Cognition.Matters-HF Cohort.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term disease-specific health status trajectories in ambulatory chronic heart failure (HF) are incompletely characterized, and the contribution of depressive symptoms remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to characterize 6-year Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary Score (KCCQ-OSS) trajectories and distinguish persistent and visit-specific depressive symptom associations with health status. METHODS: In the prospective Cognition.Matters-HF cohort, 148 patients with HF underwent assessments at baseline and 6, 12, 36, and 69 months. Linear mixed-effects models estimated KCCQ-OSS trajectories and prespecified correlates. Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores were decomposed into between-person and within-person components. Sensitivity analyses addressed missingness, and exploratory lagged analyses assessed whether recent PHQ-9 worsening predicted subsequent KCCQ deterioration or adverse clinical events. RESULTS: KCCQ-OSS remained stable over 69 months (78.0-76.6; change: -1.4; 95% CI: -4.6 to 1.8; P for time = 0.065), despite substantial individual variation. Higher between-person PHQ-9 burden (β: -3.44 per point; 95% CI: -4.00 to -2.88; P < 0.001) and within-person PHQ-9 worsening (β: -1.80; 95% CI: -2.50 to -1.11; P < 0.001) were associated with lower concurrent KCCQ-OSS. Recent PHQ-9 worsening did not predict subsequent KCCQ-OSS, a ≥5-point KCCQ decline, or all-cause death/HF hospitalization. NYHA functional class and 6-min walking distance, but not N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, left ventricular ejection fraction, or executive function, were independently associated with KCCQ-OSS. CONCLUSIONS: In ambulatory chronic HF, average KCCQ-based health status remained stable over 6 years despite substantial individual variation. Depressive symptoms were strongly associated with concurrent health status, but recent worsening did not predict subsequent KCCQ deterioration or adverse clinical events.

recs.title: A live biotherapeutic product for adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients: a partially randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial.
recs.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) microbiome disruption and impaired GI barrier integrity increase the risk of bloodstream infection (BSI) following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant. Here we report results from a two-cohort (open-label, n = 15; randomized, placebo-controlled, n = 45) phase 1b study of SER-155, an investigational, cultivated, multi-strain, oral live biotherapeutic designed to address GI microbiome disruption GI epithelial barrier integrity in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant recipients. In cohort 2, 34 of 45 participants received either SER-155 treatment (n = 20, SER-155 following microbiome conditioning with oral vancomycin), or placebo (n = 14), and subsequently received transplant. For the primary safety endpoint, SER-155 was well tolerated, with a safety profile comparable to placebo, no treatment-related serious adverse events and no infections with SER-155 species; the most common adverse events were diarrhea and nausea. Four participants in cohort 1 and four participants in cohort 2 (two participants in the SER-155 arm and two in the placebo arm) died during the study; none was attributable to SER-155. For the primary pharmacokinetic endpoint, engraftment was detected for 16 of 16 SER-155 strains, with a median of 11.5 strains detected after the first treatment course. The key secondary efficacy endpoint revealed a significantly lower incidence of BSI with SER-155 versus placebo (10.0% versus 43%; OR 0.15; 95% CI 0.01-1.13; P = 0.0423; 77% relative risk reduction). Other secondary efficacy endpoints (GI infection, acute graft-versus-host disease ≥grade 2, febrile neutropenia and a composite endpoint of BSI, GI infection or acute graft-versus-host disease) were not statistically significant. The secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint of GI domination by Enterococcus and Enterobacteriaceae spp. was not achieved. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04995653 .

recs.title: Key studies in acute cardiovascular care.
Exercise-Induced Tricuspid Regurgitation: Clinical Predictors and Hemodynamic Implications.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Exercise-induced preload/afterload changes could affect tricuspid regurgitation (TR). OBJECTIVES: The study aims to assess exercise-induced TR (exTR+), its consequences, and predictors. METHODS: Consecutive patients underwent exercise cardiac catheterization and three-dimensional echocardiography. ExTR+ was defined as a ≥1 grade increase in TR severity. RESULTS: ExTR+ occurred in 34% of 132 patients. Patients with exTR+ were older, had more atrial fibrillation, higher natriuretic peptides/heart failure with preserved ejection fraction probability scores, higher filling pressures, and lower cardiac output (P < 0.05). ExTR+ displayed greater right ventricular dilation, right atrial pressure rise, lower cardiac output, and lower oxygen consumption (P < 0.05). Exercise rather than resting TR regurgitant volume was more associated with cardiac output and oxygen consumption. Baseline TR, atrial fibrillation, and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (OR: 1.065, 4.97, and 1.0004 per pg/mL, respectively, P < 0.05) predicted exTR+ (area under the curve: 0.91). CONCLUSIONS: ExTR+ is frequent, identifies heart failure with preserved ejection fraction-like phenotypes with a maladaptive exercise response, and adds information beyond resting TR.

recs.title: Accuracy of Virtual Circle Method and Valve-to-Aorta Distance Change After Redo-TAVR: Multicenter Paired CT Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The virtual circle method is currently used in preprocedural computed tomography planning for Redo-transcatheter aortic valve (TAV) replacement to simulate the predicted outer boundary of the index TAV and the valve-to-aorta distance for coronary risk assessment, yet its accuracy against postprocedural observations has not been evaluated. This study aimed to assess the accuracy of the virtual circle method in predicting index TAV expansion and coronary risk following a second TAV implantation using paired preprocedural and postprocedural computed tomography in patients undergoing Redo-TAV replacement. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 58 patients who underwent Redo-TAV replacement at 5 sites with paired preprocedural and postprocedural cardiac computed tomography. Three valve combinations were analyzed: Evolut-in-SAPIEN (n=17), SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN (n=13), and SAPIEN-in-Evolut (n=28). Index TAV frame expansion was quantified by area- or perimeter-derived diameter change. Accuracy of the virtual circle method was defined as a diameter difference within ±1 mm between predicted and observed index TAV frame diameter. RESULTS: In the Evolut-in-SAPIEN combination, meaningful index SAPIEN frame expansion occurred only with effective pre/postdilatation, whereas in both the SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN and SAPIEN-in-Evolut combinations, consistent frame expansion was observed regardless of dilatation. Changes in index frame diameter corresponded inversely to changes in valve-to-aorta distance. In the SAPIEN-in-Evolut combination, expansion was governed chiefly by implant position and sizing strategy. Across all combinations in which the virtual circle method was applicable (n=53), accurate prediction was achieved in 31 patients (58.5%), with overestimation in 14 (26.4%) and underestimation in 8 (15.1%). CONCLUSIONS: The virtual circle method provided an accurate or conservative (overestimating) estimate of index TAV expansion and coronary risk in the majority of patients (85%), supporting its clinical utility for Redo-TAVR planning. The remaining 15% showed underestimation of modest magnitude (median, 1.3 mm), occurring predominantly in patients who underwent predilatation and postdilatation, warranting heightened caution in borderline coronary anatomy when dilatation strategies are employed.

recs.title: Prevalence-dependent thresholding and the safety of ruling out left main disease.
Closing the Diagnostic Gap in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
TECTONIC CAD: Pivotal IDE Evaluation of Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy for Severely Calcified Lesions.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe coronary calcification complicates percutaneous coronary intervention by limiting lesion compliance and impairing stent expansion. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the SonicForce Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy System (Abbott Vascular) in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. METHODS: TECTONIC CAD intravascular lithotripsy investigational device exemption (NCT06885177) was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study of 335 patients at 40 U.S. CENTERS: The primary safety endpoint was 30-day target lesion failure, defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success. Each endpoint was tested against a prespecified performance goal. A prespecified optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy evaluated calcium modification and stent expansion. RESULTS: A total of 335 patients were included in the full analysis set, with 330 and 334 as the evaluable populations for the primary safety and primary effectiveness endpoints, respectively, and a median follow-up duration of 36 days (Q1-Q3: 28-37 days). Thirty-day target lesion failure was 0.3% (1 of 330; exact 2-sided 95% CI: 0.0%-1.7%); the upper 1-sided 97.5% confidence bound was 1.7%, below the 12.9% performance goal (P < 0.0001). Procedural success was 97.0% (324 of 334; exact 2-sided 95% CI: 94.6%-98.6%); the lower 1-sided 97.5% confidence bound was 94.6%, above the 87.1% performance goal (P < 0.0001). In the OCT substudy, mean calcium length was 22.2 ± 10.3 mm, and the maximum contiguous calcium site had a calcium arc of 247.3 ± 99.0° and a thickness of 0.90 ± 0.25 mm at baseline. At this site, final stent area was 7.1 ± 1.9 mm2, with stent expansion of 95.9% ± 18.6%. Calcium fracture was identified in 62.5% (50 of 80) of lesions after intravascular lithotripsy and 66.3% (53 of 80) after stenting. CONCLUSIONS: TECTONIC CAD met both prespecified coprimary safety and effectiveness endpoints, demonstrating low 30-day target lesion failure and high procedural success. OCT demonstrated calcium fracture and favorable stent expansion at maximum contiguous calcium.

recs.title: A randomised non-inferiority trial of CCTA guidance versus IVUS guidance for PCI: rationale and design of the P4 clinical trial.
recs.abstract: Intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes compared with angiography-guided PCI. Contemporary coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides comprehensive assessment of coronary anatomy, plaque characteristics, vessel dimensions, calcification, and lesion-specific physiology, enabling detailed procedural planning before catheterisation. The Precise Procedural and PCI Plan (P4) trial is a prospective, international, multicentre, randomised, open-label trial with blinded endpoint adjudication designed to determine whether a comprehensive CCTA-guided PCI strategy is non-inferior to intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes. Approximately 1,100 patients with chronic coronary syndromes or stabilised acute coronary syndrome, at least one coronary stenosis >70%, and fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA ≤0.80 are enrolled. Following central core laboratory confirmation of anatomical and physiological eligibility, patients are randomised 1:1 to CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI. Patients assigned to CCTA-guided PCI undergo standardised procedural planning and virtual PCI simulation, with CCTA integrated into the catheterisation laboratory using computed tomography-fluoroscopy synchronisation for intraprocedural guidance. In the IVUS-guided arm, PCI is performed with mandatory pre- and post-PCI IVUS assessment. The primary endpoint is target vessel failure at 12 months, defined as the composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven target vessel revascularisation. P4 will determine whether comprehensive, non-invasive CCTA-guided PCI planning is non-inferior to IVUS-guided PCI regarding 12-month target vessel failure while potentially improving procedural efficiency and standardisation. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05253677).

recs.title: Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain. METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization. RESULTS: During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall P=0.71; P for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank P=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]). CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.

recs.title: Correlation of the Distressed Communities Index Score With Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Disease in the United States.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and death worldwide. Risk scores such as the pooled cohort equations often underpredict risk in individuals with low socioeconomic status. METHODS: We used the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Population Level Analysis and Community Estimates data set to obtain zip code-level prevalence of hypertension, obesity, stroke, diabetes, and coronary artery disease. The Distressed Communities Index (DCI) collates community socioeconomic status and social determinants/drivers of health metrics into a numerical score. Linear regression adjusted for region and rurality assessed associations between DCI and CVD prevalence. RESULTS: We included 26 058 US zip codes (2016-2020). The median DCI was 50.9 (interquartile range, 25.4-75.9). Each 1-unit increase in DCI was associated with increased prevalence of obesity (β=0.10 [95% CI, 0.09-0.10]), hypertension (β=0.08 [95% CI, 0.08-0.09]), diabetes (β=0.06 [95% CI, 0.06-0.06]), coronary artery disease (β=0.03 [95% CI, 0.03-0.03]), and stroke (β=0.02 [95% CI, 0.02-0.02]; all P<0.001). Rurality and region were independently associated with CVD and risk factor prevalence, with rural and southern zip codes having the highest prevalence. CONCLUSIONS: DCI, geographic region, and rurality are independently associated with greater prevalence of CVD and its risk factors in the United States. The DCI is a practical, scalable surrogate for socioeconomic status and social determinants/drivers of health that may enhance CVD risk stratification on the basis of an area's economic resilience or disadvantage. Using DCI with the Preventing Cardiovascular Events score may capture economic and social challenges it omits, warranting further study.

Prognostic Impact of Discharge Transprosthetic Tricuspid Gradient After Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement: The TRIPLACE Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although transprosthetic gradients are established prognostic markers after left-sided valve interventions, the prognostic significance of discharge tricuspid gradient (dTVG) after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between dTVG and clinical outcomes after TTVR and identify high dTVG determinants. METHODS: TRIPLACE (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement) is an international, multicenter TTVR registry. A discharge landmark analysis was performed, excluding patients with in-hospital mortality, lack of TTVR technical success, missing dTVG, or unavailable follow-up at any time point. Endpoints included all-cause mortality and the composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. The optimal dTVG cutoff was identified through quartile-based survival analysis and confirmed by log-rank maximization. Multivariable Cox models were developed using cross-validated candidate variable selection. RESULTS: Among 526 patients, 474 were included. Median follow-up was 208.5 days (Q1-Q3: 54-474 days). A data-driven dTVG cutoff of 3.5 mm Hg identified 122 of 474 patients (25.7%) with high dTVG. dTVG ≥3.5 mm Hg was associated with higher 1- and 3-year mortality (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.14-3.75; P = 0.017 and HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.24-3.48; P = 0.006, respectively) and composite endpoint events (HR: 1.99; 95% CI: 1.31-3.03; P = 0.001 and HR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.33-2.88; P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, dTVG ≥3.5 mm Hg remained associated with 3-year mortality (adjusted HR: 1.84; 95% CI: 1.09-3.10; P = 0.022) and the composite endpoint at 1 and 3 years (adjusted HR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.16-2.70; P = 0.009 and adjusted HR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.20-2.60; P = 0.004, respectively). Indexed inner transcatheter tricuspid valve diameter was the only potentially modifiable independent predictor of high dTVG (OR: 0.79 per 1 mm/m2 increase; 95% CI: 0.71-0.88). CONCLUSIONS: Elevated dTVG after TTVR independently identifies patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes. A 3.5 mm Hg threshold may support postprocedural risk stratification, whereas inner valve diameter represents a potentially modifiable determinant of elevated dTVG. (TRIPLACE [Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement]; NCT06033274).

recs.title: Can We Trust the Data?: Provenance, Lineage, and Auditability in Database Research.
Optimal Antithrombotics After Left Atrial Appendage Closure.
Rotational Atherectomy Plus Intravascular Lithotripsy Versus Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone for Coronary Calcified Nodules: The NODULE-SHOCK Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal lesion preparation for coronary calcified nodules (CNs) and intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) pulse delivery for severe calcification remain uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate phenotype-specific calcium modification in severe calcification with and without CNs. METHODS: In this single-center randomized trial using a new-generation coronary IVL catheter, patients with optical coherence tomography-defined CNs (Cohort A) were assigned 1:1 to rotational atherectomy (RA) plus IVL or IVL alone; patients with severe calcification without CNs (Cohort B) were assigned 1:1 to maximum or operator-determined IVL pulses. Primary endpoints were minimum stent area (MSA) at the CN site in Cohort A and at the maximum calcium arc site in Cohort B. RESULTS: Among 120 patients, 66 (55%) were in Cohort A (33 per group) and 54 (45%) in Cohort B (27 per group). MSA at the CN site was 7.41 ± 2.12 mm2 with RA plus IVL vs 6.23 ± 1.55 mm2 with IVL alone (mean difference: 1.18 mm2; 95% CI: 0.27-2.09; P = 0.012). In Cohort B, MSA at the maximum calcium arc site was 5.50 ± 1.19 mm2 with maximum IVL pulses vs 5.56 ± 1.45 mm2 with operator-determined IVL pulses (mean difference: -0.06 mm2; 95% CI: -0.78 to 0.67; P = 0.873). CONCLUSIONS: RA plus IVL increased final stent area vs IVL alone in CN lesions, whereas maximum IVL pulses did not significantly increase final stent area compared with operator-determined pulses in severe calcification without CNs. These findings warrant validation in larger multicenter trials with clinical endpoints. (Coronary Calcified Nodule Management With Rotational Atherectomy Plus Shockwave Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone: A Prospective, Randomized Trial [NODULE-SHOCK]; ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07000045).

recs.title: Insights into the 2026 ESC guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease.
Healthy Sleep Mitigates the Association Between Cardiometabolic Disease and Poorer Cognitive and Brain Health.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs), including type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and stroke, are important risk factors for dementia. We examined whether healthy sleep can support cognitive and brain health in people with CMDs. METHODS: The study included data from 408 977 adults from the UK Biobank. CMDs were defined using medical records, medication use, and medical history. Sleep patterns were defined using a composite score incorporating sleep duration, chronotype, insomnia symptoms, snoring, and daytime sleepiness. A subsample (n=34 913) underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging; volumes of total brain, gray matter, white matter, hippocampus, and white matter hyperintensities were ascertained. Associations of joint CMD (yes/no) and sleep (healthy, intermediate, poor) status with global and domain-specific cognitive scores and brain magnetic resonance imaging measures were examined using linear regression models. RESULTS: At baseline, 54017 (13.2%) participants had at least one CMD. In joint exposure analysis, performance in global cognition (β=0.02 [95% CI, 0.01-0.05]), verbal/numeric reasoning (β=0.07 [95% CI, 0.01-0.12]), and processing speed (β=0.07 [95% CI, 0.04-0.10]) was significantly higher among individuals with CMDs and a healthy sleep pattern, compared with those with CMDs and a poor sleep pattern. Similarly, in neuroimaging analyses, participants with CMDs and a healthy versus poor sleep pattern showed significantly larger total brain volume (β=0.22 [95% CI, 0.08-0.35]), gray matter volume (β=0.23 [95% CI, 0.09-0.36]), and white matter volume (β=0.19 [95% CI, 0.05-0.33]). CONCLUSIONS: Healthy sleep may attenuate the associations of CMDs with poorer cognitive performance and markers of brain atrophy. The findings highlight sleep as a modifiable factor that may support cognitive and brain health in individuals with CMDs.

recs.title: A randomized comparison of comprehensive weight loss intervention vs. usual care on recurrences of atrial fibrillation in obese patients after catheter ablation: HOBIT-AF trial.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Obesity is one of the strongest risk factors for the development of atrial fibrillation (AF), and its reduction is associated with the alleviation of AF burden. The HOBIT-AF study aimed to evaluate the impact of complex weight loss interventions on AF recurrence rate in obese individuals after catheter ablation (CA). METHODS AND RESULTS: The HOBIT-AF was a randomized controlled trial with a 15-month treatment period (3-18 months post CA) involving complex weight-reducing interventions in the active arm. The primary outcome was the change in AF/atrial tachycardia (AT) burden assessed from baseline and the final 14-day Holter monitoring. A total of 167 individuals (aged 59 years, body mass index of 35.6 kg/m2) were randomized into the active (n = 85) and control group (n = 82). At the end of the treatment period, a mean reduction of 6.8 ± 7.0% of the initial body weight accompanied by improvement of metabolic parameters was achieved in the active group. The AF/AT burden change was 0.6 ± 2.5% (95% CI: -4.2-5.5%) in the active group and -0.9 ± 1.8% (95% CI: -4.5-3.0%) in the control group. The AF/AT recurrence-free survival during the 3-18-month follow-up period was comparable between groups (70.4% vs. 69.6%). CONCLUSION: HOBIT-AF trial showed that despite the beneficial effect of body weight reduction on metabolic profile of obese patients with predominantly paroxysmal AF after CA, no reduction in AF/AT recurrence was observed in comparison with control patients. This may be likely due to low AF burden after previous CA, limiting further improvement.

recs.title: Outcomes of Transcatheter TricValve Valve Implantation in Patients With Prior Failed Tricuspid Valve Intervention.
Delays From Clinical Manifestations to Diagnosis of Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A National Retrospective Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a progressive, life-threatening condition. Timely and accurate diagnosis remains a challenge. We assessed time from first recorded clinical manifestation to ATTR-CM diagnosis in the United States and characterized manifestations associated with diagnostic delays. METHODS: Retrospective analysis of US claims data (Komodo Healthcare Map, July 1, 2016-June 30, 2024). Patients were required to have ≥3 years of continuous enrollment before diagnosis. RESULTS: Among 7509 patients, mean age 75.9 years, 63.2% male, 54.5% White, and 28.6% Black. Patients had a median of 8 manifestations before diagnosis; median observed time from first recorded manifestation to diagnosis was 5.2 years, shorter for variant versus wild-type ATTR-CM (4.4 versus 5.2 years). Within 3 years before diagnosis, patients had a mean of 12.04 (95% CI, 11.75-12.35) primary care physician visits and 14.45 (95% CI, 14.10-14.80) specialists of interest visits, most commonly with cardiologists and ophthalmologists. In adjusted analyses, variant ATTR-CM was associated with shorter time to diagnosis (β, -0.41 years [95% CI, -0.56 to -0.26]), whereas comorbidities, including hypertension (β, 0.46 years [95% CI, 0.27-0.64]), were associated with longer delays. CONCLUSIONS: The diagnostic trajectory for ATTR-CM can be prolonged and challenging, leading to more advanced disease at diagnosis and increased burden. Raising awareness may provide an opportunity for earlier diagnosis.

recs.title: Renal Outcomes With Staged Versus Concomitant PCI and TAVR: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Ventricular Fibrillation During Pulsed Field Ablation With Dual-Energy Focal Catheters in Patients With Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Arrhythmia induction during catheter ablation in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has been reported, but the risk associated with pulsed field ablation (PFA) remains poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the procedural incidence of unexpected ventricular fibrillation (VF) during PFA in patients with CIEDs and describe associated clinical and device findings. METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of consecutive PFA procedures in patients with CIEDs. All procedures were reviewed for unexpected VF. RESULTS: Among 107 consecutive procedures using PFA energy in patients with CIEDs, 83 were atrial and 24 were ventricular ablations. Unexpected VF occurred in 4 patients (overall incidence 3.7%, 95% CI 1.0% - 9.3%): 1 during left atrial PFA for pulmonary vein isolation and 3 during left ventricular PFA for ventricular tachycardia ablations. VF occurred at ablation sites both near and remote from CIED lead tips. Device electrograms demonstrated prominent ablation artifact with abnormal triggered activity and mode switch behavior. Intra-procedural recordings also demonstrated local capture and R on T mechanisms. CONCLUSIONS: Unexpected VF during PFA in patients with CIEDs occurred in 3.7% of procedures. These results complement prior adverse-event reports and support systematic pre-, intra-, and post-procedure CIED management, with external defibrillation immediately available, whenever PFA or dual-energy ablation is performed in patients with cardiac devices.

recs.title: Cardiac and vascular involvement in protein misfolding diseases.
recs.abstract: Protein misfolding diseases impose a substantial and often under-recognized burden on both the heart and vasculature. In this Review, we outline how the failure of proteostasis drives oligomer toxicity, amyloid deposition and inflammation in cardiovascular tissues as well as microvascular injury and thrombosis, which culminate in cardiovascular dysfunction. We define the cardiovascular hallmarks of protein misfolding diseases, focusing on transthyretin amyloidosis and immunoglobulin light chain amyloidosis, and the disease-specific organ tropisms. We examine neurodegenerative proteinopathies affecting the heart-vascular-brain axis, highlighting how amyloid-β and α-synuclein accumulation contribute to dysautonomia, vascular dysfunction and adverse outcomes. We summarize diagnostic pathways and clinical indicators for early diagnosis of cardiovascular involvement in protein misfolding diseases and review established and emerging biomarkers of vascular stress and proteotoxic load. We also map the current therapeutic landscape for protein misfolding diseases, including strategies to reduce the synthesis of precursor proteins or promote the stabilization of mature proteins as well as fibril-directed therapies, and discuss remaining challenges, such as residual cardiovascular risk, that support the development of mechanism-informed therapeutic approaches. Finally, we propose a research roadmap that prioritizes systematic cardiovascular screening in at-risk populations, harmonized methods for vascular phenotyping, biomarker-anchored mechanistic clinical trials across protein misfolding diseases, and artificial intelligence-based approaches and precision medicine frameworks that integrate genotype or distinct protein conformational strain patterns, organ tropism and dynamic proteostasis measures.

recs.title: Paradoxical 1-Year Improvement in Right Ventricular Function After Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement: A Cardiac CTA Analysis.
Prevalence, clinical implications and prognostic impact of frailty and other geriatric conditions in patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Frailty in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) remains poorly characterized. The aim of this study was to analyze the prevalence and prognostic influence of frailty and other geriatric conditions such as nutritional risk, cognitive status, depression, and dependence in patients with ATTR-CM. METHODS: We performed an observational, prospective, single-center study of 110 ATTR-CM patients who underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment from October 2024 to April 2025 and were followed up to September 2026. Study endpoints were all-cause death and the combined event of all-cause death or worsening heart failure. Outcomes were assessed by the Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox regression. RESULTS: The prevalence of frailty, based on 4 different criteria, varied from 32.7% to 62.7%. Dependence, depression, nutritional risk, and cognitive impairment were detected in up to 70.9%, 29.1%, 27.3%, and 15.5% of patients, respectively. Frailty, defined as a Clinical Frailty Scale > 4, a Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe-Frailty Instrument > 2, or a Short Physical Performance Battery < 10, was independently associated with an increased risk of both study outcomes. Dependence (Katz index < 6) and cognitive impairment (Mini Examen Cognitivo score < 23) were also independent predictors of both outcomes. Frailty diagnosis showed incremental prognostic value when added to United Kingdom National Amyloidosis Centre stages. CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is frequent in patients with ATTR-CM and is associated with impaired clinical outcomes.

recs.title: N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Hepatic Angiotensinogen in Hypertension: A Phase I Clinical Trial With Randomized Part A and Open-Label Part B.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Angiotensinogen (AGT) is the precursor of angiotensin peptides and a key determinant of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system activity. ART101 is an investigational N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA (GalNAc-siRNA) designed to durably suppress hepatic AGT synthesis. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of single ascending doses of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA in healthy volunteers and to provide an initial exploratory assessment of blood pressure effects in patients with hypertension. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase I study was conducted from January 2025 to April 2026 with 24-week follow-up. Part A was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, single ascending-dose trial; part B was an open-label, single-dose study. The study took place at Beijing Friendship Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, China. Part A enrolled 40 healthy adults randomized 6:2 to receive the GalNAc-siRNA (25-600 mg) or placebo; 39 completed the study. Part B enrolled 8 patients with hypertension receiving the GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg; all completed the study. INTERVENTIONS: A single subcutaneous injection of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA (25, 75, 150, 300, or 600 mg) or placebo in part A; a single open-label subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg, in part B. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was safety and tolerability; secondary outcomes included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, exploratory blood pressure assessments, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system biomarkers. RESULTS: Among 40 healthy volunteers (27 [67.5%] male; mean [SD] age, 40.4 [7.8] years) and 8 patients (6 [75.0%] male; mean [SD] age, 47.3 [10.3] years) with hypertension, the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA was well tolerated. In part A, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) occurred in 23 of 30 active-treatment participants (76.7%) vs 7 of 10 placebo recipients (70.0%); in part B, 6 of 8 patients (75.0%) had TEAEs. No serious adverse events, injection site reactions, or hyperkalemia were observed; all TEAEs were mild to moderate. Plasma exposure (maximum plasma concentration [Cmax] and area under the plasma concentration-time curve [AUC]) increased with dose over the wide dose range from 25 mg to 600 mg. Mean maximum serum AGT reductions of 93% (at 600 mg) in healthy volunteers and 90% (at 600 mg) in patients with hypertension were observed. At 24 weeks after a single 600-mg dose, the placebo-corrected 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure decreased by 12.9 mm Hg in healthy participants. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this phase I study, no serious treatment-related safety signals were identified. Sustained, dose-dependent AGT reductions and exploratory blood pressure lowering were observed. These findings support further investigation of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA as a potential long-acting therapeutic for hypertension. TRIAL REGISTRATION: China Drug Clinical Registry Identifiers: CTR20250041 (part A) and CTR20253973 (part B).

recs.title: Angio-IMR alone is not enough: A survival tree for risk stratification in CCS.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of the angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (Angio-IMR) in chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) remains unclear, particularly regarding its interaction with other clinical variables. METHODS: We enrolled 1415 CCS patients who underwent coronary angiography and were followed for 2 years for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). A survival tree was applied within the Angio-IMR-high subgroup to identify prognostic factors, and four risk groups were derived. Multivariable Cox regression and bootstrap resampling were used for model validation. The net reclassification improvement (NRI) was calculated to assess the incremental prognostic value beyond Angio-IMR alone. RESULTS: The survival tree identified NT-proBNP, age, and coronary stenosis severity as splitting variables, forming a stepwise risk gradient: the very-low-risk group (n = 223, 0% MACE), the low-risk group (n = 704, 4.0%), the intermediate-risk group (n = 389, reference, 7.5%), and the high-risk group (n = 99, 19.2%). After multivariable adjustment, the high-risk group remained independently associated with a significantly higher risk of MACE (HR 2.41, 95%CI 1.30-4.46, P = 0.005), whereas the low-risk group had a lower risk (HR 0.54, 95%CI 0.32-0.91, P = 0.020). The tree-derived groups significantly improved risk reclassification compared with Angio-IMR alone (NRI 0.309, 95%CI 0.183-0.549, P = 0.001). Notably, systemic inflammatory markers (SIRI, NLR) increased stepwise across the groups (both P < 0.001), paralleling the risk gradient. An online risk calculator was developed based on these findings (https://heartlab.shinyapps.io/calculator/). CONCLUSION: Angio-IMR alone does not adequately stratify risk in CCS. Integrating it with NT-proBNP, age, and coronary stenosis severity via a survival tree significantly improves 2-year MACE prediction, enabling precision targeting of preventive therapies.

recs.title: Threshold Optimization Vs Assay Advancement.
Heart failure therapy in congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries: effect on right ventricular function and survival.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The aim of the study was to assess the effect of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) on cardiac function, neurohormonal activation, and mortality in adults with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (cc-TGA) presenting with systemic right ventricular (RV) systolic dysfunction. The study hypothesis was that GDMT use (assessed using the GDMT score) was associated with improved cardiac function (higher RV free wall strain [RVFWS]), less neurohormonal activation (lower N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP] levels), and lower mortality. METHODS: GDMT score, RVFWS, and NT-proBNP levels were assessed at baseline and 1-year follow-up. GDMT uptitration was assessed using ΔGDMT (GDMT at 1-year minus GDMT at baseline). Improvements in RV systolic function and neurohormonal activation were defined as a relative increase in RVFWS of >20% and a relative decrease in NT-proBNP levels of >20%, respectively. RESULTS: Of 213 patients (age 43 ± 15 years; 54% male), baseline GDMT score was 1.97 ± 1.27, and ΔGDMT score was 0.74 ± 0.39. Baseline RVFWS was -18 ± 5%; 25% had improved RV systolic function. Baseline NT-proBNP was 369 (142, 1004) pg/mL; 56% had improved neurohormonal activation. Higher baseline GDMT score and ΔGDMT score were associated with improvement in RV systolic function and neurohormonal activation. Overall, 34 (16%) patients died, and higher baseline GDMT score and ΔGDMT score were associated with a lower risk of mortality and of the composite adverse event endpoint (heart failure hospitalization, death, and heart transplantation). Clinical benefits of GDMT use were observed only in patients with moderate/severe RV systolic dysfunction, and not in patients with mild RV systolic dysfunction. CONCLUSIONS: GDMT use was associated with improved outcomes in patients with moderate/severe RV systolic dysfunction.

recs.title: Guided P2Y12 inhibitor selection after rapid CYP2C19 genotyping in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dual antiplatelet therapy remains the standard treatment following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). While prasugrel and ticagrelor offer consistent antiplatelet effects, they increase bleeding risk compared with clopidogrel, which requires CYP2C19 bioactivation. AIMS: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of rapid CYP2C19 genotyping at the time of PCI on P2Y12 inhibitor selection and clinical outcomes in real-world patients. METHODS: A total of 974 patients who underwent PCI and rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and received P2Y12 inhibitor treatment were included. P2Y12 inhibitor selection, P2Y12 inhibitor switching, major atherothrombotic events (MAE; a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, stent thrombosis, or unstable angina requiring revascularisation), and bleeding events were assessed throughout the first year post-PCI. Time-varying Cox regression analysis was performed to assess event risk in patients treated with clopidogrel (reference) versus prasugrel/ticagrelor after stratifying by loss-of-function (LOF) status and adjusting for stratum-specific confounders. RESULTS: Clopidogrel was prescribed more frequently at discharge among CYP2C19 non-LOF versus LOF carriers (43% [296/691] vs 31% [87/283]; p<0.001). The median duration of follow-up was 359 days (interquartile range [IQR] 190-362 days). Among LOF allele carriers de-escalating to clopidogrel, the median de-escalation time was 180 days (IQR 92-354 days). MAE were not significantly different between P2Y12 inhibitor regimens after stratifying by LOF status (LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=147] vs LOF-clopidogrel [n=136]: adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.87 [95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.36-2.10]; non-LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=272] vs non-LOF-clopidogrel [n=419]: adjusted HR 1.26, 95% CI: 0.67-2.36). No significant differences in Bleeding Academic Research Consortium bleeding events were observed. CONCLUSIONS: This real-world study shows that, among LOF carriers managed with rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and delayed de-escalation, ischaemic and bleeding event rates were not significantly different between those taking clopidogrel versus those taking prasugrel/ticagrelor, though findings should be interpreted cautiously.

recs.title: Exercise Prescriptions Recommended for Cardiovascular Health.
Comprehensive m6A landscape from direct RNA sequencing reveals SYNPO2L RNA isoform regulation mechanisms in heart failure.
recs.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that epitranscriptomic regulation, particularly the m6A modification, contributes to heart failure progression. However, modification dynamics are not yet mapped and studied at base resolution and transcript isoform level. Here we use Nanopore direct RNA sequencing to profile m6A remodeling at transcriptome-wide and site-specific resolution in a mouse heart failure model. We identify thousands of differentially methylated sites with distinct sequence motifs and associations with RNA regulatory and cardiac function processes. Cross-species comparison reveals conserved m6A regulatory features in mouse and human heart failure. Isoform-resolved analysis further uncovers co/posttranscriptional regulation events involving isoform switching and m6A regulation in the SYNPO2L transcript. Mechanistically, m6A modification, alternative promoter usage and associated regulatory elements collectively explain this observation. Overall, our study provides a comprehensive, high-resolution characterization of m6A landscape and its remodeling in heart failure. Isoform-level regulation exemplifies an underappreciated shaping of RNA expression and modification.

recs.title: Hemodynamic Effects of Reducing LV Afterload With Impella or Intra-Aortic Balloon Counterpulsation During Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Cardiogenic Shock: HERACLES Trial.
recs.abstract: Background: Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) provides organ support in cardiogenic shock but increases left ventricular (LV) afterload, potentially impairing cardiac recovery. LV unloading with an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or micro-axial flow pump (mAFP) may mitigate this effect. HERACLES compared their effects on myocardial oxygen supply and demand. Methods: Patients receiving VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock were randomized to LV unloading with IABP or mAFP, stratified by ischemic/non-ischemic etiology. Distal coronary, aortic and LV pressures and coronary flow (inverse mean transit time, Tmn) were measured with and without unloading. Myocardial oxygen demand was estimated as the area under the LV pressure curve in systole (TTI) x heart rate (HR). The primary endpoint was the change in myocardial oxygen supply-demand ratio calculated as [(Tmn * TTI*HR)off / (Tmn * TTI *HR)unload]. Secondary endpoints included changes in coronary flow [device flow ratio (DFR) =(Tmn)off/ (Tmn)unload], oxygen demand per beat (DTTI), contractility (DdP/dtmax) and filling pressure (DLVEDP). Results: Twenty-four patients were enrolled (age 51 [46-57]; 46% male; 96% SCAI D/E; 38% ischemic). At randomization, lactate was 4.3 mmol/L [IQR 2.5 to 8.4], LV ejection fraction 10% [10 to 17], LVEDP 18 mmHg [14 to 24]. The myocardial oxygen supply-demand ratio improved with IABP but not mAFP (1.48 [1.23 to 2.10] vs 0.97 [0.92 to 1.39]; P=0.036), driven predominantly by differential reduction of TTI. Coronary pressure increased but flow was unchanged with mAFP (DFR 1.00 [0.86 to 1.13]). Coronary flow increased marginally with IABP (DFR 1.16 [1.00 to 1.51]). LV pressures decreased with both devices and contractility with IABP only, with no between-group differences. Thirty-day mortality was similar (38% vs 45%, p=0.84). Conclusions: In VA-ECMO supported SCAI D/E cardiogenic shock, IABP improved myocardial oxygen supply-demand balance, whereas mAFP did not. Further research is needed to determine whether these mechanistic differences translate to clinical outcomes.

recs.title: Differential half-life of major titin isoforms in normal and remodeling mouse hearts.
Reinitiation of Optimal Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy After Coronary Bypass Grafting in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
Effectiveness of Radiofrequency Renal Denervation in the United States: Six-Month Primary End Point Results From the SPYRAL AFFIRM Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Radiofrequency renal denervation (RDN) is a guideline-recommended therapy for uncontrolled hypertension. SPYRAL AFFIRM is a single-arm, postapproval study assessing the efficacy and safety of radiofrequency RDN using the Symplicity Spyral catheter. We report the 6-month primary end point results in the SPYRAL AFFIRM US population. METHODS: Enrolled patients had an office systolic/diastolic blood pressure (BP) ≥140/90 mm Hg and a home systolic BP ≥135 mm Hg. Patients with type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c >8.0%), or an estimated glomerular filtration rate <45 mL/min per 1.73 m2 were excluded. The primary end point was the 6-month change in office systolic BP from baseline compared with a prespecified performance goal (-6.0 mm Hg). RESULTS: Among 594 patients treated in the AFFIRM study from 73 US clinical sites, baseline clinical characteristics included: mean (±SD) age, 57±12 years; female, 45%; African American, 27%; Hispanic, 11%; type 2 diabetes, 19%; and mean estimated glomerular filtration rate, 79±20 mL/min per 1.73m2. Baseline systolic/diastolic office, home, and 24-hour ambulatory BP (mm Hg) were 169±21/106±13, 158±17/101±13, and 151±18/96±13, respectively. Patients were prescribed an average of 3.6±2.0 antihypertensive medications at baseline that remained unchanged through 6 months. Six months after RDN, the change in systolic BP (mm Hg) was -18.2±22.0, -9.4±13.8, and -9.7±16.8 for office, home, and 24-hour ambulatory measures, respectively (P<0.001 compared with baseline). Adverse clinical events through 6 months were uncommon. CONCLUSIONS: In this US postapproval study, the primary end point was met with significant BP reductions following radiofrequency RDN consistent across different measures. In a broader patient population with uncontrolled hypertension, these results reaffirm the safety and efficacy of radiofrequency RDN. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT05198674.

recs.title: Intersection of Patient and Hospital Rurality in Heart Failure Care and Outcomes.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Rural-urban disparities in heart failure (HF) care delivery and outcomes are well documented. However, it remains unclear if differences in outcomes after HF hospitalization are primarily driven by patient rural residence, hospital resources, or both. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations of patient and hospital rurality with quality of care and postdischarge outcomes after hospitalization for HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries in US hospitals with HFrEF with an index hospitalization from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2021. Included were Medicare beneficiaries discharged alive after an index hospitalization for HFrEF. Participants were classified as rural patients hospitalized in rural hospitals (rural-rural), rural patients in urban hospitals (rural-urban), urban patients in urban hospitals (urban-urban), and urban patients in rural hospitals (urban-rural). Study data were analyzed from July to September 2026. EXPOSURES: Patient rural residence and hospital rurality. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality after hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included inpatient cardiology consultation, 90-day postdischarge guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) use based on prescription fills, and HF readmission at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year. RESULTS: Among 735 460 beneficiaries (median [IQR] age, 77 [70-85] years; 415 077 male [56.4%]), 69 061 (9.4%) were rural-rural, 65 510 (8.9%) rural-urban, 582 947 (79.3%) urban-urban, and 17 942 (2.4%) urban-rural. Compared with rural patients treated in rural hospitals, rural patients treated in urban hospitals were more likely to receive inpatient cardiology consultation (odds ratio [OR], 2.02; 95% CI, 1.84-2.22) and initiation of several GDMT classes, including β-blockers (OR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.16-1.25), ARNIs (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.13-1.34), MRAs (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.15-1.31), and SGLT2Is (OR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.32-1.67). They also had lower rates of HF readmission and mortality at all time points (HF readmission 1-year: OR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.82-0.88; mortality 1-year: OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.89-0.94) than rural-rural patients. Compared with urban patients hospitalized at urban hospitals, rural patients hospitalized at urban hospitals more often received inpatient cardiology consultation (OR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.31-1.44), whereas postdischarge GDMT differences were modest (absolute difference in GDMT score 0.09 points; 95% CI, 0.05-0.14). Rural patients also had lower HF readmission (1-year OR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.79-0.82) but higher 30- and 90-day mortality than urban patients (30-day OR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; 90-day OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.02-1.08). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results suggest that hospital rurality was associated with lower odds of GDMT use and higher rates of all-cause mortality, whereas rural residence was associated with mortality differences despite treatment in urban hospitals. Interventions addressing both inpatient resource disparities and postdischarge transitions of care may reduce rural-urban inequities in HF outcomes.

recs.title: Assessment of Ototoxicity in Patients With Heart Failure Receiving High-Dose IV Loop Diuretics.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Concern for ototoxicity hinders loop diuretic (LD) dosing in heart failure (HF); given the mechanism by which LDs affect the ear, high-dose LDs should produce transient, not permanent, hearing changes. OBJECTIVE: To measure the association of LD dose with permanent and temporary ototoxicity. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Cohort 1 received a randomized sequence of LD doses (bumetanide, 1.25-10 mg) across study visits with serial audiometry assessments. Cohort 2 received serial LD up to furosemide 500-mg doses during a HF hospitalization with audiometry at baseline and prior to discharge. Cohort 3 retrospectively characterized clinically diagnosed ototoxicity in HF hospitalizations was defined using International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. Cohorts 1 and 2 were single center, while cohort 3 was multicenter. Cohort 1 studied outpatient participants with stable HF, while cohort 2 (n = 40) and cohort 3 studied hospitalized patients with acute HF. EXPOSURE: Intravenous LD. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were clinically diagnosed ototoxicity and hearing changes via audiometry. RESULTS: Cohort 1 contained 50 participants, cohort 2 contained 40 participants, and cohort 3 contained 22 656 participants. In cohort 1, mean (SD) participant age was 63.2 (10.4) years, and 21 of 50 participants (42%) were women. In cohorts 1 and 2, clinically diagnosed ototoxicity was not observed. In cohort 1, at peak diuretic concentration, worsening hearing shifts were infrequent (24 ears of 400 doses [6%]) but were more common with higher doses (odds ratio [OR], 1.99; 95% CI, 1.21-3.28 per doubling dose; P = .007). Within hours, hearing shifts largely resolved and were absent in 98% of measurements (393 ears of 400 doses). No significant association between LD dose and hearing shifts was present at any time aside from peak LD concentration. In cohort 2, hearing shifts were not different across groups divided by the median daily LD dose and were not associated with LD dose (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.71-1.98 per doubling dose; P = .52). In cohort 3, 608 HF hospitalizations (2.7%) had clinically diagnosed ototoxicity. In multivariable analyses, peak dose of 160 mg furosemide equivalents or greater (OR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.52-1.31; P = .43) and 400 mg furosemide equivalents or greater (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 0.71-2.31; P = .41) were not associated with greater clinically diagnosed ototoxicity risk relative to less than 160 mg. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this analysis of 2 small HF cohorts, short-term exposure to high-dose LD was not associated with permanent ototoxicity, although concomitant ototoxin use was excluded. Future studies are needed to understand the risk of ototoxicity with repeated LD exposure and in broader HF populations. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT04481919 and NCT05323487.

recs.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids and Atrial Fibrillation: Current Evidence and Expert Opinion.
recs.abstract: Recent clinical trials have reported an increased risk for atrial fibrillation (AF) in individuals treated with omega-3 fatty acids (FA). As virtually all these studies were conducted with pharmaceutical omega-3 FA preparations in populations at higher risk for cardiovascular disease (CVD), it is unclear to what extent these findings apply to the general population consuming omega-3 FA either from oily fish or from omega-3 FA supplements. Based on an updated meta-analysis reviewed here, consumption of up to 1500 mg/day (and possibly 2400 mg/day) of eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) + docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) from food or dietary supplements in the general adult population does not appear to significantly increase risk for AF. Indeed, the preponderance of the evidence suggests that chronic intakes in this range are associated with lower risk for AF (and other CVD outcomes) in the general population. For individuals at high risk for CVD, treatment with EPA+DHA doses of >1500 mg/day might increase the absolute risk for AF (by <1%) and the relative risk (by ∼43%). Because of the favorable effects of EPA+DHA on CVD (and other health) outcomes, our view is that, for the general population, intakes of EPA+DHA afford several health benefits and do not meaningfully increase the risk for AF. For patients with prevalent CVD or at high risk for CVD, the risk-benefit ratio for EPA+DHA intake is favorable, especially for intakes up to 1500 mg/day, but also at higher doses where there may be increased risk for AF.

recs.title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation vs surgical replacement in low-risk aortic stenosis: time-dependent late mortality in a pooled analysis of trials.
Artificial Intelligence Detection of Aortic Valve Calcification on Routine Noncontrast Chest CT: A Real-World Cohort.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Routine noncontrast chest computed tomography (CT) may reveal aortic valve calcification (AVC) outside aortic stenosis evaluation. Its prevalence, burden, and documentation remain uncertain. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enable systematic detection. OBJECTIVES: The study aims to evaluate AVC prevalence and burden, clinical correlates, radiology documentation, and AI-assisted case finding. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study screened 511 consecutive noncontrast, non-electrocardiographically gated chest CT examinations in adults aged ≥50 years. After 15 protocol exclusions and 56 software-designated nonevaluable examinations, 440 underwent quantification by 2 blinded readers. AVC was defined as >10 AU using a 130-Hounsfield-unit threshold adjusted for blood-pool attenuation and image noise when needed. Locked HealthAVC V1.0 was a secondary comparator. RESULTS: Manual quantification identified AVC in 172 of 440 scans (39.1%; 95% CI: 34.6%-43.7%); 97 of 440 (22.0%) had ≥100 AU. Inter-reader agreement at >10 AU was 99.5% (kappa = 0.990). Age (adjusted OR: 1.92 per 5 years; 95% CI: 1.63-2.26) and male sex (adjusted OR: 2.09; 95% CI: 1.32-3.30) were associated with AVC. Reports documented 27 of 172 positive scans (15.7%; 95% CI: 11.0%-21.9%). AI detected 169 of 172 manually confirmed cases (98.3%) among 440 evaluable scans, including 142 of 145 undocumented cases. Of 496 submitted scans, 56 (11.3%) were nonevaluable. End-to-end sensitivity counting positive rejected scans as missed was 89.9%. Among 86 AI-positive patients with echocardiography, 10 (11.6%) had mild-or-greater aortic stenosis. CONCLUSIONS: AVC was common but infrequently documented on routine chest CT. AI detected most cases among evaluable scans; 11.3% were nonevaluable, yielding 89.9% end-to-end sensitivity. Prospective studies should assess clinical pathways.
