Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in the Middle East and North Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Data on transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region are limited. We synthesized available evidence on post-TAVR clinical outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through May 2025 for studies reporting TAVR outcomes in this region. Outcomes included device success, all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, new-onset atrial fibrillation, moderate to severe paravalvular leak, and permanent pacemaker implantation. Overall incidence rates were pooled via Poisson analysis and reported per 100 person-years with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Forty-eight studies encompassing 7331 patients (mean age, 76.9±8.5 years; 52.4% women) were included. Pooled device success rate was 96.4% (95% CI, 95.8%-97.0%). At latest follow-up, pooled incidence rates per 100 person-years were 13.7 for all-cause death (95% CI, 12.9-14.6), 4.8 for cardiovascular death (95% CI, 4.1-5.7), 1.0 for myocardial infarction (95% CI, 0.7-1.4), 1.6 for stroke (95% CI, 1.3-1.9), 2.7 for moderate to severe paravalvular leak (95% CI, 2.2-3.4), 6.5 for new-onset atrial fibrillation (95% CI, 5.5-7.7), and 10.0 for permanent pacemaker implantation (95% CI, 9.2-10.9). Post hoc exploratory meta-regression identified significant study-level modifying effects, with higher mean age and greater use of first-generation versus second-generation valves associated with higher overall all-cause mortality incidence following TAVR. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: TAVR in the Middle East and North Africa region was associated with high device success rate and relatively low cardiovascular death. Permanent pacemaker implantation was the most prevalent post-TAVR complication. Further studies are warranted to optimize TAVR practice in this region.

recs.title: Percutaneous Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Symptomatic Mitral Regurgitation: 2-Year Outcomes From the ENCIRCLE Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is an approved treatment option for select high-risk patients with symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR). The main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial, evaluating fully percutaneous transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system, demonstrated 13.9% mortality, significant MR reduction, and improved functional and health status outcomes at 1 year. OBJECTIVES: We report 2-year outcomes from the main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial. METHODS: Eligible symptomatic patients with ≥3+ MR who were not suitable for surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair underwent TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system. Independent study oversight included an echocardiographic core laboratory and a clinical events committee. Endpoints included the nonhierarchical composite rate of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization (HFH) as well as clinical, echocardiographic, functional, and health status outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 299 patients were treated, with 2-year follow-up data available for 202 of 210 eligible patients (96.2%). Mean age was 75.5 ± 9.3 years, 50.8% were men, and the mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 6.6% ± 4.1%. At 2 years, MR reduction was sustained, with MR ≤1+ in 97.0% patients (P < 0.001). The 2-year composite rate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 35.6% (25.1% all-cause mortality, 23.0% HFH). In a 365-day landmark analysis, 1- to 2-year rates were 13.0% for all-cause mortality and 10.6% for first HFH. At 2 years, the rates of disabling stroke, clinically significant valve thrombosis, and hemolysis requiring intervention were 6.6%, 7.1%, and 7.6%, respectively. There were no instances of clinically significant left ventricular outflow obstruction. Improvements in functional and health status outcomes were sustained with 87.0% of patients in NYHA functional class I/II (P < 0.001) and a mean Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score increase of 17.2 points (P < 0.001). The 6-minute walk distance increased by +9.0 ± 97.3 m compared to baseline (P = 0.246). CONCLUSIONS: The 2-year results of the ENCIRCLE trial demonstrated durable near MR elimination with sustained improvements in functional and health status outcomes in surviving patients. These findings support transseptal TMVR as a therapeutic option for carefully selected patients with symptomatic MR. (The ENCIRCLE Trial [ENCIRCLE]; NCT04153292).

recs.title: Efficacy of fludrocortisone for symptom relief in patients with autonomic syncope and hypotensive phenotype.
recs.abstract: AIM: To assess the efficacy of fludrocortisone therapy in patients with autonomic syncope and hypotensive phenotype. METHODS AND RESULTS: Multicentre, prospective, non-randomized study. Fludrocortisone therapy was guided by clinician experience and supported by two 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) assessments-one before treatment start (ABPM 1) and one after drug optimization (ABPM 2). Primary endpoint: reduction of the syncope burden and presyncopal symptoms based on validated semi structured questionnaires. Secondary endpoint: hypotensive episodes on ABPM. In a cohort of 94 patients treated with fludrocortisone (median age 38 [IQR 21-57]) years, 83% females), 16 patients stopped therapy due to side effects, occurring during optimization (#11) or follow-up (#5). A total of 83 patients were analysed. The average 24-hour systolic blood pressure (SBP) increased from 106.3 ± 8.2 mmHg at ABPM 1 to 112.3 ± 9.3 at ABPM 2 (p = 0.0001). The number of daytime SBP drops <90 mmHg and <100 mmHg decreased by 61%, and 45% respectively (p < 0.001 for both). The annual syncope burden was reduced by 50.2%, from 2.0 (IQR 1.0-4.0) before therapy to 0.0 (IQR 0.0-1.8) episodes during a median follow-up of 12.9 months (p = 0.0001). Subjective symptom improvement was reported by 85.6% of patients. The frequency of syncope/presyncope decreased significantly, p = 0.009. The outcome was similar in 42 younger (23 ± 6 yrs) and in 41 older (56 ± 12 yrs) patients. CONCLUSION: Fludrocortisone therapy was associated with reduced hypotension and the burden of symptoms both in younger and in older patients. Side effects lead to discontinuation of therapy in 17% of cases.

recs.title: Vascular Phenotypes and Recurrent Arterial Events After Nontraumatic Cervical Artery Dissection.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic cervical artery dissection (CeAD) is often approached as a localized cervicocranial vascular disorder, although overlap with fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) and other arteriopathies suggests broader vascular disease. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to determine whether head-to-pelvis imaging identifies clinically meaningful vascular phenotypes after nontraumatic CeAD and whether these phenotypes are associated with recurrent arterial events. METHODS: Consecutive adults with CeAD evaluated in an institutional vascular medicine clinic underwent head-to-pelvis computed tomography and/or magnetic resonance angiography. Patients were classified as isolated CeAD, FMD-associated CeAD (FMD-CeAD), or multiple artery aneurysm and dissection without FMD (MAAD). Outcomes were recurrent CeAD and incident extracervical artery dissection. RESULTS: Among 315 patients, 136 (43.2%) had isolated CeAD, 100 (31.7%) had FMD-CeAD, and 79 (25.1%) had MAAD-CeAD. Overall, 179 patients (56.8%) had systemic vascular abnormalities, and 125 (39.7%) had findings below the neck. Recurrent CeAD was most frequent in isolated CeAD. Incident extracervical artery dissection occurred most frequently in MAAD-CeAD. Isolated CeAD was associated with recurrent CeAD compared with FMD-CeAD (HR: 3.26; 95% CI: 1.43 to 7.43). Among patients with FMD-CeAD or MAAD-CeAD, MAAD-CeAD was associated with incident extracervical artery dissection after adjustment for age at index CeAD (HR: 3.75; 95% CI: 1.17-12.00; P = 0.026), with similar results after additional adjustment for baseline aneurysm. CONCLUSIONS: Head-to-pelvis imaging identified frequent extracervical vascular abnormalities in patients with CeAD and phenotypes with distinct recurrent-event patterns. These findings support a cardiovascular arteriopathy framework for CeAD and provide a rationale for prospective studies of phenotype-guided imaging, genetic evaluation, counseling, and surveillance.

recs.title: Disparities in Editorial Leadership of Highly Cited Cardiology Journals by Gender and Country Income Classification.
The Impact of Clinical and Biochemical Frailty on Outcomes following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty results from declining reserve and function and is a modifiable cardiovascular risk-factor. Despite this, there is limited evidence surrounding its role in lower-risk TAVR cohorts. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate frailty among contemporary TAVR patients, delineate the impact of biochemical and clinical frailty, and understand its additive value to existing risk-prediction tools. METHODS: Analysis of a multicenter Australian registry. Biochemical frailty (BF) was defined as serum albumin <35 g/L and clinical frailty (CF) as a Rockwood Clinical Frailty Scale ≥5. Patients meeting BF or CF criteria were categorized as frail. RESULTS: Of the 2,661 patients, the median age 82 (IQR: 77-86), 60% male, and median STS 3.3 (2-5.2), 920 patients (35%) were considered frail. A total of 171 (19%) of frail patients fulfilled both BF and CF criteria. The frail group was older (83 vs 81, P < 0.001), more females (43% vs 38%; P = 0.016) with higher STS scores (4 vs 3, P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a stepwise increase in 12-month mortality with increasing frailty (no frailty 4% vs BF or CF 7% vs BF + CF 16%, Log-rank P < 0.001). In Cox proportional hazards regression BF or CF (adjusted HR: 1.6; 95% CI: 1.0-2.4; P = 0.033) and BF + CF (adjusted HR: 3.3; 95% CI: 1.9-5.6; P < 0.001) independently predicted 12-month mortality. Addition of frailty to STS Score improved mortality prediction (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: 0.608 vs 0.664; DeLong's P = 0.021), with Shapley analysis demonstrating significant contribution from frailty. CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is common with significant implications in TAVR. Patients with biochemical and clinical frailty criteria are highest risk. Development of strategies to address frailty is critical.

recs.title: Long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents versus coronary artery bypass grafting for left main coronary artery disease: a prospective analysis of the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stents has been widely used to treat patients with left main coronary artery disease; however, long-term comparative outcomes versus coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in real-world populations remain poorly characterised. We aimed to compare long-term all-cause mortality after PCI or CABG in Asian patients with unprotected left main coronary artery disease. METHODS: We analysed prospectively collected data from the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry, conducted at 46 hospitals in South Korea, India, Japan, Indonesia, and Malaysia. The registry enrolled adults aged 18 years or older with unprotected left main coronary artery disease (defined as a stenosis diameter of ≥50% as visually estimated on angiography), who had been treated with PCI, CABG, or medical therapy alone. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. We used a target trial emulation framework to compare the long-term risk of all-cause mortality between PCI with drug-eluting stents and isolated CABG. We used propensity-score overlap weighting to adjust for measured baseline covariates. The IRIS-MAIN Registry study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01341327). FINDINGS: Between Jan 1, 2003, and Dec 31, 2024, 6900 patients were enrolled in the IRIS-MAIN registry, of whom 5379 (78·0%) underwent coronary revascularisation through either PCI with drug-eluting stents (3836 [71·3%]) or CABG (1543 [28·7%]) and were included in the analysis. The median duration of follow-up for all patients was 10·0 years (IQR 5·0-16·7). In the overlap-weighted population, no statistically detectable difference in 10-year weighted Kaplan-Meier rates of all-cause mortality was observed between PCI and CABG (24·0% vs 22·9%; overlap-weighted hazard ratio 1·00 [95% CI 0·87-1·14]; p=0·99). The confidence interval does not exclude a mortality benefit or harm with either strategy. INTERPRETATION: In this non-randomised registry analysis of patients with left main coronary artery disease, there was no statistically detectable difference in all-cause mortality between PCI and CABG. For patients considered suitable for either strategy, multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion might help patients and clinicians weigh potential trade-offs in the choice between PCI and CABG. These findings are observational and cannot establish causal treatment effects or equivalence in survival. FUNDING: The CardioVascular Research Foundation (South Korea).

recs.title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction. METHODS: This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates. RESULTS: Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm3) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death. CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

recs.title: Percutaneous aspiration of vegetations in right-sided catheter-related infective endocarditis.
Implications of SGLT2 Inhibitors, GLP-1RAs, and Nonsteroidal MRAs on the Anticipated Burden of Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Several treatments that reduce the risk of heart failure (HF) have been introduced recently. Their impact on the future burden of HF in the U.S. has not been well characterized. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to estimate the potential impact of recently approved cardiometabolic medications on the future burden of HF in the United States. METHODS: Using a nationally representative sample of persons in the United States 30-79 years of age without cardiovascular disease at baseline, we used the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events) equation to estimate the 10- and 30-year burden of HF and the projected impact of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on these estimates. The authors estimated the total number of HF cases that could be averted with risk-based treatment and calculated the number needed to treat to prevent HF. RESULTS: An estimated 5.5 million (95% CI: 5.1-5.8 million) U.S. adults 30-79 years of age without established cardiovascular disease will develop HF over 10 years. It is estimated to decrease to 5.1 million (95% CI: 4.7-5.4 million) with indicated treatment with a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, 5.2 million (95% CI: 4.8-5.6 million) with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, 5.4 million (95% CI: 5.0-5.7 million) with nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and 4.8 million (95% CI: 4.4-5.2 million) with the use of combination therapy. The use of combination therapy in eligible persons with an estimated 10-year HF risk of ≥10% would result in 6.8 million (95% CI: 6.1-7.5 million) eligible participants, and 498,000 (95% CI: -663,000 to -319,000) fewer cases of HF, with a number needed to treat of 14 (95% CI: 10-22) to prevent 1 incident case. CONCLUSIONS: The projected burden of HF in the U.S. is substantial. A risk-based approach to preventive treatment may help reduce this considerably. The feasibility of such an approach deserves further investigation.

recs.title: An uncontainable 'ball' in the heart: a giant right sinus of Valsalva aneurysm.
TGFβ establishes the cardiac maturation niche.
Microvascular Resistance Reserve and Outcomes in Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is highly prevalent in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) is a novel index to assess CMD independently of epicardial disease and driving pressures, but the long-term prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR in patients with ANOCA is unknown. OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR and its association with clinical outcomes and symptom burden in patients with ANOCA. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective, multicenter cohort study within the Netherlands Registry of Invasive Coronary Vasomotor Function Testing (NL-CFT) included patients between July 2020 and June 2025 in 4 clinical centers in the Netherlands. Follow-up for clinical events and patient-reported symptoms was completed for up to 3 years. Clinical events were adjudicated by investigators blinded to CFT results. Consecutive patients with ANOCA who underwent continuous thermodilution were included. EXPOSURE: Abnormal MRR (CMD) was defined as less than 2.1, gray zone as 2.1 to 2.7, and normal microvascular function as 2.7 or greater. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, clinically indicated revascularization, repeat angiography without intervention, and unplanned hospital admittance or emergency department visit due to angina or heart failure. Secondary outcomes included angina at baseline and follow-up. Symptoms were assessed using the patient-reported Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) scores. RESULTS: Among 553 included patients (mean [SD] age, 59.1 [9.6] years; 459 female [83.0%]) with a mean (SD) follow-up of 27.5 (16.1) months, CMD was observed in 94 patients (17.0%). The main composite outcome did not differ across the 3 MRR categories (18 of 94 patients with abnormal [19.1%] vs 21 of 98 patients with gray zone [21.4%] vs 76 of 361 patients with normal [21.1%] MRR; log-rank P = .85). Individual outcomes did not differ between groups. There was no overall longitudinal interaction between MRR and SAQ summary scores. While low MRR (abnormal vs normal groups) was not associated with an increased symptom burden at baseline, it was associated with worse angina at follow-up (mean [SD] SAQ summary score, 53.0 [16.7] vs 60.1 [16.6]; P = .04) and less clinically relevant improvement (9 of 30 patients [30.0%] vs 52 of 88 patients [59.1%]; P = .02). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, CMD assessed by continuous thermodilution-derived MRR was not associated with clinical outcomes.

recs.title: Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement: The SINGLE-CLOSURE Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial. OBJECTIVES: This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications. METHODS: The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications. RESULTS: A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%). CONCLUSIONS: A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.

recs.title: Complementary Cardiohepatic Prognostic Value of Hepatic Steatosis in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic steatosis carries substantial cardiovascular risk, whereas cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome contributes to liver disease progression, highlighting the need for integrated cardiohepatic risk assessment. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate whether hepatic steatosis provides incremental prognostic value beyond CKM staging for cardiovascular and liver outcomes. METHODS: We included 313,970 UK Biobank participants with CKM stages 0 to 3. Hepatic steatosis was primarily assessed using the Fatty Liver Index, with the Hepatic Steatosis Index as an alternative measure and the Fibrosis-4 Index for liver fibrosis. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). The secondary outcome was major adverse liver events (MALEs). RESULTS: During a median 15.7-year follow-up, 32,110 MACEs and 1,599 MALEs occurred. Hepatic steatosis and advanced CKM were independently associated with both outcomes, with coexistence conferring the highest risks (MACEs: HR: 2.33; 95% CI: 2.19-2.47; MALEs: HR: 5.09; 95% CI: 3.97-6.54, vs neither exposure). For MACEs, the association with hepatic steatosis was stronger in nonadvanced CKM (stages 0-2: HR: 1.51; 95% CI: 1.48-1.55) than in stage 3 (HR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.97-1.23; Pinteraction < 0.001). For MALEs, hepatic steatosis mediated 41.1% of the association with CKM stage. The findings were consistent across alternative steatosis measures, whereas liver fibrosis showed no significant stage-dependent association with MACEs and a smaller mediation proportion for MALEs. Adding hepatic steatosis to CKM staging improved discrimination for both outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Hepatic steatosis provided complementary cardiovascular and liver prognostic value beyond CKM staging, supporting its integration for more comprehensive cardiohepatic risk stratification.

recs.title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown. METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population. RESULTS: A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: the H-HeFT trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate (H-ISDN) has shown benefit in earlier randomized trials of patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and chronic heart failure. This trial tested if H-ISDN could reduce worsening heart failure or mortality in patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) receiving contemporary treatment. METHODS: The Hydralazine-Isosorbide Dinitrate in Patients With Chronic Heart Failure Trial (H-HeFT) was a multicentre, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with HFrEF at 23 Danish hospitals (New York Heart Association class II-IV, elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and LVEF ≤40%). Target treatment was hydralazine 75 mg/isosorbide dinitrate 40 mg three times a day (t.i.d). The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization with worsening heart failure, an urgent outpatient visit resulting in intravenous/metolazone therapy for heart failure, heart transplantation, left ventricular assist device implantation, or death. Secondary endpoints included components of the primary outcome. RESULTS: Overall, 592 predominantly White patients (median age 72 years, 18% women) were randomized with a mean follow-up of 3.7 years. The primary outcome occurred in 90 of 294 patients (30.6%) in the H-ISDN group and in 91 of 298 patients (30.5%) in the placebo group [hazard ratio (HR) 0.90; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-1.21; P = .48]. There were 57 deaths in the H-ISDN group vs 72 in the placebo group (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.51-1.02); worsening heart failure events occurred in 52 vs 47 patients (HR 1.01; 95% CI 0.68-1.50). CONCLUSIONS: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate did not change the incidence of the composite endpoint of heart failure events or death in patients with heart failure and LVEF ≤40%.

recs.title: Norepinephrine Equivalent Dose for Mortality Risk Stratification in VA-ECMO Cardiogenic Shock.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) complicated by vasoplegia requiring venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) often need escalating vasopressor support and face high mortality. Norepinephrine equivalent dose (NEE) quantifies vasopressor burden, yet its prognostic value in VA-ECMO remains undefined. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to characterize the dose-response relationship between NEE and 30-day mortality, identify a clinically relevant NEE threshold, and determine factors associated with high vasopressor burden. METHODS: This bicentric retrospective study included 572 consecutive patients with CS requiring VA-ECMO. We collected vasopressor regimens, NEE trajectories, and hemodynamic parameters at predefined intervals. Restricted cubic splines assessed dose-response linearity. Maximally selected rank statistics with bootstrap validation identified optimal thresholds. Cox models estimated mortality risk. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with high vasopressor burden. RESULTS: The median NEE at ECMO initiation was 0.30 (IQR: 0.09-0.72) μg·kg-1·min-1; 86.2% received norepinephrine. NEE showed a linear dose-response with mortality (HR: 1.06 per 0.1 μg·kg-1·min-1 increment; 95% CI: 1.04-1.08; P < 0.001). A threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 identified high vasopressor burden with elevated 30-day mortality (61.8% vs 42.6%; P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 1.42; 95% CI: 1.11-1.81; P = 0.005). Factors associated with high vasopressor burden included mechanical ventilation (OR: 2.96; 95% CI: 1.08-8.07), prior epinephrine use (OR: 1.87; 95% CI: 1.12-3.14), renal replacement therapy before VA-ECMO (OR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.02-3.03), baseline lactate (OR: 1.05 per mmol/L; 95% CI: 1.01-1.09), and lower Survival After Veno-Arterial ECMO score (OR: 0.96 per point; 95% CI: 0.92-1.00). Left ventricular unloading was inversely associated (OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.34-0.87). CONCLUSIONS: In VA-ECMO-supported CS with vasoplegia, vasopressor burden shows a linear relationship with mortality. A NEE threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 may identify patients with elevated mortality risk.

From a single label to a life-course map: reading the whole pregnancy history to gauge maternal cardiovascular risk.
Hematopoietic loss of KDM6A impairs cardiac recovery in heart failure via epigenetic reprogramming of myeloid cells.
recs.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH), the expansion of blood cell clones carrying acquired mutations, is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Although mutations in DNMT3A and TET2 are well studied, the cardiovascular consequences of KDM6A mutations remain unclear. KDM6A is an X-linked histone demethylase that is commonly mutated in patients with heart failure (HF). Here we performed multiomics profiling and functional characterization of mouse models and patient-derived data to show that hematopoietic KDM6A loss impairs cardiac recovery after myocardial infarction (MI). KDM6A deficiency increases myeloid cell recruitment to the injured heart and reprograms monocytes, macrophages and neutrophils toward inflammatory, migratory and glycolytic states. Patients with HF and KDM6A-driven CH show similar pro-inflammatory monocyte signatures. KDM6A-silenced macrophages promote cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and cardiac fibroblast activation. Notably, IL-1β blockade after MI rescued the adverse cardiac phenotype of hematopoietic KDM6A loss. These findings identify KDM6A-driven CH as a driver of immune dysregulation and IL-1β signaling as a potential therapeutic target in CH-associated HF.

Angiography-Derived Radial Wall Strain Across All Epicardial Vessels Before Acute Coronary Syndrome: The CULPRIT-STRAIN Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Angiography-derived radial wall strain (RWS) is a biomechanical index associated with plaque vulnerability. Whether elevated RWS demonstrates culprit-vessel predominance or broader multivessel distribution within the same patient is unknown. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to compare maximal RWS (RWSmax) in the future culprit vessel with nonculprit vessels within the same patient and assess its association with time to acute coronary syndrome (ACS). METHODS: In the multicenter CULPRIT-STRAIN study, consecutive ACS patients with a prior coronary angiogram (≥3 months before event) were identified from a prospectively maintained registry (NCT04185285). RWSmax was measured in all 3 epicardial coronary arteries at the index angiogram. The primary endpoint was within-patient comparison of culprit vs nonculprit RWSmax; secondary endpoints included its association with index-to-ACS interval and the prevalence of multivessel biomechanical elevation. RESULTS: Among 101 patients (303 vessels; median index-to-ACS interval, 35 months), culprit-vessel RWSmax was higher than nonculprit-vessel RWSmax (19.7% vs 11.3%; P < 0.001). The culprit vessel had the highest RWSmax in 96 patients (95.0%; P < 0.001), with a median within-patient ΔRWS of 7.0% (IQR: 3.6%-13.2%). In exploratory analysis, higher culprit-vessel RWSmax was associated with a shorter index-to-ACS interval (ρ = -0.34; P < 0.001). Overall, 60.4% of patients had ≥2 vessels with RWSmax >12%. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who developed ACS, RWSmax demonstrated marked culprit-vessel predominance despite frequent multivessel elevation, indicating a graded distribution across vessels. These retrospective findings do not establish prospective risk prediction and require validation in unselected populations with event-free controls.

recs.title: Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) can compromise the administration and absorption of oral P2Y12 inhibitors and carries high ischaemic and mortality risks. This trial assessed whether intravenous cangrelor was non-inferior to crushed oral ticagrelor for short-term clinical outcomes and whether it provided faster and more consistent platelet inhibition in patients with AMI-CS. METHODS: DAPT-SHOCK-AMI was a double-blind trial conducted at 29 hospitals across five European countries (Czech Republic, France, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia). Patients older than 18 years with AMI-CS were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio, stratified by centre, age, sex, presence or absence of ST-segment elevation, and mechanical ventilation) to cangrelor (30 μg/kg bolus followed by an infusion of 4 μg/kg per min for at least 2 h) or crushed ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose). The primary laboratory endpoint was a platelet reactivity index of less than 50% at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary clinical endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, or ischaemic stroke at 30 days. The primary clinical endpoint was analysed for non-inferiority with a prespecified margin of 1 percentage point among all randomly assigned patients who received study treatment. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03551964) and EudraCT (2018-002161-19); recruitment and 1-year follow-up are complete, and 5-year follow-up is ongoing. FINDINGS: Between Aug 1, 2018, and Jan 19, 2024, 605 patients (137 [23%] were female) were randomly assigned to cangrelor (n=298) or ticagrelor (n=307); no surviving patients were lost to the 1-year follow-up. The primary laboratory endpoint was analysed in 56 (19%) patients in the cangrelor group and 68 (22%) in the ticagrelor group, and was achieved in 56 (100%) of 56 patients receiving cangrelor and 15 (22%) of 68 receiving ticagrelor (p<0·0001). The 30-day primary clinical endpoint occurred in 112 (38%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 126 (41%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor; non-inferiority was not demonstrated (difference -4 percentage points [90% CI -10 to 3]; Pnon-inferiority=0·13). Major bleeding at 30 days occurred in 19 (6%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 16 (5%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor. INTERPRETATION: To our knowledge, this is the first randomised trial to compare P2Y12 inhibitor strategies specifically in patients with AMI-CS. Cangrelor achieved effective platelet inhibition more frequently than crushed ticagrelor at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Non-inferiority of cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor was not demonstrated for the primary 30-day clinical endpoint. These trial findings can inform future trials of P2Y12 inhibition strategies in patients with AMI-CS. FUNDING: Czech Republic Ministry of Health, Charles University (Czech Republic), and NextGenerationEU.

recs.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate whether GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), compared with DPP4 (dipeptidyl peptidase-4) inhibitors or sulfonylureas, are associated with reduced all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalizations in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. METHODS: PRAISE-HFpEF (Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction) was a nationwide multicenter cohort study using a new-user, active-comparator design within the national Veterans Affairs Health System (170 US hospitals). Adults with type 2 diabetes between January 1, 2000 and December 31, 2021, were identified from centralized electronic health records. Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and a body mass index ≥30 kg/m2 were selected using a validated diagnostic algorithm. Exposure was initiation of a GLP-1RA versus DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2021. The primary outcome was time to all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on the propensity score was used to balanced baseline characteristics. RESULTS: Among 179 288 patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, 1024 GLP-1RA users and 796 DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea users met inclusion criteria. Over a median follow-up of 1.5 years, GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.64-0.95], P=0.01). Weight loss was modestly greater with GLP-1RAs compared with DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea (-12.9% versus -10.1%). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with obese heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a lower incidence of death or heart failure hospitalization compared with alternative oral agents.

Ventricular arrhythmia-heart failure interaction and mortality in ICD recipients after myocardial infarction.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Ventricular arrhythmia (VA) and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist in patients with ischaemic left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Whether VA and HF events are bidirectionally associated remains unclear. We investigated their bidirectional relationship and associations with mortality. METHODS: We analysed 1014 patients from the multicentre WICD-MI study. All received a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator after acute myocardial infarction (MI) and subsequently underwent implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) implantation, with persistent LV ejection fraction ≤35%. Associations between ICD-treated VA, HF-events (HF hospitalization, heart transplantation, or LV assist device implantation), and all-cause mortality were assessed using time-dependent Cox models. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 2.6 years post-ICD implantation, VA was independently associated with an increased risk of HF events [aHR = 3.50 (1.66-7.38), P = .001], while HF events similarly preceded subsequent VA [aHR = 2.96 (1.59-5.50), P = .0008]. Both were independently associated with all-cause mortality, with a numerically higher aHR for HF events [aHR = 7.96 (4.71-13.47), P < .0001] than for VA [aHR = 4.43 (2.35-8.36), P < .0001]. Sensitivity analyses suggested that the VA-HF association was strongest for shock-treated arrhythmias. In exploratory analyses, VA was strongly associated with subsequent HF events in subcutaneous ICD recipients [aHR = 15.08 (4.62-49.22), P < .0001] but not in transvenous ICD recipients (P for interaction = .0002). CONCLUSION: In ICD recipients with persistent LV dysfunction following MI, VA and HF events are bidirectionally associated and independently associated with mortality. The VA-HF association was strongest for shock-treated arrhythmias. These findings highlight the potential value of integrated HF and VA management.

recs.title: Atrial Leadless Pacemaker Implantation at the Superior Right Atrial Site.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Right atrial appendage (RAA) pacing may produce nonphysiological atrial activation. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and electrocardiographic characteristics of atrial leadless pacemaker implantation at the superior right atrium (RA). METHODS: Sixty-eight consecutive patients undergoing dual-chamber leadless pacemaker implantation were studied. Procedural, device, electrocardiographic, and clinical outcomes were compared between superior RA and RAA base pacing. RESULTS: Superior RA implantation succeeded in 26/46 attempts (56.5%), increasing from 27.8% to 60.0% and 92.3% across sequential periods. In noncrossover cases, procedure (72.7±16.4 vs 76.8±27.2 minutes; P=0.533) and fluoroscopy times (15.4±5.8 vs 18.6±11.9 minutes; P=0.249) were comparable. P-wave duration remained unchanged with superior RA pacing (99.7±29.9 to 98.1±25.6 ms; P=0.543) but increased with RAA pacing (106.7±23.1 to 134.9±25.6 ms; P<0.001); P-wave terminal force in V1 changed from 3.6% to 3.6% versus 10.0% to 45.0%, respectively (P<0.001 for RAA). PR intervals increased from 228.4±72.8 to 229.7±77.5 ms (P=0.038) and from 205.5±72.0 to 234.4±72.6 ms (P<0.001), respectively; the increase was smaller with superior RA pacing (+5.7±11.7 vs +38.6±31.3 ms; P<0.001). At 3 months, sensing amplitudes (3.4±1.5 vs 2.4±1.1 mV; P=0.091) and pacing thresholds (0.8±0.5 vs 0.8±0.3 V; P=0.785) were comparable. No pericardial tamponade occurred. During 10.4±4.6 months, mortality, heart failure events, and atrial fibrillation incidence did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: Superior RA pacing was feasible, showed a marked learning curve, and better preserved intrinsic atrial activation than RAA pacing.

recs.title: AI algorithms and external validation: promises, pitfalls, and a practical blueprint.
recs.abstract: External validation involving the testing of a frozen AI model on independent data from other sites, populations, time periods, or devices provides the clearest estimate of intended-use setting performance when those external data are deployment-representative of the expected population, measurement processes, and clinical workflow. It yields realistic estimates of discrimination and calibration, exposes shortcut learning and distribution shift, quantifies clinical utility through decision-analytic measures, and reveals subgroup disparities requiring mitigation. Yet common pitfalls undermine credibility: quasi-external splits with hidden relatedness; spectrum and prevalence mismatch; site, workflow, and hardware effects; label noise and reference-standard drift; analytic flexibility and selective reporting; small, underpowered samples; reliance only on the area under the curve; unreported threshold tuning; and leakage. A practical blueprint emphasizes pre-registration; representative, multi-site cohorts spanning geography, time, and acquisition; prevention of patient and temporal overlap; comprehensive evaluation of discrimination, calibration (including calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, and calibration plots), and net benefit with confidence intervals; pre-specified subgroup and fairness audits; transparent labelling procedures and uncertainty analyses; principled sample-size calculations; and minimal, well-documented model updating (recalibration before revision). Finally, external validation should connect to post-deployment governance via drift detection, performance triggers, and change-control plans, complemented by site-specific local evaluation to ensure safety and reliability across diverse clinical environments. When executed to these standards, external validation transforms promising prototypes into dependable clinical tools, clarifying where a model performs, where it fails, and what adaptations are necessary for safe, equitable, and sustainable use. This framework links statistical evaluation to clinical use, model updating, and post-deployment monitoring.

recs.title: Early Increases in GDF-15 Are Associated With Declines in Cardiac Function With Breast Cancer Therapy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15 is a stress-responsive cytokine induced by mitochondrial dysfunction and genotoxic stress, mechanisms central to anthracycline cardiotoxicity. Whether early changes in GDF-15 following cancer therapy relate to subsequent cardiac dysfunction is not established. OBJECTIVES: We evaluated the longitudinal trajectory of GDF-15 and its associations with changes in cardiac function and structure following cardiotoxic cancer therapy in women with breast cancer. METHODS: In 366 women receiving anthracyclines and/or trastuzumab from the Penn Cardiotoxicity of Cancer Therapy prospective cohort study, associations between baseline, early-peak (maximum 0-6-month change), and longitudinal GDF-15 concentrations with quantitative echocardiographic measures of systolic, diastolic, and structural function over 36 months were evaluated using multivariable linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS: GDF-15 rose from a median baseline of 662 to an early-peak of 1,412 pg/mL, with trajectories differing across regimens (P = 0.004). Each doubling of the early-peak-to-baseline GDF-15 ratio was associated with a subsequent 1.5 percentage point decline in left ventricular ejection fraction (β -1.5%; 95% CI: -2.5 to -0.6; P = 0.002) and a 0.9-unit worsening in longitudinal strain (β 0.9; 95% CI: 0.4-1.4; P = 0.001). GDF-15 was not associated with diastolic outcomes, incident diastolic dysfunction, or incident cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction. CONCLUSIONS: In women receiving anthracycline- and/or trastuzumab-based breast cancer therapy, early increases in GDF-15 were associated with modest declines in left ventricular ejection fraction and worsening of longitudinal strain, without associations with diastolic measures. These findings support mechanistic investigation of GDF-15 in anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity. (Cardiotoxicity of Cancer Therapy [CCT]; NCT01173341).

recs.title: CaMKIIδ-TRPC6 Activates an RyR-BKCa Feedback Axis in Aging Arteries.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: TRP (transient receptor potential) cation channels play a crucial role in maintaining normal blood pressure and flow. We hypothesize that, during aging, TRPC6 (transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily C member 6)-mediated Ca2+ influx promotes sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ refilling and RyR (ryanodine receptor) Ca2+ sparks, thereby activating BKCa (large-conductance Ca2+-activated K+) channels to limit myogenic arterial tone. METHODS: Using vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) from resistance-sized small mesenteric arteries, we tested selective TRPC6 inhibitors (SH045 and SAR7334) and smooth muscle-specific TRPC6 knockout mice. Ca2+ sparks, BKCa currents, and myogenic tone were measured in young (3-4 months) and old (12-14 months) mice. CaMKIIδ (Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase IIδ) signaling was assessed pharmacologically and with a proteolysis-targeting chimera peptide degrader targeting CaMKIIδ. RESULTS: Inhibiting TRPC6 with SH045 or SAR7334 suppressed RyR-mediated Ca2+ spark generation in VSMCs from old mice but not young mice. Similar results were found in smooth muscle-specific TRPC6 knockout mice. SH045 or SAR7334 also suppressed BKCa currents and elicited constriction in mesenteric arteries from old mice. These effects were due to increased translocation of TRPC6 channels to the VSMC plasma membrane, mediated by CaMKIIδ signaling. Using a proteolysis-targeting chimera peptide degrader targeting CaMKIIδ, we demonstrated the impact of CaMKIIδ on TRPC6 externalization and RyR activation in old VSMCs. CONCLUSIONS: Together, our findings identify age-dependent CaMKIIδ upregulation as a key regulator of TRPC6 membrane trafficking, thereby indirectly enhancing RyR-BKCa signaling through sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ handling and promoting VSMC hyperpolarization and vasodilation in aging.
