Controversy: Anticoagulants need to be maintained after catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in patients at risk of stroke-Pro and Contra.
recs.abstract: The pillars of atrial fibrillation (AF) management include stroke prevention, patient-centred symptom directed decisions on rhythm or rate control, and the proactive management of comorbidities and lifestyle changes. These pillars are not in isolation; they are complementary to each other. While oral anticoagulants (OACs) are highly effective for reducing stroke and all-cause mortality in patients with AF, these drugs confer a risk of major bleeding, including intracranial bleeding. Evidence from clinical trials and observational data shows that early rhythm control, especially with catheter ablation, results in a reduction in stroke risk and/or the reduction in AF burden. The question arises therefore, whether in patients with intermediate or low stroke risk after successful catheter ablation, whether or not to continue or discontinue OAC. Recent randomized trials and observational data have created some debate about whether OAC can be routinely stopped after a successful catheter ablation procedure, without a higher risk of thromboembolism. In this pro/contra article, we will debate the arguments for and against the cessation of anti-coagulation after catheter ablation, in the context of recent evidence from clinical trials, observational data, and meta-analysis.

recs.title: Variability of lipoprotein(a) levels in patients with acute myocardial infarction between admission, discharge, and follow-up.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Using Lp(a) concentrations measured during stable follow-up as the reference, we aimed to assess the temporal variability of Lp(a) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and to explore a pragmatic strategy for Lp(a) measurement. METHODS AND RESULTS: The FRENCHIE-Lp(a) cohort enrolled consecutive adults hospitalized for AMI in 21 centres. Lp(a) mass concentration, measured at admission, hospital discharge, and 3-12 months follow-up, was analysed both as a continuous and predefined categorical variable (≤20, >20-≤50, >50-≤70, >70 mg/dL). Assuming follow-up Lp(a) as the reference, we aimed to identify the threshold values that would allow us to accurately identify patients with Lp(a) > 70mg/dL, the threshold mostly used for patient selection in phase III trials of targeted Lp(a) therapies. A cumulative threshold analysis was performed to identify the Lp(a) value below which the misclassification rate (i.e. % of patients with follow-up Lp(a) > 70 mg/dL) remained <1%. Among 1561 patients (aged 61 ± 12 years; 21.3% women), median Lp(a) was 13 mg/dL at admission and remained stable over time (median difference overtime = 0 mg/dL). However, only 68.5% of patients remained in the same Lp(a) category overtime. In patients with discharge-Lp(a) ≤37 mg/dL (72.5% of the population), only 0.97% had Lp(a) >70 mg/dL at follow-up compared to 39.9% of those with discharge-Lp(a) >37 mg/dL. CONCLUSION: Although the median Lp(a) level remained stable between admission and follow-up, one-third of AMI patients shifted within Lp(a) categories over time. Pending external validation, an exploratory two-step strategy based on Lp(a) measurement at discharge, followed by repeat testing in patients with Lp(a) >37 mg/dL, showed a misclassification rate below 1% for identifying patients potentially needing intervention. REGISTRATION: Clinical trial Number: NCT04050956.

recs.title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: The SIMPLAAFY Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown. OBJECTIVE: To determine if either reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment. RESULTS: The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, -1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, -3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, -0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria (P < .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06521463.

recs.title: Statin-Ezetimibe Combination Therapy versus Statin Monotherapy in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the Randomized Ez-PAVE Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In a target-directed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)-lowering strategy, the impact of the initial treatment regimen has not been investigated in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. We compared the efficacy and safety of initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy versus statin monotherapy within intensive or conventional LDL-C-targeting strategies. METHODS: In this prespecified second randomization of the randomized Ez-PAVE trial (Effects of Ezetimibe Combination Therapy for Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Randomized Comparison of LDL Cholesterol Targeting <70 versus <55 mg/dL) conducted at 17 centers in South Korea, a total of 3048 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled between January 2021 and July 2022. Following the first randomization to either an intensive (<55 mg/dL) or conventional (<70 mg/dL) LDL-C-targeting strategy, patients underwent subsequent randomization (initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy [n=1525] versus statin monotherapy [n=1523]) and were followed up for 3 years. Lipid-lowering therapy was adjusted according to a predefined protocol to achieve LDL-C targets. The primary end point was a 3-year composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, any revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina. RESULTS: The mean±SD age was 64.4±9.0 years, and 638 patients (20.9%) were female. The incidence of the primary end point did not differ between statin-ezetimibe combination therapy (128 patients [8.5%]) and statin monotherapy (119 patients [7.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.83-1.37]; P=0.596). Patients who received statin-ezetimibe combination therapy achieved lower median LDL-C levels during follow-up than those who received statin monotherapy in both the intensive-targeting (53 mg/dL [interquartile range, 45-62 mg/dL] versus 62 mg/dL [interquartile range, 53-74 mg/dL]) and conventional-targeting (63 mg/dL [interquartile range, 55-73 mg/dL] versus 70 mg/dL [interquartile range, 62-81 mg/dL]) strategies. During follow-up, ezetimibe was added to the treatment regimen of 241 patients (34.3%) and 177 patients (24.8%) who initially received statin monotherapy in the intensive- and conventional-targeting strategies, respectively. The treatment effect of intensive-targeting versus conventional-targeting strategies was consistent regardless of therapy regimens without significant heterogeneity (Pinteraction=0.583). The safety end points were similar between the groups. CONCLUSIONS: Within a target-directed LDL-C-lowering strategy, cardiovascular efficacy and safety did not differ significantly, whether initiated as statin-ezetimibe combination therapy or as statin monotherapy, but combination therapy facilitated achievement of a lower LDL-C target. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04626973.

recs.title: Systemic Hypertension and Survival in Pulmonary Hypertension.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a progressive and life-threatening condition with rising prevalence among older adults, frequently coexists with systemic hypertension, the prognostic impact of which is poorly understood. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between systemic hypertension and survival in patients with PH. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter cohort study analyzed data from the Pulmonary Vascular Research Institute GoDeep meta-registry, integrating global retrospective and prospective PH cohorts (n = 3238 in Europe, n = 3014 in North America, n = 96 in Africa, n = 802 in Asia, and n = 851 in Oceania). Survival was assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and adjusted for key confounders, with sensitivity analyses to validate robustness. Independent external validation was performed in a cohort in the UK. A total of 12 771 patients with incident PH (median [IQR] age, 65 [53-73] years; 7372 [58%] female) were diagnosed via right heart catheterization and comprehensive clinical data, encompassing PH groups 1-5 and all age categories. The study spans diagnosis decades from 1980 to 2020. Data were analyzed from February 2025 until September 2026. EXPOSURES: Center-reported diagnosis of systemic hypertension, baseline systolic systemic arterial pressure (sSAP), and heart rate as well as longitudinal sSAP and heart rate trajectories. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: All-cause mortality, adjusted for confounding variables, including age, PH group, antihypertensive and PH-specific medications, and cardiac index. RESULTS: Higher baseline sSAP and preexisting systemic hypertension were independently associated with improved survival. Patients with hypertension exhibited a 26% reduced mortality hazard (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74; 95% CI, 0.68-0.79) compared to their counterparts without hypertension. Survival benefits correlated positively with increasing sSAP (80-180 mm Hg), remained consistent across PH groups and age groups, and were independent of antihypertensive and PH-specific medications. Elevated heart rate was associated with higher mortality. sSAP increments correlated with improved cardiac index and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion. Decreased sSAP and higher heart rate during follow-up correlated with higher mortality. External validation in a separate UK cohort confirmed these findings. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this global PH cohort, higher sSAP was associated with enhanced survival, while a higher baseline heart rate and declining systemic blood pressure during follow-up were significantly associated with increased mortality risk.

recs.title: When the Conversation Is the Intervention: Serious Illness Communication Skills in Adult Congenital Heart Disease.
PCSK9-Targeting Therapies and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
recs.abstract: AIMS: To evaluate the association of PCSK9-targeting therapies with mortality and cardiovascular events in stable or clinically stabilized randomized trial populations. METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized trials comparing alirocumab, evolocumab or inclisiran with placebo or active control. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261395609). Treatment effects were pooled as incidence rate ratios (IRRs) using random-effects models. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Prespecified subgroup analyses were based on trial-level known atherosclerosis status, as defined by enrollment criteria. RESULTS: Thirty-two trials enrolled 77,178 participants. Individual atherosclerosis status could not be determined beyond trial-level eligibility criteria. Mortality estimates were predominantly informed by large cardiovascular outcome trials. All-cause mortality was lower with PCSK9-targeting therapy (IRR 0.88, 95% CI 0.82-0.95). Estimates favored PCSK9-targeting treatment in both trials requiring known atherosclerosis for enrollment (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.98) and trials without such an enrollment requirement (IRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.62-0.97; interaction p = 0.21). PCSK9-targeting treatment additionally reduced myocardial infarction, stroke, and coronary revascularization rates. Leave-one-out estimates remained directionally consistent. CONCLUSION: PCSK9-targeting therapies were associated with lower all-cause mortality and fewer ischemic events across trial populations. The predominant contribution of large cardiovascular outcome trials enrolling populations with known atherosclerosis and using PCSK9 antibodies limits the ability to infer a survival benefit in populations not selected on the basis of atherosclerosis status and across individual therapies, particularly inclisiran.

recs.title: Prognosis of Native T1 Mapping in TTR Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: Beaten to the Finish Line by Extracellular Volume.
Role of reverse remodelling in recurrence of atrial fibrillation after patient-tailored catheter ablation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Catheter ablation (CA) is a curative treatment for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet success rates remain sub-optimal, with ∼50% of patients with persistent AF experiencing recurrence after 1 year. This may be due to the self-perpetuating nature of AF, which remodels atrial structure and cellular properties, while successful treatment can induce reverse remodelling (RR). This study develops a patient-specific CA strategy to directly target re-entrant drivers (RDs) and investigates the role of RR in AF recurrence. METHODS: Left atrial (LA) models were reconstructed from LGE-MRI scans of AF patients (n = 15) and coupled with the Courtemanche-Ramirez-Nattel (CRN) electrophysiology model. RDs were induced via pacing, identified using DGM analysis, and targeted ablation was performed in-silico. Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) was applied as a reference. Following termination, AF recurrence was tested under three levels of electrical reverse remodelling (ERR: 0%, 50%, and 100%), with and without structural reverse remodelling (SRR). RESULTS: Targeted ablation acutely terminated AF in all patient-specific models. After the first procedure, AF recurrence decreased progressively from 55% at 0% ERR to 36.7% at 50% ERR and 5% at 100% ERR; with additional SRR, recurrence was further reduced to 46.7%, 26.7%, and 0%, respectively. After the second CA procedure, AF recurrence rate was 42.9%, 17.9%, and 0% without SRR and 25%, 14.3%, and 0% with SRR. CONCLUSION: This study highlights the importance of RR for therapy success, with a novel targeted CA technique ensuring <5% AF recurrence in patient-specific simulations. After clinical validation, this approach can help improve long-term patient outcomes.

recs.title: Characteristics and Mechanisms of Septal Myocardial Injury and Repair Following Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) requires screwing the lead deep into the interventricular septum. Multiple attempts are often required to achieve proper capture of the conduction system. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of deep screwing attempts on septal myocardial injury and repair and to explore the underlying mechanisms. METHODS: Prospective LBBAP implantation was performed in 41 patients with bradycardia. Serum creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) and left ventricular (LV) global longitudinal strain (GLS) were used to evaluate myocardial damage. Mechanisms of septal damage were explored in 24 LBBAP canines using histopathological and molecular changes. RESULTS: Compared to patients with ≤ 3 attempts, those with >3 attempts had a higher incidence of CK-MB elevation (6 vs. 44%, P=0.004), a less negative LV endocardial (-17.9 vs. -13.6 %, P<0.001), and mid-myocardial GLS (-15.3 vs. -12.4 %, P<0.001). In animal study, molecular changes associated with >3 attempts featured amplified HMGB1-centered sterile inflammation and enhanced CD206+ macrophage-mediated profibrotic remodeling. Canines with >3 attempts were characterized by three markedly thickened concentric reparative layers around the lead-inner thrombus layer, middle fibrous sheath layer, and outer reactive fibrotic layer. Interestingly, removal of the pacing lead after >3 attempts resulted in only mild scattered fibrosis, with markedly attenuated CD206+ macrophage-mediated profibrotic pathway. CONCLUSIONS: LBBAP with >3 deep septal screwing attempts was associated with a higher risk of septal myocardial injury and markedly thickened concentric reparative layers, underpinned by more pronounced sterile inflammation, profibrotic remodeling, and foreign body reaction.

recs.title: Impact of Statin and Aspirin Use on Dementia Diagnosis Stratified by Cardiovascular Risk.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) dementia share common risk factors. However, the role of ASCVD prevention therapies in AD dementia prevention is not fully understood. We examined the effect of LLT and antiplatelets with dementia and AD dementia diagnoses across ASCVD risk profiles. METHODS: We used data from primary prevention registry derived from a large healthcare network. Multivariable Cox proportional models were generated to study dementia and AD dementia diagnoses, stratified by ASCVD risk profiles. Impact of aspirin and LLT use on dementia and AD dementia diagnoses was assessed in adjusted models. RESULTS: Among n= 347,128, 2.4% developed dementia and 2.0% developed AD dementia over a median follow-up of 7.94 years. In adjusted models, dementia (HR, 2.59; 95% CI [2.29-2.92]) and AD dementia (HR, 2.85; 95% CI [2.49-3.25]) was higher in high risk patients. Low and high-dose aspirin among high ASCVD risk had lower dementia (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, [0.77-1.00] and HR, 0.83; 95% [CI 0.77-0.90]) and AD dementia (HR, 0.83; 95% CI [0.77-0.91] and HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.73-0.97]). Similarly, moderate- to high-dose LLT use among high ASCVD risk groups was associated with lower dementia (HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.79-0.93]) and AD dementia (HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.78-0.93]). CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline ASCVD risk was associated with increased risk of dementia and AD dementia diagnoses. Aspirin and moderate- to high-dose LLT use among patients with high ASCVD risk was associated with lower dementia and AD dementia risk.

recs.title: Performance of the PREVENT-HF Equations Across Heart Failure Subtypes in Community-Based and Ambulatory Healthcare Samples.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The PREVENT-HF equations estimate 10-year risk of overall heart failure (HF), inclusive of both HF with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF; HFrEF). Given differential risk factor profiles, pathophysiology, and therapeutic strategies for each HF subtype, we sought to examine the performance of PREVENT-HF for subtype-specific risk assessment. METHODS: We included data from five pooled longitudinal cohort studies (baseline exam 1989 to 2013) and two longitudinal primary-care electronic health record-based samples (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center [BIDMC], baseline 2004 to 2014; Mass General Brigham [MGB], baseline 2001 to 2018). We assessed the performance of the PREVENT-HF equations in predicting 10-year incident HFrEF and HFpEF, including model discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC]; average precision [AP]/event rate) and calibration (integrated calibration index [ICI]), in adults aged 30-79 years without prevalent cardiovascular disease or HF. RESULTS: The pooled cohort studies included 23,652 (55% women, age 60 ± 13 years), of whom 1,232 developed HF (432 [35%] HFpEF, 522 [42%] HFrEF). The BIDMC sample included 29,815 (55% women, 50 ± 13 years), of whom 259 (1%) developed HF (133 [51%] HFpEF, 101 [39%] HFrEF). MGB included 138,999 (62% women, 52 ± 13 years), of whom 1050 developed HF (586 [56%] HFpEF, 381 [36%] HFrEF). PREVENT-HF demonstrated better discrimination for HFpEF than HFrEF across all samples: in the pooled cohorts, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.824 (95% CI 0.807, 0.839) versus 0.789 (95% CI 0.770, 0.807) for HFrEF; in BIDMC, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.897 (95% CI 0.874, 0.918) versus 0.833 (95% CI 0.791, 0.869) for HFrEF; in MGB, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.864 (95% CI 0.848, 0.880) versus 0.797 (95% CI 0.771, 0.820) for HFrEF. Similar results were reflected in the AP/event rate ratios: 2.92 (95% CI 2.47, 3.54) for HFpEF compared to 2.66 (95% CI 2.33, 3.14) for HFrEF in the pooled cohorts; 8.08 (95% CI 6.12, 12.30) for HFpEF compared to 5.12 (95% CI 3.84, 8.17) for HFrEF in BIDMC; and 6.84 (95% CI 5.66, 8.28) for HFpEF compared to 4.12 (95% CI 3.37, 5.16) for HFrEF in MGB. Calibration was similar for HFpEF and HFrEF across samples. For example, in the pooled cohorts, the ICI for HFpEF was 0.041 (95% CI 0.039, 0.043) and for HFrEF was 0.038 (95% CI 0.036, 0.040). CONCLUSIONS: PREVENT-HF demonstrated excellent discrimination for both HF subtypes across community-based cohorts and real-world samples, with consistently better discrimination for HFpEF as compared to HFrEF. Given PREVENT-HF was developed to estimate overall HF risk rather than subtype-specific risk, future studies are needed to establish subtype-specific risk thresholds.

recs.title: Beyond the Lumen: Rethinking Plaque, Patency, and Outcomes in Coronary Bypass Grafts.
Defining the Substrate in Scar-Related Ventricular Tachycardia: A Hierarchy of Evidence for Arrhythmogenicity.
recs.abstract: Scar-related monomorphic ventricular tachycardia is sustained by a limited re-entry circuit within a much larger field of diseased myocardium. Late gadolinium enhancement cardiac magnetic resonance and cardiac computed tomography define scar distribution, channel architecture, wall thickness, and tissue composition, but cannot demonstrate conduction or circuit participation. Voltage mapping and abnormal electrograms identify electrically abnormal myocardium, although their appearance depends on activation sequence, catheter geometry, contact, and annotation. Functional mapping reveals rate-dependent slowing, decrement, and block that may be concealed during baseline rhythm. Mapping during ventricular tachycardia (VT) provides the most direct evidence of circuit participation, but is often limited by hemodynamic instability, noninducibility, or incomplete surface representation of a 3-dimensional circuit. This review examines how to weight these findings when defining the arrhythmogenic substrate. Structural imaging establishes where a circuit could reside and how it may be accessed. Baseline electroanatomic mapping characterizes the electrical expression of surviving myocardium, while functional mapping tests whether conduction deteriorates with changes in wave front or coupling interval. Activation and entrainment provide the strongest evidence that a region participates in a specific VT. These findings should be integrated hierarchically rather than by simple spatial overlap, adjusting interpretation for disease phenotype, substrate depth, mapped surface, and recording conditions. The arrhythmogenic substrate is best understood as surviving myocardium within scar whose 3-dimensional architecture and electrophysiological behavior permit re-entry. A reproducible definition will require standardized acquisition and annotation, explicit reporting of the evidence linking a region to VT, and prospective validation using mapped circuits.

recs.title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Sudden Cardiac Death: Epidemiology, Mechanisms, Risk Stratification, and Prevention.
recs.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most prevalent chronic metabolic liver disease worldwide. Cardiovascular adverse events have long been the leading cause of death in the MASLD population, far exceeding liver-related mortality. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) represents the most insidious and rapidly progressing extreme clinical phenotype among these cardiovascular complications. However, the relationship between MASLD and SCD has long received insufficient attention. Accumulating evidence from clinical studies indicates that MASLD is associated with elevated sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) risk independent of conventional cardiometabolic risk factors. Notably, while non-invasive clinical proxies of hepatic steatosis (such as the fatty liver index) identify individuals with heightened susceptibility to SCA, advancing liver fibrosis shows the strongest, gradient-dependent association with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, although its relation to SCA or SCD specifically requires confirmation. Sudden death in MASLD may result from primary ventricular arrhythmias or, in advanced cirrhosis, from non-shockable arrest due to hemodynamic, infectious, or metabolic decompensation. Although shared cardiometabolic risk factors account for a substantial portion of this association, proposed mechanisms include insulin resistance-related myocardial energy disturbances, inflammation-associated myocardial and electrophysiological remodeling, cirrhosis-associated circulatory dysfunction, and gut-derived endotoxemia. In clinical practice, non-invasive fibrosis scores, circulating biomarkers, and imaging parameters represent promising candidate risk markers for evaluating electrophysiological vulnerability, though a validated, MASLD-specific SCD risk prediction model remains to be established. Strategies such as lifestyle intervention, metabolic-targeted pharmacotherapy, and intensive management of cardiovascular risk factors may interrupt the progression from MASLD to SCD. This review summarizes the current evidence to inform cardiovascular risk management across the course of MASLD.

recs.title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion and Anticoagulation: From Alternative to Complementary Stroke Prevention.
Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis. METHODS: In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing. RESULTS: At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

recs.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability.
recs.abstract: Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. EVLF-FM supports disease diagnosis, visual question answering and pixel-level visual grounding with reasoning capabilities. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. A hybrid training strategy combining supervised and visual reinforcement fine-tuning enables EVLF-FM to generate clinically interpretable explanations aligned with visual evidence. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment.

recs.title: Validation of the PREVENT-HF Risk Prediction Equation in US Veterans.
The Art Behind the Algorithm: Hybrid Ablation and the Need for a Lifetime Strategy in Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
recs.abstract: The management of persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation remains highly variable in clinical practice, despite increasingly refined guidelines and an expanding ablation armamentarium. Treatment sequencing is frequently driven by local program infrastructure and institutional culture, and hybrid ablation is often deferred until multiple endocardial procedures have failed, by which point progressive atrial remodeling may have already narrowed the therapeutic window. Randomized and registry data support a meaningful role for hybrid ablation earlier in the disease course of selected patients with non-paroxysmal AF, particularly those with enlarged atria, prolonged AF duration, advanced substrate, or failed prior endocardial ablation. Contemporary pulsed-field ablation technology has improved procedural safety and efficiency, yet freedom from recurrence at one year in persistent AF remains substantially lower than in paroxysmal AF across all current energy platforms, reflecting the complexity of atrial substrate over time. This ongoing myocardial remodeling places non-paroxysmal AF closer to a chronic structural cardiac disease than to a discrete procedural target and demands a lifetime management strategy rather than a sequence of isolated procedural decisions. The mindset for other progressive structural cardiac diseases has already moved in this direction-aortic valve stenosis is now managed through a multidisciplinary team that integrates anatomy, timing, procedural durability, and long-term risk across the full patient trajectory. We propose an AF Heart Team framework for non-paroxysmal AF in which catheter-based, hybrid, and surgical strategies are selected according to disease phenotype and lifetime trajectory, with the goal of intervening before advanced remodeling reduces the likelihood of durable rhythm control.

recs.title: Impact of CKD and Hemodialysis on Treatment of Severely Calcified Lesions: The ECLIPSE Trial.
recs.abstract: Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and coronary calcification increase risk for adverse events following drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation. We evaluated whether outcomes following vessel preparation with orbital atherectomy (OA) versus balloon angioplasty (BA) vary according to CKD. Methods: This pre-specified CKD sub-analysis of the prospective, multicenter ECLIPSE trial evaluated 2,001 patients with severely calcified lesions randomized to OA versus BA prior to DES. Independent predictors of two-year target-vessel failure (TVF)-a composite of cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction (TV-MI), or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization (ID-TVR)-were determined using multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling. Results: CKD (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m² or hemodialysis) was present in 694 (34.7%) patients; 112 required hemodialysis. Two-year TVF was significantly higher with versus without CKD (21.2% vs. 11.6%; p<0.001), driven by increased cardiac death and ID-TVR. Hemodialysis independently predicted TVF (adjusted HR 2.14, 95% CI 1.30-3.53; p=0.003), whereas reduced eGFR alone did not (p=0.070). In patients on hemodialysis, OA versus BA was associated with higher rates of TVF (52.3% vs. 30.7%; adjusted HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.16-5.41; P=0.020), driven by higher rates of TV-MI and ID-TVR, whereas TVF was similar after OA versus BA in patients not on hemodialysis (13.5% vs. 13.1%; adjusted HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.81-1.35; P=0.730); however, the interaction between treatment assignment and hemodialysis status was not significant (Pint=0.244). Conclusions: CKD remains a major predictor of adverse outcomes after DES implantation in severely calcified lesions, with the highest risks in patients on hemodialysis. In the ECLIPSE trial, higher two-year rates of TVF were observed after vessel preparation with OA compared with BA in patients on hemodialysis but not in patients with CKD not on hemodialysis or in those without CKD. Given the modest hemodialysis subgroup size and non-significant interaction testing, confirmation of these findings in additional studies is warranted.

recs.title: Noncontrast PCAT and the Statin Signal in REPRIEVE: A Methodological Caveat.
Urinary Metals, Soluble Urokinase Plasminogen Activator Receptor, and Outcomes in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Environmental metal exposure is associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, potentially through inflammation. Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR), a stable marker of immune activation associated with CVD and death, may capture this pathway. We examined associations of urinary metals with suPAR and whether suPAR-associated components were present in cadmium-outcome associations. METHODS: In the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, we studied 5,148 adults free of clinical CVD (2000-2002). We estimated associations of 11 creatinine-standardized urinary metals with serum suPAR by linear regression (per interquartile-range [IQR] increase), compared associations across suPAR, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and D-dimer, and used VanderWeele 4-way decomposition to estimate suPAR-associated indirect components of cadmium associations with all-cause mortality and four adjudicated cardiovascular outcomes. RESULTS: Of 11 metals, 7 were associated with suPAR; cadmium showed the strongest association (7.99% higher suPAR per IQR; 95% CI, 6.14-9.87) followed by cobalt, copper, molybdenum, tungsten, and zinc, whereas barium was inversely associated. The association was monotonic and persisted among never-smokers (5.54%; 95% CI, 3.03-8.11). Over a median 14.7 years, higher urinary cadmium was associated with all-cause mortality (Q4-vs-Q1 hazard ratio, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.18-1.74); the suPAR-associated proportion was 0.30 (95% CI, 0.13-0.47). CONCLUSIONS: Cadmium showed a larger association with suPAR than with hs-CRP, IL-6, or D-dimer. An exploratory decomposition identified a suPAR-associated component of this association. Findings for cardiovascular outcomes were directionally consistent but not definitive. suPAR-related immune activation is a candidate pathway linking cadmium to mortality, warranting longitudinal and mechanistic confirmation.

Great debate: a dual biomarker strategy improves the triage of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome.
recs.abstract: Suspected myocardial infarction in patients with acute chest pain at rest is one of the most common diagnostic categories leading to emergency hospital admission and emergency department overcrowding worldwide. Efforts are being made to improve the efficiency of currently used triage and diagnostic work-up strategies. Despite major advances in recent years with the use of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin, challenges still exist regarding how to accurately and rapidly rule out or rule in myocardial infarction, as current strategies are relatively slow due to the need for serial troponin measurements. The 2023 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines recommend a 0 h/1 h or a 0 h/2 h high-sensitivity troponin diagnostic algorithm, instead of the previously suggested 0 h/3 h diagnostic protocol, to reduce the time required to discharge patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome/myocardial infarction. The ESC endorsed algorithms are not without difficulty, and alternative ways of improving triaging have been proposed, particularly a dual biomarker rule-out strategy involving the combined measurement of copeptin and troponin. Supporters of the dual biomarker strategy argue that a timely optimized algorithm can potentially allow the safe rule-out of myocardial infarction earlier than currently used strategies. In the present Great Debate article, two expert teams discuss the 'pros' and 'cons' of implementing single vs dual biomarker strategies for the rule-in and rule-out of myocardial infarction, under the moot topic 'A dual biomarker strategy improves the triage of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome'. They address in detail many of the controversial issues currently affecting everyday clinical practice and provide insightful comments on how to best triage patients presenting with suspected acute myocardial infarction.

recs.title: Targeting ALDOA Lactylation Reverses Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension by Disrupting Actin Polymerization and YAP Activation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Maladaptive vascular remodeling is a hallmark of pulmonary hypertension (PH), and therapeutic strategies directly targeting the pathological activity of smooth muscle cells remain limited. Metabolic and epigenetic dysregulation are established drivers of PH, and lysine lactylation has emerged as a novel posttranslational modification implicated in diverse diseases; however, its direct contribution to PH progression remains undefined. METHODS: Integrated lactylomic and proteomic profiling was performed in hypoxic human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells. The functional role of ALDOA (aldolase A) lactylation at lysine 42 (K42) was assessed using site-specific mutant virus and smooth muscle cell-specific inducible ALDOA knockout mice in 2 established PH models: SU5416+hypoxia in mice and monocrotaline in rats. RESULTS: We identified ALDOA as a prominent lactylation target in hypoxic pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells, with K42 lactylation consistently elevated in primary pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells derived from PH rodent models and human PH tissues. Mechanistically, AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1)-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation enhanced its binding to γ-actin, independent of glycolytic activity. This lactylation-enhanced interaction promoted F-actin polymerization and activated YAP (Yes-associated protein) signaling via LATS1 (large tumor suppressor kinase 1) inhibition, thereby driving pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell proliferation and phenotypic switching. Moreover, YAP/TEAD4 (TEA domain transcription factor 4)-mediated transcriptional upregulation of AARS1 established a positive feedback loop reinforcing ALDOA K42 lactylation under hypoxia. In vivo, ALDOA inducible knockout or reconstitution with the lactylation-deficient K42R (lysine 42 mutant to arginine) mutant attenuated experimental PH progression, with suppressed F-actin/YAP activation and reduced vascular remodeling. Furthermore, competitive inhibition of lactylation through β‑alanine reduced ALDOA K42 lactylation and ameliorated vascular remodeling in ALDOA-overexpressing rodent PH models. Translationally, pharmacological disruption of the ALDOA/γ-actin interaction by raltegravir suppressed cytoskeletal reorganization and YAP signaling, mitigating PH progression in both mouse and rat models. CONCLUSIONS: AARS1-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation drives pulmonary vascular remodeling through a mechanism independent of ALDOA's catalytic activity, promoting F-actin polymerization and YAP activation. Precision targeting of this modification selectively inhibits pathological signaling while preserving metabolic homeostasis, highlighting a translational potential for precision intervention in PH.

3-Year Comparison of Sirolimus- Versus Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Artery Disease: The SIRONA Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) have emerged as alternatives to paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs), but randomized comparative data beyond 2 years are lacking. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes, effectiveness, and safety through 3 years in symptomatic femoropopliteal artery disease. METHODS: SIRONA was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing SCB angioplasty with a PCB strategy. Patients were randomized 1:1 after successful predilation. Prespecified 3-year outcomes included walking capacity, health-related quality of life, clinically driven target lesion/vessel revascularization (cdTLR/cdTVR), mortality, major amputation, and amputation-free survival. RESULTS: Among 482 randomized patients (SCB, n = 238; PCB, n = 244), 96.3% had intermittent claudication; 3-year follow-up was completed by 76.5% and 79.6%, respectively. Changes in patient-reported walking distances did not differ between-groups. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was 88.2% (95% CI: 83.1%-91.9%) versus 80.2% (95% CI: 74.1%-85.0%; HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.36-0.97; nominal log-rank P = 0.03). Post-hoc analysis suggested time-varying treatment effects (treatment-by-period interaction P = 0.006), with separation after the first year. Freedom from cdTVR (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.50-1.21; nominal P = 0.27) and amputation-free survival (HR: 1.09, 95% CI 0.57-2.09; nominal P = 0.79) did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: Through 3 years, no between-group differences were observed in walking capacity and health-related quality of life or clinical safety outcomes between SCB angioplasty and the PCB strategy. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was higher with SCB angioplasty, with treatment effect that varied over time. Given the exploratory, nonmultiplicity-adjusted 3-year analysis, the cdTLR difference requires confirmation.

recs.title: Extended Outcomes of the ADAPT AF-DES Trial.

Correction to: Pathophysiology, prevention, and management of coronary microvascular obstruction: A clinical consensus statement of the ESC Working Group on Coronary Pathophysiology & Microcirculation, the ESC Working Group on Thrombosis, and the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) of the ESC.
Androgen Imbalance, Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages, and Mortality in Men.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Androgen measures reflect adiposity, metabolic health, and systemic illness, but their associations with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome and mortality may differ across measures and combined profiles. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to examine associations of total testosterone (TT), sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), calculated free testosterone (cFT), and joint TT-SHBG phenotypes with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome and mortality. METHODS: We analyzed men aged ≥20 years in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2013 to 2016 using survey-weighted logistic (odds ratio [OR]) and Cox (hazard ratio [HR]) regression models. Advanced CKM syndrome comprised determinate National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey-adapted stages 3 to 4; cFT was calculated using the Vermeulen equation. Analyses assessed adiposity adjustment and mortality robustness. RESULTS: Among 5,505 men, 4,005 had determinate CKM status. Low measured TT was associated with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome (OR: 1.78; 95% CI: 1.31-2.42), but the association was attenuated after adjustment for body mass index (OR: 1.27; 95% CI: 0.90-1.79) or waist circumference (OR: 1.22; 95% CI: 0.85-1.75), suggesting that adiposity may partly account for this association. Low TT and cFT measures showed no consistent association with all-cause mortality. In exploratory analyses, the low-TT/high-SHBG phenotype was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR: 2.06; 95% CI: 1.18-3.58). CONCLUSIONS: Low measured TT was associated with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome, but this association was strongly adiposity-dependent. The low-TT/high-SHBG profile showed an exploratory mortality association not observed for TT or cFT alone and may represent a distinct systemic-vulnerability phenotype. These findings underscore the noninterchangeability of androgen measures and support prospective evaluation of combined TT-SHBG profiles.

Antecedent Kidney Function and Cardiovascular Mortality in Over 300 000 Patients With Incident Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease is a frequent comorbidity in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and has been proposed as a contributor to its development. However, the spectrum of antecedent kidney function before incident HFpEF and its association with subsequent cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter cohort study across 170 US Veterans Affairs hospitals, including patients with incident HFpEF diagnosed between January 1, 2000, and June 30, 2025. HFpEF was ascertained using natural language processing-derived left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% closest to the incident HF date and a validated HFpEF algorithm incorporating loop diuretic use, elevated natriuretic peptide levels, and an HFpEF-age, body mass index, and atrial fibrillation score >0.5. Antecedent kidney function was classified using 2 estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) measurements obtained ≥90 days apart before incident HFpEF and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. We characterized antecedent kidney function, including albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g), and examined its associations with 5-year cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Competing-risk analysis was performed accounting for noncardiovascular death as a competing event for cardiovascular death. RESULTS: Of 304 712 patients meeting HFpEF ascertainment criteria, 236 910 comprised the final cohort; 51% had antecedent eGFR ≥60 mL/min per 1.73m2. Overall, 15% had an eGFR ≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 were older and had more diabetes and hypertension. 51% of the patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 had body mass index <30 kg/m2, including 20% with body mass index <25 kg/m2. Progressively lower antecedent kidney function was associated with graded increases in cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Among decedents, the proportion of deaths attributed to cardiovascular causes increased from 25% in the preserved eGFR (≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2) without documented albuminuria to 32% with albuminuria and 38% with advanced kidney dysfunction (P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide study of patients with incident HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction was common but not uniformly present before HFpEF onset. Furthermore, among patients who developed HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction identified a higher-risk phenotype, with progressively greater cardiovascular mortality and heart failure hospitalization with declining kidney function.

recs.title: Normative Values for QRS Duration in Athletes aged 12-35 years undergoing Pre-participation Exams.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Due to limited data on athletic QRS duration, this cross-sectional study aims to establish normative digital reference values in asymptomatic, apparently healthy athletes ages 12 to 35 undergoing pre-participation examinations. OBJECTIVES: We hypothesized that QRS duration of athletes would be longer in males, increase with age, and rarely exceed 120 ms in the absence of a bundle branch block. METHODS: We analyzed QRS duration from standardized digital ECG recordings in 9,084 athletes (58% male, age 12-35 years, mean age 18) obtained during pre-participation examinations. Sex-stratified 99th-percentile quantile-regression equations were developed and applied in an APP to demonstrate that QRS duration outliers could be easily identified. RESULTS: Females had shorter QRS durations than males (88.5 +/- 8.3 ms vs. 97.3 +/- 9.1 ms; mean difference 8.9 ms, 95% CI: 8.5-9.2 ms). QRS duration demonstrated a positive cross-sectional association with age and was greater in men than women. Female 97.5th and 99th percentile QRS duration were 106.0 ms and 108.0 ms, respectively, with range 62-130 ms. Male 97.5th and 99th percentile QRS duration were 116.0 ms and 118.3 ms, respectively, with range 70-132 ms. 7(0.2%) females and 55 (1.0%) males had QRS duration >120 ms. 99th percentile quantile regression equations were derived (Female: QRS=99.6 + 0.56 x age; Male: QRS = 104.7 + 0.74 x age). CONCLUSIONS: Our results indicate that defining prolonged QRS criteria necessitates adjustments according to age and sex. To facilitate future prospective research, we offer specific regression models to detect outliers.

recs.title: Clinical Impact of Multiple-Clip Implantation for Residual Mitral Regurgitation After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Residual moderate or greater mitral regurgitation (MR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is strongly associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, the prognostic impact of implanting additional clips in patients with significant residual MR after the first clip remains uncertain. We evaluated the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of multiple-clip implantation for significant residual MR following placement of the initial clip. METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 826 patients with moderate or greater residual MR on intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiography after placement of the first clip during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center from 2014 to 2023. Patients were categorized into single-clip (n=113) and multiple-clip (n=713) groups. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization at 1 year. RESULTS: Procedural technical success and complication rates were comparable between groups. The multiple-clip group demonstrated greater MR reduction and higher transmitral pressure gradients at discharge, 30 days, and 1 year. At 1 year, the composite end point occurred less frequently in the multiple-clip group than in the single-clip group (16.8% versus 29.2%; P=0.002), along with greater and more sustained improvement in New York Heart Association functional class. In subgroup analyses, multiple-clip implantation consistently reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with moderate as well as moderate-severe/severe residual MR. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with significant residual MR after implanting the first clip, multiple-clip implantation improved MR reduction and 1-year outcomes without increasing complications. Even in moderate residual MR, additional clips were associated with more favorable clinical outcomes.

Digital Health Intervention to Optimize Heart Failure Management After Hospital Discharge in Brazil (OPT-HF): A Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Barriers to optimizing guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure include infrequent clinical visits, clinician inertia, and poor patient knowledge. Digital health interventions (DHIs) may mitigate these barriers, but evidence from low- and middle-income countries is limited. We evaluated whether a DHI would improve GDMT use and other outcomes in Brazil. METHODS: We enrolled adults admitted for heart failure with ejection fraction <50% and GDMT gaps (≥1 GDMT class not started or ≥2 classes ≤50% target dose) across 5 Brazilian public hospitals from November 2023 to August 2025. Participants were randomized to usual care or the DHI comprising a patient-facing app linked to a provider dashboard, supporting nurse-led remote monitoring, cardiologist teleconsultations, and self-care education. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in mean heart failure GDMT score (0-12) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included differences in health status, self-care, hospitalization rates, and all-cause mortality. Intention-to-treat analyses used baseline-adjusted linear regression and estimated risk ratios. RESULTS: Among 154 randomized patients (DHI: 87; usual care: 67), mean age was 65±14 years; 62% were male, 66% were Black, 44% had ≤4 years of education, and 68% were New York Heart Association class III/IV. Primary outcome data were available for 141 participants (91.6%; DHI: 81; usual care: 60). Mean GDMT scores increased from 7.2 in both groups to 10.5 with DHI versus 7.5 with usual care at 90 days (changes: +3.3 versus +0.3 points; adjusted difference, 3.01 [95% CI, 2.30-3.73]; P<0.001). A borderline difference was observed in health status (7.89; P=0.052). Improvements were observed in self-care (β=14.79 [95% CI, 9.78-19.81]; P<0.001). Fewer participants were hospitalized with DHI than usual care (9/87 [10.3%] versus 15/67 [22.4%]; risk ratio, 0.46 [95% CI, 0.21-0.99]; P=0.048), with no statistically significant difference for deaths. CONCLUSIONS: In patients hospitalized for heart failure in Brazil, a context-adapted DHI improved GDMT use, self-care, and reduced hospitalizations. These findings provide early randomized evidence supporting DHI for GDMT optimization in low-resource settings. REGISTRATION: URL: https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-10vpf9bm; Unique identifier: U1111-1295-1864.

Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient). AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment. METHODS: Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index. RESULTS: Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04794868).

A global men's health epidemiology within an intersectional framework.
recs.abstract: Males have lower life expectancies and greater disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) than females, and particularly poor outcomes are seen among males in marginalised contexts. In this paper, we provide an epidemiological overview and highlight the intersectional nature of men's health. We analyse mortality and DALYs data from the 1990-2023 Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Studies to illustrate our intersectional framework and draw attention to how health varies in men and to show key themes. Conditions that contribute most to the poor health of males include non-communicable diseases (eg, cardiovascular diseases and cancers), substance use, suicide, injuries (eg, road traffic incidents and interpersonal violence), and respiratory infections (eg, tuberculosis and COVID-19). Although cardiovascular disease and cancer make the largest contributions to men's higher mortality rates, determinants of health such as violence and war, migration, economic stagnation, and labour market changes due to automation and new technologies will disproportionally affect their health in the future. Injuries, violence, and other external morbidity causes often occur at a young age and in unequal distributions across the sexes, making a large contribution to DALYs. Although biology plays a role, the pattern of many diseases contributing to health differences reflects the intersection of health behaviours, shaped by patriarchy, ideas of masculinity, and structural drivers (including commercial determinants of health); many of these are preventable. Although improvements in some health behaviours are seen, exceptions occur in marginalising social conditions (eg, incarcerated men, men experiencing homelessness, men with mental illnesses, men with substance use disorders, men with low income, men who have sex with men, and those who are gender non-conforming). Multiple data sources detail men's shorter life expectancies and the drivers compared with women, but going beyond sex disaggregation remains challenging and is an urgent priority for research and health monitoring.

recs.title: Exercise Right Atrial Stiffness From Pressure-Volume Loops and Prognosis in Pulmonary Hypertension.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In pulmonary hypertension (PH), risk assessment focuses on right ventricular function and may overlook exercise-related right atrial (RA) functional limitation. We investigated whether RA stiffness during exercise reflects impaired right-heart filling reserve and is associated with prognosis beyond conventional measures. METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 68 participants in this observational study, including 42 with precapillary PH. Participants who had PH ruled out and patients with postcapillary PH formed reference groups. Participants underwent 3-dimensional echocardiography, right heart catheterization, and invasive RA pressure-volume loop analysis at rest and during standardized semisupine exercise. RA filling stiffness was derived from the reservoir phase. Patients with precapillary PH were stratified by median exercise RA filling stiffness. RESULTS: At rest, high- and low-stiffness groups had comparable right ventricular function, afterload, and cardiac index, but the high-stiffness group exhibited impaired phasic RA strain and venous congestion (median [interquartile range] liver stiffness, 7.1 [6.0-8.8] versus 5.2 [4.8-5.8] kPa; P=0.021). During exercise, mean RA pressure increased similarly, but the high-stiffness group had impaired peak cardiac index (3.3±1.0 versus 4.1±0.9 L/min per m2; P=0.015) and RA strain. Unlike resting RA stiffness, high exercise RA stiffness was independently associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 4.37 [95% CI, 1.20-15.96]). A model including RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve discriminated high RA stiffness (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.90). CONCLUSIONS: RA stiffness during exercise integrates resting congestion with limited cardiac reserve and unmasks mortality risk missed by resting metrics. RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve noninvasively identify the high-stiffness subgroup.

recs.title: Faster troponin, same time in the emergency department: what is next for acute coronary syndrome assessment?
Long-Term Impact of Vutrisiran in Patients With TTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: 1-Year Efficacy and Safety Outcomes From the HELIOS-B Open-Label Extension.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In HELIOS-B (A Study to Evaluate Vutrisiran in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy), vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) and recurrent cardiovascular events and slowed disease progression measures versus placebo in patients with TTR (transthyretin) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy after 33 to 36 months. We report the long-term efficacy and safety of vutrisiran from an ongoing open-label extension of HELIOS-B. METHODS: Patients who completed HELIOS-B could enroll in the open-label extension, continuing with vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (continuous vutrisiran) or, if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (placebo/vutrisiran). Prespecified end points assessed in the open-label extension are the composite of ACM and cardiovascular events, ACM, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score, New York Heart Association class, and NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide) and troponin I levels. Outcomes were assessed through month 48 in this analysis. RESULTS: Of 654 participants in HELIOS-B (vutrisiran, n=326; placebo, n=328), 478 completed double-blind treatment and 466 (vutrisiran, n=243; placebo, n=223) entered the open-label extension. In the continuous vutrisiran group, the risk of first cardiovascular event or ACM was reduced by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.51, 0.79]; P=0.0001) and ACM by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.46, 0.84]; P=0.0023) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Through month 48, patients in the continuous vutrisiran group had preserved health status and quality of life per Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score (least squares mean difference, 9.0 [95% CI, 5.3, 12.6]; P<0.0001) and more patients had improved or stable New York Heart Association class (odds ratio, 1.6 [95% CI, 1.1, 2.2]; P=0.0084) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Benefits in the continuous vutrisiran group were maintained for NT-proBNP and troponin I levels (adjusted geometric mean fold change ratios, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.58, 0.74]; P<0.0001; and 0.71 [95% CI, 0.64, 0.79]; P<0.0001, respectively) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Similar benefits were observed in the vutrisiran monotherapy population. No new safety signals were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Long-term vutrisiran resulted in clinically meaningful benefits across mortality, cardiovascular events, cardiac biomarkers, functional status, and quality of life in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy through month 48. Patients initially treated with vutrisiran had better outcomes than those first receiving placebo, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04153149.

recs.title: Coronary angiography in heart transplants from donors older than 40: a Eurotransplant study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The increasing age of heart donors in Europe raises concerns about undetected coronary artery disease (CAD), a contributor to early graft dysfunction and long-term complications. This study examined the association between donor coronary angiography (CA) and heart transplant utilization, particularly in donors aged >40 years. METHODS: A total of 20 681 donor heart offers reported to Eurotransplant between 2004 and 2020 were analysed. The use of CA, donor characteristics, and acceptance rates were assessed. CAD status was imputed for donors without angiography using logistic regression based on clinical risk factors. Transplantation probabilities were modelled using observed and imputed CAD severity to explore potential differences under a scenario of broader CA availability. RESULTS: CA was performed in 23.5% of cases, predominantly in older donors and those with cardiovascular risk factors. Among donors with CA, 37.5% had CAD, which was significantly associated with age, male sex, hypertension, and smoking. Donors with normal CA findings had lower odds of rejection compared with those without CA (odds ratio 0.36, P < .0001). In a counterfactual model, broader CA availability in donors aged >40 years was associated with a higher estimated transplant utilization (56.4%-67.1%), corresponding to a model-based increase of ∼535 transplants. CONCLUSIONS: In this observational cohort, CA availability was associated with differences in donor heart utilization, particularly when findings were normal or showed non-significant CAD. These findings suggest that angiographic information may reduce diagnostic uncertainty and support clinical decision-making in older donors. A risk-adapted, resource-sensitive approach to CA use is warranted.

recs.title: Leadless Cardiac Resynchronization Results in Left Ventricular Reverse Remodeling: A Randomized Substudy of the SOLVE-CRT Study.

Multimodality Cardiac Imaging Substudy of the DAPT-SHOCK-AMI Randomized Trial: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Cangrelor versus Crushed Ticagrelor in Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Acute Myocardial Infarction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), the myocardium sustains a dual injury: ischemia of the culprit territory and global hypoperfusion from low cardiac output. Whether platelet inhibition at reperfusion affects the microcirculation, the infarct, the noninfarcted myocardium, and ventricular function, and over what time course, has not been examined with serial imaging. The prespecified multimodality imaging substudy of the randomized DAPT-SHOCK-AMI trial (intravenous cangrelor versus crushed oral ticagrelor) addressed this question. METHODS: Patients at prespecified imaging sites underwent serial echocardiography (208 enrolled; evaluable examinations in 175, 120, and 99 patients in the acute phase, at 1 month, and at 1 year) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR; 93 enrolled; 73, 68, and 63); 81 patients (40 and 41) underwent both modalities. Blinded core laboratories analyzed all studies. The primary imaging endpoint was microvascular obstruction (MVO) on acute CMR, evaluable in 60 patients; secondary endpoints were infarct size, native T1 of the global, infarcted, and remote myocardium, left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', and left atrial volume, and their changes. Comparisons between the cangrelor and crushed ticagrelor arms used covariate-adjusted logistic or linear regression; the substudy was not separately powered. RESULTS: The odds of acute MVO were lower with cangrelor (adjusted odds ratio 0.27 [95% CI 0.08 to 0.98]; P=0.023). Infarct size did not differ between the arms. At 1 year, native T1 of the remote myocardium was lower with cangrelor (adjusted mean 1114 [95% CI 1057 to 1171] versus 1171 [1115 to 1228] ms; P=0.005). Over 1 year, LVEF increased more with cangrelor on echocardiography (37.9% versus 21.7% of the acute value; adjusted P=0.046) and CMR (15.8% versus 2.1%; P=0.027), with greater improvement in GLS, lower E/e', and less left atrial enlargement; no parameter differed between the arms at 1 month. CONCLUSIONS: In AMI-CS, serial multimodality imaging characterized microvascular, tissue-level, and functional injury over 1 year. Cangrelor was associated with less acute MVO, lower remote native T1, and more complete recovery of LV function than crushed ticagrelor, without a difference in infarct size; these hypothesis-generating findings suggest differences in the microcirculation and non-infarcted myocardial injury but do not establish a treatment mechanism.

recs.title: A Potential New Therapeutic Option for Exercise Intolerance in Patients with Heart Failure and Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Efficacy and Safety of Routine Postdilation in Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Platform: The DUOTAP Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: In patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), asymmetric valve expansion can estimate prosthetic dysfunction and death. Postdilation has shown promising results in optimizing valve geometry in observational studies; however, randomized evidence is currently lacking. OBJECTIVE: To determine the efficacy of routine postdilation on transcatheter heart valve (THV) geometry and hemodynamic performance, and associated safety outcomes. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: DUOTAP was a single-center, single-blinded randomized clinical trial. Recruitment took place from January 2025 to April 2026 and end points were assessed periprocedurally (fluoroscopy) at 30 days (adverse events) and at 3 months (computed tomography [CT]). The trial was conducted at a high-volume tertiary referral center, the Medical University of Vienna, Austria. Included patients had severe AS suitable for transfemoral TAVI with a balloon-expandable THV and without high-risk features on preprocedural CT or coronary angiography and were randomized in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by THV size, to routine postdilation vs no postdilation. These data were analyzed from July 2026 to September 2026. INTERVENTION: Routine postdilation using the original delivery balloon at the identical filling volume. A sham procedure was performed in the control group. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The fluoroscopic THV asymmetry index served as primary end point. Further fluoroscopic and CT-derived measures of valve geometry, hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), paravalvular leak (PVL), and THV hemodynamics on echocardiography, and freedom from major procedural adverse events served as secondary end points. RESULTS: Overall, 148 patients (median [IQR] age, 81 [77-85] years; 69 female [46.6%] and 79 male [53.4%]; median EuroSCORE-II, 2.3%) underwent randomization (n = 74 intervention vs n = 74 control). Intervention yielded a 70% lower THV asymmetry index compared with control (median: 1.2% vs 2.8%; geometric mean ratio: 0.30; 95% CI, 0.18-0.47; P < .001), with consistent effects across prespecified subgroups, induced by frame height reduction across the outer curve. Additionally, intervention yielded numerically larger THV diameters on fluoroscopy and significantly larger THV areas at the inflow, midframe, and outflow level on CT. HALT and mild or worse PVL were significantly less frequent and the Doppler Velocity Index was significantly higher in the intervention group. No differences in procedure-related adverse events between groups were recorded (χ2 test: P = .36). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, postdilation led to reduced THV asymmetry, optimized geometry, and improved hemodynamic performance, without increasing procedure-related adverse events. These results support the use of routine postdilation to optimize THV geometry and hemodynamics in suitable patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07477002.
